author: Chloe Tan
review_text: Carbonara, sushi and fries was really good! Order the matcha cake dessert, its nice but abit too thick if finish the whole slice can share with people. Staffs and Thara was really nice and friendly

author: Happy Mama
review_text: I always come back here for the shoyu spice chicken . I loved the combination flavour of the homemade sambal with the chicken, mashed potato and rice . My son will always order the Odaiba big maxx burger. After main course, we will always have space for the bask cheese cake . You can choose Original and Yuri matcha . Both are delicious . We loved the tiramisu here too.

author: Pushpah Pushpah
review_text:
The moment we enter until we pay the bill we really feel welcomed. The food recommendation were amazing and taste so good. Staff name Thara and Sasha provided an excellent service without a complaint and we are glad to tumble upon them, thank you

The caramel pudding were simply awesome as this is our first time trying and it's simply excellent. Thanks TTR for making my day special.

author: szey t
review_text:
Came here purposely for the cheesecake and honestly I totally get why people rate it 100/100. The texture is super smooth and creamy, and the taste is just amazing. Definitely worth the hype!

We also tried two mains:
1️⃣ Lemon Cream Pasta
The sauce was really refreshing and light which I liked. But the chicken... not so great. It had that weird taste, like it’s been sitting in the fridge for too long — not sure how to describe it, but hope you get what I mean.

2️⃣ Imperial Beef Curry
The curry was rich and creamy, and the beef was super tender. Portion-wise only got 3 cubes of beef so a bit on the pricey side. Can added RM8 for an omelette

Service-wise, no complaints at all. All the staff were super friendly and attentive.

author: DANIEL LOKE
review_text:
I visited this restaurant on 28 November 2025 for lunch with my colleagues (around 1:40pm–2:40pm). The ambience was fine, but the food quality was disappointing. The miso soup and the TTR Napolitian (spaghetti) were extremely salty.

A few hours after the meal, I started feeling unwell. Around 5:30pm I felt dizzy, and by 8pm I vomited and had diarrhoea twice. I went to a clinic, and after a blood test the doctor confirmed that I had a bacterial infection. The doctor also asked what I had eaten earlier.

The only food I had before the symptoms started was the spaghetti and a spoon of salmon from this restaurant, so I am sharing this experience as a caution for others. I hope the management reviews their food handling and quality control.

Unfortunately, I do not feel comfortable returning after this incident.

author: KY
review_text: Tried the original Basque cheesecake which it is really nice and delicious, especially with the side of cream that had a rich milk taste. The bar environment is also great, making it an enjoyable spot to relax with dessert.

author: Aisyah
review_text:
First time tried out this restaurant. The food was scrumptious. The ebi roll was perfect. The burnt cheesecake was the bomb. Tiramisu cake was okay. The rice with omelette was a hit, no wonder it’s the signature of this restaurant. The price for food is reasonable too.

The staffs were very welcoming and accomodating. Definitely love the warm hospitality. Definitely come again to try another menu.

author: Hristo Petkov
review_text: We visited specifically for the cheesecake after it was recommended by a local friend, and what a great recommendation! The cheesecake was absolutely delicious: creamy, soft, and perfectly sweet, all at a very reasonable price. We didn’t have dinner here, so this review is based solely on the dessert. The place itself was lovely, though a bit tricky to find, so you may need to ask for directions.

author: Rian Yamazaki
review_text: Shahmie was great! The raspberry matcha he made was really good. Highly recommend the bask cheese cake yuri matcha as well! 10/10 would come for desserts again 😆💖

author: Ji Yan Ong
review_text: Fantastic cheesecake (as always since we first tasted 10+ years ago) and great food. We were very well served by staff Danish throughout the dinner. He’s been offering high standards of services to us and being attentive to our needs. We enjoyed

author: Whitney Yee
review_text: Go there purposely for bbc. It's smooth creamy and for a reason the original one has a hint of chocolate fragrant. Slightly sweet. The matcha on another hand very rich in matcha taste, bitter and kaw, can be a bit jelak in the end. The lighting very dark in the snack zone, everyone can be seen switching on their camera light to have a look at the menu. The table light proves to be useless😅

author: Gabby H
review_text: Ordered the Miso Salmon and their signature Bask cheesecake. The Cheesecake is a must try for this place! Chill atmosphere and friendly staff. Would eat here again :)

author: Summer Gan
review_text:
I used to love The Tokyo Restaurant's cheesecake — the one I had before covid
was absolutely amazing. It was rich, creamy, and melted in the mouth effortlessly. Sadly, the current version feels quite different. The texture is now more solid and no longer has that signature melt-in-your-mouth consistency that made it so special. Still decent, but definitely not as memorable as before. I really hope they bring back the original recipe!

Also tried the grape juice this time, but unfortunately it tasted quite bitter — not sure why. A bit disappointing overall compared to my past experiences.

author: Hayden Hayden
review_text:
I would say their cheesecakes were awesome. Original cheesecake was so creamy and smooth. Tasted so good.

Matcha cheesecake was a little bit solid but tasted good with a little salty taste.

The only thing was too dark that day we went to, like having event and turned off most of the lights.

author: Sook Yee Chow
review_text: Amazed by their signature burnt cheese cake, silky smooth creamy texture . Love their Shoyu Spiced Chicken. It come with special made sambal , definitely a good combination. Great service and attentive staff.

author: Agus Syafika Raimon
review_text: Nice ambient & great food ! I really love their tiramisu & cheesecake. Love the vibes here, calm & romantic. Really have a great time here ! Will visit again for the cakes hehe ! Thanks Aiman for the great service ! So friendly & attentive 🤍

author: Altalia Sabri
review_text: All the dessert cakes were really good like seriously good! Their tiramisu, cheesecake, pudding, and everything else were just delicious. The rest of the menu was okay. I absolutely loved how the staff treated us. special shoutout to Aiman Danish who served us so nicely and friendly. Big star for him! Keep it up, guys! Will definitely come again. Highly recommended!

author: Samham Tam
review_text:
Came here for the bask cheesecake after reading the reviews. The texture of the cheesecake was creamy smooth and paired well with the light whipped cream that came with it. It was a tad too sweet for my liking though. Ice latte was decent

What impressed me most was the level of service. Serving drinking water and replacing it when the water glass was empty- all without prompting. Something you may not get at a restaurant these days. A big shout out to the service crew for the attentive service!

author: KM SY
review_text:
Came across The Tokyo Restaurant on social media and heard many good things about their cheesecake, so I decided to give it a try by ordering a takeaway. The restaurant is tucked away in a corner on the fourth floor of Lot 10, so it’s not that easy to spot at first.

I bought the Matcha Cheesecake, and it was really good — rich, creamy, and full of cheese flavour. The price is slightly on the steep side, but for the quality, it’s worth a try at least once.

author: Shang Yih Leong
review_text: Located inside the Lot10 Isetan food centre. Amazed by their matcha burnt cheese cake. Overall food taste also good.

author: Michelle Tey
review_text:
I visited Joja Bagel recently and it was such a pleasant experience!
I tried three flavors -Super Mario, The Breakfast Club, and Pistachio.
Among all,The Breakfast Club was definitely my favorite😋

Their coffee was also really good, smooth and aromatic, the perfect match with the bagels.
The staff were very friendly and welcoming, which made the whole visit even more enjoyable.
Overall, a cozy place with great food, great coffee, and even better service.
Highly recommended for all bagel and coffee lovers! 💛

author: Réka Fehér
review_text: Incredibly tasty and super generous serving! I had the breakfast club one (the omelette melted in your mouth) and the super Mario with an amazing mushroom cheese patty! Best to come early in the morning to reduce queuing time. The service is kind & efficient, waiting times were never too long. Thanks, I will be back ❤️

author: Anoulack Chanthakhat
review_text:
I read online that there’s usually a queue, but I didn’t realize how serious it was. The shop opens at 8:30, and when I arrived at 8:31, about ten people were already in line. I tried two bagels, but since I have a sweet tooth, I especially enjoyed the pistachio one. The matcha latte was also high quality.

While I was peeling the sticker off my matcha cup, one of the staff noticed despite how busy they were and kindly offered me new stickers. I was really impressed by that level of service 😊 I’d definitely visit again!

author: Eileen Lock
review_text:
⭐️ 2/5
Queued for more than an hour and honestly… not worth it.

We ordered the Breakfast Club bagel — the texture leans more towards a soft Japanese-style bagel, so if you’re expecting that classic chewy bagel bite, this isn’t it. Felt a bit too soft for my liking.

The matcha latte, though… sorry, this was the biggest letdown. It was super sweet and the matcha powder clearly wasn’t sifted properly — everything settled at the bottom in clumps. Really unpleasant to drink.

Overall, overhyped and disappointing. Definitely not worth the queue.

author: xawrax
review_text: Best bagels in town, hands down! You can taste the quality in every bite. I love that they offer so many options. The store has a cozy vibe and the service is quick even during busy hours. Highly recommend!!! Five stars all the way! <3

author: Cheong YP
review_text:
Loves their bagel. Tried 5 different bagels. My rating from the best: Super Mario > Matcha Yuzu > Pistachio Grandeur > Lox in a bagel > Caramelized onion & cheddar.
Main cons: shop is too small to serve all customer, have to queue & wait about 30 mins no matter take away or dine in. Besides, very limited car park.

author: Yvonne Yee
review_text:
Joja bagel shop really live up to the high ratings ;) as someone who has tried many bagel shops in different countries (London Bagel in Seoul, TwoMenBagelHouse and Keen Bagelry in Singapore + a bunch of bagel shops in KL) JOJA definitely ranks high in my heart now.

We ordered pistachio, portobello cheese, spam & egg and a fish bagel. Sauces on the generous side, should have gone for less dressing (available option when placing order).. really enjoyed the portobello one eventho I usually go with the ones with meat. Pistachio cream cheese was nice but cream cheese was too much for my liking , it's also the most expensive one among the 4 I ordered. Fish one taste like elevated version of filet o fish and spam one is classic and you can't go wrong with this combi.

We reached the shop just around 9am on a rainy Saturday and there was already a queue outside. Waited for 50mins to get in and strangely there's no Q at around 10am... one could easily walk in. Maybe we should have gone abit later. Worth the hype nevertheless I would go back at anytime to try other flavours.

author: Winnie Lee
review_text: Long Q means is good food! Waited less than 20 mins for our turn. We tried ice caramel shaken espresso, pistachio grandeur and smokin beast. Thought will be waiting for quite some time but not. The serving is fast. First visit here and overall the food is good. will come back to try more other flavour.

author: Tâm Anthony
review_text:
Must-visit bagel store!

The bagels themselves are perfection—crisp on the outside, chewy on the inside, and packed with flavor. I tried Philly Cheesesteak bagel with well-cooked steak, scallion cream cheese, and it was hands down one of the best I’ve ever had.
The staff is friendly, fast, and genuinely seems to care about the quality of everything they serve.

The coffee is solid, the vibe is cozy and welcoming, and the service is quick even they were having a lot of Grab delivery orders!

author: Vickie Lam
review_text:
we went early so there's no wait. but some people dont queue or they asked for a table for 2 and ended up having 6 people, which is very rude. also some people simply walked in and thought they can sit wherever they want, despite having a notice asking customers to wait to be seated. the servers are not handling this kind of issues very well.

the bagels are ok, the fillings are good but the bread is soso. the drinks are good, very refreshing for the hot weather in penang.

toilet is clean. ac available.

author: Megan Rose Jagger
review_text:
Love this spot. The bagels were amazing, our group had the mushroom, pistachio and smoked salmon, everyone enjoyed them! No complaints at all.

The coconut coffee was delicious also!

Nice vibe, peaceful and no one is too loud.

They have oat milk!

author: Benjamin Chen
review_text:
Tastes great — definitely one of the best breakfast bagel options in George Town. I really love their bagels!

The restaurant was quite busy, so we waited a short while for seats, but it wasn’t too long. I did find a hair in one of the bagels, but the staff handled it well and remade it for us. I appreciate their good attitude, so it’s fine for me — I’d still be happy to come back next time I’m in Penang!

author: Zara Zulkipli
review_text: good bagel but pricey. i ordered everything in standard form, but i think the bagel and the drink would have taste better with some customization. the philly cheese would be a bomb with extra cheese and caramelized onion. standard portion of cheese seems small, to me. i went alone so i was lucky to get a table for one. i heard there can be long queue, so if you are in big pax or on their busy days you might experience long wait as the shop size is so cute and tiny 😊 i went there on thursday around 10am so it wasn't that busy. i appreciate the QR ordering and online payment as i am an introvert myself. im not so chatty, but the worker there are chatty and social butterfly. the extroverts would definitely appreciate that.

author: cxcxline
review_text:
No wait on weekday morning but mostly full. Ordered the signature bagel, generous portion size and I was very full, only around 6-8 tables and not suitable for groups bigger than 4.
I got matcha yuzu and pistachios bagels takeaway and both were great as well!

author: Eugene Khoo
review_text:
The bagels are so good, especially super mario. Price on the higher side but match the portion and quality. Highly recommended for white sesame bagel!
Go early as the place has limited seating. The queue move quite fast and the service is good. Definitely will be back again.

author: Tanakorn Lueangkajonvit
review_text: This is an interesting burger because they use bagels instead of regular bread. They offer four different types of bagels, allowing for a variety of flavors. It's crowded, but the wait isn't long. All the staff provide good service.

author: Rui Ern Low
review_text:
We visited on a Sunday morning hence we are required to queue up and wait for approximately 30 minutes. But i really think that it’s surely worth the wait!! I’ve visited the place previously on a weekday afternoon and there is no wait needed, so it would be rather decent and recommended to pay a visit on weekdays.

For the bagels, it’s toasted till perfection, not too crunchy yet remaining the unique chewiness that bagels have.

My favourite would be matcha yuzu where the yuzu cream cheese pairs nicely with the layer of matcha filling. As their matcha are sourced from a local coffee shop— forest cloud, the quality is promised ! A perfect option to opt for if you’re craving for something sweet and flavourful.

The staff are very attentive, overall it was a splendid and fulfilling dining experience.

author: Lee Pui Kuan
review_text:
Very disappointed with the experience. And a very bad way to start a day. This is what happened.
To be fair the food is good. The ground service is also very good and well presented and friendly.
ut, a big But, the kitchen is very inflexible and the staff have a bad attitude and was impatient when reponsding to our request to cut the bagel into 4 (instead of the standard 2 piece that they stated in the menu).
I can totally understand their 1 slice bagel standard and no-cutlery policy, however what annoyed me is the way the kitchen staff responded to our request. To start, he walked to us with a "wanting to argue and fight" expression and body language. Then what shocked me were the words that come out from his mouth. Not only did he not want to listen to our explanation as to why we need the bagel to be sliced into 4 pieces, he impatiently told us indirectly "if you are not happy, you can leave".
SHOCK!!!
I can't accept this type of attitude coming from such a highly graded place.
Although I like the food, I but will not come back if this is the kind of service I am getting. I won't say "customer is god", but at least show us some basic respect.
I can get same food at other places like FOUNDERS, and many more.

author: Thanaschaphan Suphantakit
review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
SMOKIN’ BEAST is our absolute favorite! The sauce blends perfectly with the juicy beef patty — such a great combo of flavor. Definitely recommend giving it a try!

author: Anantaya G
review_text:
Had this for breakfast on my first morning in Penang, totally loved it! A great choice of protein after a morning run. The combo of bagel, beef, and sauce is perfect. I usually have a problem eating burgers/bagels for its size and disproportional slice, but here they made it so easy for someone with a tiny mouth like me haha. And the signature beef bagel goes really well with the lemonade. Will def come back to try other menu! :)))
Just a bit on the bgm, it was a bit loud for the size of the shop. But still a really love place esp for the morning eat :))) <3.

author: Choon Chang Lee
review_text:
Good food, good service,
Nice environment..
1 bad thing is the parking ..
And for wheelchair and elderly, please book earlier for ground floor ..

author: JacobBiscuitsAreBest
review_text:
It was out first time trying out at this place and it apparently had good some good pasta. We were awfully eager to try out their pasta and was greeted by an adorable cat streching outside the dior. The interior design is cosy and rather spacious with air-conditioning, making it a comfortable place for dining.

The food came quite fast and the Crab Meat Aglio Olio. The plate was filled with many little pieces of roe and it was overflowing with crab meat. The flavoring was spot on, not too creamy, just a light and fun flavour. I was a little disappointed at the fact that the crab meat was frozen crab meat, not the fresh one , so it kind of made the whole dish feel cheap.

The truffle mushroom gnocchi however, was a different story. Everybite was glorious, the rich and thick truffle cream coating everybite of the gnocchi, simply perfection. Since parmesan cheese was mixed into the sayce, there was a lot of strechy heavenly chessy goodness. This is highly recommended.

Overall a pretty good experience. Would definitely come back to try the lunch set and the pizzas.

author: max rampage
review_text:
Came here for the RM32 set lunch (main + 2 sides + drink). It's available every day including weekends and public holidays!

We basically ordered everything off the menu and It's so worth it.  The hae bee hiam carbonara is a unique one and we loved it, as well as the cream spinach.

author: Hammerhead
review_text: Hidden in a nice secluded alley. Serving great western food. Top notch in term of food quality. Service is great as well and love the vibe and the environment.

author: Anas Aqilah Abdul Salam
review_text: It’s my second time eating. And I tried different menu today, their set lunch. For the portion and price, it’s very reasonable, taking into account their appetiser + main course + sides/ dessert + drinks for only RM32++. Very reasonable and of course, quality food. It’s pork free, their poultry sources are halal, but the reason they can’t obtain halal is because they sell alcohol beverages. Overall, good food good quality good portioning and reasonable price.

author: Jamie X.M Lee
review_text:
Great atmosphere. Food was good. And they have set lunch with very reasonable price. With RM28 you can get one appetiser,  one main, one sides and a cup of fruit punch which consider quite a great deal. Their pizza taste good too.
The cafe is just along the alley next to Sri Weld Foodcourt which is very easy to find.
Not to forget to mention their mushroom soup taste real good.
Overall great experience.

author: H.T. 6001
review_text:
This was the first time coming to this restaurant and it's kinda hidden inside a small road along Beach Street.

I'm really surprise with how tasteful their foods are! The texture, taste, favour, everything was really nice! They don't really have much choice when comes to main dishes. We ordered a pasta and a plate of western dish. Honestly, it was super delicious! The food portion is big too.

The overall environment is cosy. Quite suitable for gathering with your friends and so on.

Overall, I'm really happy to found this restaurant and experience their delicious food. Highly recommended. Just one thing could be improve was their iced latte which was kinda mild. However still consider acceptable, but thicker coffee taste would be better.

Looking forward to my next visit here.

author: Patricia G.
review_text:
I wasn’t sure about trying this restaurant at first, given its 4.4 rating and my past disappointments with some of the higher-rated (4.7) places in town. But we wanted something different from the usual Chinese or Indian options, so we decided to give it a try.

What a great surprise! Their hamburgers were not only huge and tasty, but the service was also very friendly.

In my opinion, this restaurant deserves a much higher rating than many of the other places I visited.

author: Hyung “Logy” J
review_text:
I regret that I only visit here recently!

It was always in my want to go bucket list and many of my friends recommend to stop by for their food especially pizza !

Margarita pizza was superb with extra cheese on top and the crust is not so thick!

The fish & chip portion is damn big because normally it’s only either one piece or two piece but it’s three piece here !!

The resto is spacious and well maintain.

And !! It is just beside of cdc!

Would revisit in future!

author: Fauzan Nazar
review_text: This is my first time visiting this restaurant during my holiday with my family here in Penang. They served us delicious food for dinner, and we absolutely loved it! It was a wonderful dining experience with my family. I highly recommend this place to everyone. From the bottom of my heart, I wish Wooden Wagon all the best—keep serving great food and excellent service!

author: ChrisTina
review_text:
charming restaurant with rustic retro decor. The indoor ambience was cosy, though seating was limited.

We've tried the crab meat aglio olio and truffle fries, which were decent but didn't stand out. However, the fish and chips and pizza were quite tasty. The real star of the meal was the beef bolognese; it was superbly delicious, bursting with flavour.

Overall, the delightful atmosphere and the standout food makes this restaurant worth another visit for a comforting and flavorful meal.

do take note that the entrance is behind the alley. there are few parking spots in front of the restaurant.

author: Max
review_text:
Food and service is amazing. Especially the old aunty that is serving us.

However, there is a younger barista at the counter is very rude to her colleague and keep shouting them. It kinda ruined the mood for our meal plan.

Hope the staff can handle it more privately.

author: YunYi
review_text:
An unplanned late dinner at this restaurant, and it is absolutely astounding! Thus far, this is the only cafe/restaurant I find serving gnocchi (I probably have not been visiting  Penang cafe/restaurant quite a while).
Ordered mushroom soup, fried mushroom, gnocchi. You know the food is finger licking good when you continuously taking bites after bites.
Definitely worth to revisit for rest of the menu, and of course the wine.

author: Ne Ale
review_text: Very enjoyable dinner, good menu choices, nice food quality and presentation wth good portion sizes. Would certainly go back to try some other dishes. Friendly helpful staff.

author: Jakey Low
review_text:
Nice ambience, cozy and the service was excellent👌 Food and price, okla.

Ordered the following
1. Mushroom fungi pizza, ⭐⭐ ⭐ ⭐
2. Wagon Fried Fish, ⭐⭐⭐⭐
3. Roast chicken leg, ⭐⭐
4. Smoked duck pasta, ⭐⭐⭐⭐
5. Mushroom pasta, ⭐⭐⭐⭐

author: sc Pear
review_text: Definitely will visit again!! Came here quite late and they still willing to take my food order.Tried their crab spagetti and fries. Everything are so delicious. Was joking with the chef that fish roe is my favourite snack, he is so generous and gave me extra fish roe FOC. The two young chefs are friendly,foods are good, reasonable price,atmosphere calm and relaxed. Recommended!!

author: Tay Liang Chou
review_text: Very nice hidden cafe with excellent dining atmosphere. Serving time slightly slow but all the food were great. However, portion might be small for heavy eaters. Recommended for gathering or family dining.

author: Mark Lim
review_text:
Where to start? It's a western cafe for sure. Simple deco and open kitchen. What's worth is the set lunch. A larte price is slight higher probably due to location. Thats my opinion.
There are 3 choices to choose from for set lunch, 2 chicken and 1 fish. Sides selection have multiple. I would prefer an option of coffee or tea aside from only fruit punch. Overall food were nice.

Note: pork free

author: Jo Jan
review_text:
Parking space is quite limited, have to park behind other ppl's cars so may need to shift cars during dining.

Love the atmosphere. Mushroom soup was delicious, mashed potato and spinach was nice too. Ordered soy sauce salmon, the sauce was very nice and salmon wasnt too dry luckily.

author: Lay Ying Yeoh
review_text:
A hidden cafe in an alleyway with good atmosphere. The lunch set is worth, the portion might be small and the taste just average, more delicious is Chicken Alfredo Penne.

The menu slightly change compared to before, now only can choose the main dish from three choice, side dish, appetizers and drinks are fixed. Parking won't be the problem here, can park at the alleyway.

author: Shanas Ishak
review_text:
I recently had the pleasure of dining at Thong Ne Thae, and I must say it was an excellent experience from start to finish. The restaurant offers a warm and welcoming atmosphere, perfect for casual meals with friends or family. From the moment we walked in, the staff were friendly, attentive, and made us feel right at home.

Now onto the food — every single dish we tried was absolutely delicious! You can really taste the freshness of the ingredients and the love put into the cooking. Whether it was the soups, grilled items, or the side dishes, everything was well-seasoned, balanced, and full of flavor. The portion sizes were generous too, making it worth every cent.

One of the things that stood out was the consistency in quality. Sometimes you get one or two standout dishes at a restaurant — here, every dish we ordered was a hit. It's clear that the team behind Thong Ne Thae takes pride in maintaining high standards.

Overall, I highly recommend Thong Ne Thae to anyone who appreciates authentic, tasty food served in a friendly setting. Definitely a place I’ll be returning to again soon. Five stars from me!

author: Muhammad Aliff Imran
review_text:
Recommended, boleh try once and see if you like it.
1. Vibes/Cleanliness
- The area itself is quite large, lots of tables, and when we visited, it was sort of self service.
- Tables were a bit unkempt, needed to call service staff a few times to clear the tables (they were part-timers).
2. Staff/Service
- was okay from the ordering, pickup station. Need to improve on response time clearing tables.
3. Food/Drinks
- Ordered a few of thier 'must haves'
- overall was OK, a pricey, but overall quite satisfied.
4. Price
- standard fare, dining with a view
- slightly pricey I think
5. Other of note
- there are some snacks/sweets from Thailand that you can buy displayed there.
- they a surau for muslims too

author: akmlftni_
review_text: The siakap “masak dua negeri” was delicious, but too sweet 6/10. I really loved the daging bakar, it was tender with a very tasty sauce 7/10. The beef soup was also flavorful and well-seasoned 7/10. We got to try many dishes and the price was still reasonable for 5 people. The place is spacious, with indoor and outdoor seating near the jetty. Highly recommended!

author: Ninetales
review_text: Overall food is decent except fried shrimp not fresh. We love squid, chicken and bone soup.

author: Apple Jee
review_text:
Need to self service for drinks and food also. Atmosphere ok and nice view. Came at rainy day so won't so hot.
The fish and soup is super nice.

author: Yeoh Poh Choo
review_text: Delicious Thai food. Self service. Food is ready quite fast. Reasonable price. Very nice sea view. Recommended.

author: Sudeepa Herath
review_text:
Very well hyped and rightly so. The place offers a different dining experience. You should go on a busy day just to experience the chaos. Don't expect a peacefully dining experience here. The view during sunset is nice.

Payments are done upfront and you have to take a trolley and collect your own food when your name is announced over the speaker. Even on a busy day, our order was ready in 20min.

Food is reasonably priced and tastes quiet good. Expect to spend around RM 30 - 50 per person. There is a also a stall to buy Thai snacks and drinks.

Large parking area available. You would have to pay RM 5 to enter the jetty area tho.

author: Bamin Razali
review_text:
Food is just fine. Self service system. Food ready was quite fast despite the many patrons. Too noisy and hot and humid.

Choice of food is limited as well. The only food I enjoy here is the Daging Bakar. The rest is okay nothing to shout about.

Also it's a RM5 paid entrance/parking area.

author: sally
review_text:
If you come on weekdays before 7pm, need to pay parking fee rm3.

Order service was good, the menu explained well by the cashier guy.
After order food, you need to wait until your name being called and go collect at the food counter (trolley provided). The seating is convenient and the view is seaview (not too hot and windy eventhough we came around 12pm). Price is quite reasonable.

author: Syazwan Azizi
review_text: Their dish is so tasty. Thai cuisine is on point, and the price is reasonable. The view is the best when you come at sunset. Their service is own served, and orders will be called by your name to get ready for pickup on your own. The place is big enough for group dining and has more tables. There is plenty of parking, you can park near the entrance or behind.

author: Halimi Abdullah
review_text:
Quite a popular restaurant and justifiable since the food is reasonably priced, taste good and prepared fast, even though there were quite a number of customers when we arrived.

The “Dua Negara” siakap (sea bass) fish is recommended, and for RM47 for a good sized fish (can easily feed 2-3 people), quite a good value for our money. We also saw a lot of people ordering the “Daging salai berapi”, well, that’s for our next visit.

author: Tengku Ana
review_text:
Order and collect your own food. Queue is quite slow and long on weekend.

Parking cost RM5, but not many parking spaces available. Parking is available behind the restaurant but u need to hike up to the restaurant and pass by a big garbage bin which is so smelly.

Food price reasonable. Taste is so-so, ikan 2 negara tasted like they cook it with some readymade sauce. Ayam bakar served cold.

I can say it is famous only bcoz of the atmosphere & view.

Will not return.

author: Lini Lynn
review_text: Just come to dine for the view. Best to come during weekdays & earlier to avoid the busy lunch & dinner crowd. Self-service. U need to pay in advance after placing an order & collect your own food & drinks. We ordered Daging Salai, Salted Fish, Seafood Tom Yam & Harimau Menangis. It's tasted ok, but there are too many flies. Can't stand it & can't enjoy our food in peace. The price of Thailand & local snacks are slightly more expensive as they are targeting tourists. Total bill RM 150++

author: Nora
review_text:
A lot of parking space still quite challenging to find an empty parking 😆 punyala ramai haha

You need to order and pay at counter first, and we got our order super duper fast. I honestly think it took about 10 minutes only after ordering mmg gila efficient 👍🏻 However you need to reminded that all orders you need to get yourself from the food/drink pickup point

All foods taste delicious and feel really worth it for the whole experience. But ofcourse lagi berbaloi if you come with large groups since can taste a bit of everything.

If you're a fan of fruit cocktails and durian crepe, please please please don't hesitate to buy from their vendor, sumpah sedapppp😭 Nak crepe dia lagiiii, i bought a few and made my family and friends tasted it, all of them loved the crepes, tak muak langsung

Really recommend the place, worth the hype, keep up the good work 👍🏻👍🏻

author: Hooi Yin Kee
review_text: Good place to hang out with friends. Open environment and fast servings. Enjoy evening sunset view . Foods taste average acceptable at reasonable price. Self servings and the continuous calling loud speaker spoil the nature view. Need to pay MYR 5 parking fees at the entrance.

author: Clarissa Mulan
review_text: Went here for lunch during weekdays. There weren't many people. Parking is rm3. The view is just stunning by the sea. The food we ordered was daging salai, tomyam, kailan and fried egg for about rm110. It was just nice and affordable for 3pax. It is self service hence no service charge haha. They have stalls selling thai snacks and desserts such as cakes. It is a nice place to take photos and across the sea is penang island. Recommended to come for a gathering!

author: Asnida Amri
review_text:
Nice place to dine in with beautiful sunset.
Place is huge and have a lot of table.
Menu is based on Thai cuisine.
So tasty and affordable. Waiting time is just nice. No need to wait that long eventough got many people.
Also got products from Thai available here.
Will repeat again...

author: Yelloboi Jaysen TJ
review_text:
Just drop a while after visiting IKEA and Décathlon since it's quite trending place now. Reached around 8pm++, not a good time to see sunset. it was crowded and self service from ordering to picking up the order. Only tried sate and baked chicken. The chicken was cool🙄 and taste average only.
At the other side, they sell snacks from Thailand too... Not to miss popular dessert brand from Thailand 🇹🇭, Afteryou, 🤔

author: Asyraf Rahim
review_text: Scrumptious!! 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟 for Sup tulang/daging! The meat was so tender and the soup was tasty! But, since I’m not a fan of ayam bakar, i cannot say much, but the chicken was soft and well cooked 👍 Good ambience as well as a lot of parking spots available (RM3 per entry). The workers also were friendly and helpful✌️Overall, good experience with a good food!

author: Raymond Chua
review_text:
Great food. Nice atmosphere. But all self service. And the self-service system is a bit messy. Suitable for patient person.

The food taste sooooo good and the price is reasonable.

restaurant: Ee Ji Ban Chicken Rice Ball
author: Hafizun Mushtafa
review_text: Perhaps one of the best chicken rice I have ever tasted. Ever. Sadly we went here when our tummy is a bit full so we cannot fully feel the taste of this nasi ayam. Even so, the taste when our stomach is full is still damn delicious. The nasi ayam perfect 10 out of 10, got choices between steam and roasted. Both are great. One thing that caught my attention was the rice ball. I thought it was just a plain ball with rice taste but it was good. Feel like a soup in the form of rice. The portion is fair and the price is a bit high lah but deserve with the quality. The service is good, the worker is nice and the waiting time is not that long too. The restaurant is clean and comfortable. We went during weekend afternoon and there are less customers during our visit. Fast forward to 10 minutes, there are already a long queue waiting for turn. limited seating available for sure. I guess we are the lucky customers. We look through the hall and saw a lot of prominent figures and famous artists already went here.

restaurant: Ee Ji Ban Chicken Rice Ball
author: The WAT31
review_text: The food was amazing. The chicken was tender, even the breast was tender surprisingly. Rice balls packs a lot of chicken flavour compared to the plate of rice. Additional star since owner gave us a free bowl of soup with fishball. Would recommend and the taste is on par or slightly lacking compared to Singapore chicken rice.

restaurant: Ee Ji Ban Chicken Rice Ball
author: Ilyah AA
review_text: The chicken rice balls were good and fulfilling. The roasted chicken was tasty, including the steamed fish. An order of the chicken liver was good also. The soup with fishball was ni e and warm. Great chilli sauce and soya sauce to compliment the chicken rice balls.

restaurant: Ee Ji Ban Chicken Rice Ball
author: Wariz Game
review_text:
I finally tried this place today, a spot highly recommended by locals! It wasn't crowded at all, which seems to be the case if you avoid Friday, Saturday, and Sunday.

The food was absolutely delicious – seriously, let the pictures do the talking! Everything I had, from the prawns, fish, and squid to their most popular dishes, was incredibly tasty. Honestly, you've just got to come and try it for yourself!

restaurant: Ee Ji Ban Chicken Rice Ball
author: Patrick Riddle
review_text: Got there around 11 am and it wasn't too busy but that didn't last long. Rice balls were very good and went well with the sambal. Ordered both the steamed and roast chicken and both were equally delicious. Overall would I would recommend stopping in and giving the place a try.

restaurant: Ee Ji Ban Chicken Rice Ball
author: Alan Tang
review_text:
We arrived at the shop lot restaurant at 1:15pm. Restaurant was still full of patrons - both outside restaurant as well as indoor.

Our party of three was lucky to secure a table when the diners ahead of us just completed their meals.

We knew exactly what we wanted as we read their reviews. We had their popular chicken rice balls (charged by the number of rice balls), their white and roasted chickens, oysters omelette and small plates of livers and gizzards. And our orders came with a large bowl of fish ball soup good for 3 pax.

Both the poached and roasted chicken meat were rather ordinary. The much talked about were simply “mashed cooked rice” squeezed into lumps bigger than fish ball size. Interesting but not something I would repeat ordering.

The oysters omelette was delicious; would be better if bigger sized oysters were used.

The complimentary fish ball soup was good. The fish balls were “bouncy”.👍

Overall, we felt that prices were a little on the steep side.

restaurant: Ee Ji Ban Chicken Rice Ball
author: akmal abbas
review_text:
Visited Ee Ji Ban Chicken Rice Ball recently. The staff were friendly and service was quick, which was great. The food was alright—not particularly memorable, but decent.

Just a heads-up: parking can be a challenge, and they accept QR payments (no cards), I'm not sure about cash, so plan ahead. Overall, an okay experience.

restaurant: Ee Ji Ban Chicken Rice Ball
author: Elaine Quek
review_text:
Read good reviews. Decided to give it a try. Rice balls are quite small. One person probably needs 4 to 5. Steamed kampung chicken was disappointing but roast chicken was better. Chinchalok omelet was very salty. Kai Lan was well prepared. Service staff are a bit indifferent. There is chilli sauce but no ginger sauce.

Parking is a hassle. Hard to find lots.

Overall, was okay but nothing to rave about.

restaurant: Ee Ji Ban Chicken Rice Ball
author: Sryo
review_text: Rice ball was very tasty! Chicken a bit bland for me, but the kangkung was really nice. Sotong also good, just portion quite small for the price. Overall okay to visit, worth trying for the experience.

restaurant: Ee Ji Ban Chicken Rice Ball
author: Shahrul IM
review_text: Great food here. I love the taste of Nasi Ayam and Rice Ball. Worth it coming from KL to taste the food. Plus, the owner and staffs are very friendly and serve food very fast. Definitely will come here again anytime visiting Malacca.

restaurant: Ee Ji Ban Chicken Rice Ball
author: Mike Yong
review_text:
Came about 3PM on Sunday. Still pretty crowd; but managed to get a table inside the shop soon enough.
Ordered both steam & roasted chicken and a plate of rice balls.  Both chicken were equally tender enough; and rice balls were dense and flavorful too. The chili was good & spicy too.

restaurant: Ee Ji Ban Chicken Rice Ball
author: Cindy Aurellia
review_text:
i loveeeeee these. look how sexy is this. i mean all of it just taste okay but the chicken taste so damn good. we got fishball soup for free thanks!! i also always like vegetables with these sauces. i juat hope the sambal can be better, its kinda bitter and no flavor.
my mom even came back to take food away to the hotel 😂😂 ate other dishes and it didnt dissapoint me. out of topic but this restaurant has a good music taste 😃 love yall

restaurant: Ee Ji Ban Chicken Rice Ball
author: MML Reviews
review_text:
Disappointed with the food.
The chicken is very soft, I prefer a chicken that has a chewy texture.
Rice was soggy
Sorry not to my taste

3 chicken rice fish veg and 3 drinks 92 rm

restaurant: Ee Ji Ban Chicken Rice Ball
author: Shah G
review_text: Finally had the chance to dine here during the peak hour during the Raya Haji weekend.It was crowded but thankfully we got a seat. Ordered Chicken rice with roasted chicken. The rice is fragrant and flavourful and we ended up ordering second serving of rice..Lol. The chicken is tender and juicy.Service was fast considering it was packed. Overall we enjoyed the meal and thank you for the soup!

restaurant: Ee Ji Ban Chicken Rice Ball
author: Mark D Food
review_text: Delicious food. Chicken is moist and cabbage had wok hey. Rice is fragrant. Could clear the cabbage alone. It is that good.

restaurant: Ee Ji Ban Chicken Rice Ball
author: Norlaila Norddin
review_text:
We eat at around 4.30 pm today. We got a front seat inside area. We order chicken rice ball, roasted chicken, hainan chicken (first time i like to eat hainan chicken, it's very good and i asking my husband to tapaw it makan kat hotel.. hahahaha..)

Service also very good. Boss very friendly. Thank you boss for a free large bowl of fish ball. I give you 5 stars and mini love🫰🏻

restaurant: Ee Ji Ban Chicken Rice Ball
author: Sourav Kalra
review_text:
Ee Ji Ban Chicken Rice Ball Restaurant is a must-visit in Melaka! The chicken is tender and full of flavor, and the rice balls are perfectly soft and fragrant – a unique twist on the traditional Hainanese chicken rice. The sambal and sauces served alongside add the perfect spicy kick!

The restaurant has a clean and comfortable setting with friendly staff who serve food quickly, even during busy hours. I also loved the variety of side dishes, especially the nyonya-style dishes that give a real taste of Melaka culture.

Perfect place for lunch or dinner with family and friends if you’re visiting Jonker Street or exploring the city. Highly recommended for anyone who wants to try the best chicken rice balls in town!

restaurant: Ee Ji Ban Chicken Rice Ball
author: CAROL ANG
review_text: Tried the chicken rice here and it was quite disappointing. The rice balls were very small, and the roasted chicken had no taste at all. The chilli sauce wasn’t nice either. I also ordered the sambal prawns — the portion was small and the prawns were tiny. Overall, not worth it. There are definitely better options elsewhere.

restaurant: Ee Ji Ban Chicken Rice Ball
author: al
review_text: I come here few times whenever I crave for chicken rice ball. The food is okay for me. Even the price may look pricey but the chicken portion quite big for one person. Worth to eat. I prefer chicken rice ball instead normal chicken rice. Service is good and fast. There’s one day, I was lucky bcs the boss gave free fishball soup. I was so happy. Recommended for anyone who wants to try chicken rice ball to come here 😊👌🏻

restaurant: Ee Ji Ban Chicken Rice Ball
author: MightyFoodie
review_text:
Halal-certified, and known for its signature chicken rice balls, Ee Ji Ban in Malacca serves moist, tender steamed chicken paired with fragrant, compact rice balls.

Location: Ee Ji Ban Chicken Rice Ball, 275, Jalan Melaka Raya 3, Taman Melaka Raya, 75000 Melaka, Malaysia

author: Dan Tang
review_text:
Such a lovely foodcourt selling local street food....all the hawker stalls are clean and tidy.
You'll be spoilt for choice!
Recommended.

author: Jenny Choo
review_text:
Came here for an early dinner. Revisiting this place for the Penang authentic popiah or also known as spring roll. Had their fried and dry version. Both are such a delight! And paired my meal with a cold amberella drink during hot day - perfect combo!

P/S: I got to know that the popiah stall starts selling as early as around 3:30pm and until 9pm. Highly recommend their popiah! :)

Also, I had the chance to try the Penang black coffee while i was there too. Such aromatic coffee flavour.

author: chris H
review_text:
Lattern deco.
Variety of food.
White curry not bad.

author: SS Eng
review_text: Windy hawker centre, nice environment. Next to 玄天上帝temple. Variety food choices including pg curry mee, hokkien mee, kuey zap, you tiao etc..like the Curry mee very much. If you come for lunch better come at earlier hour as the food selling quite fast, they started business already since morning.

author: Hin Wai Chang
review_text: This charming food centre is located right beside the splendid Pek Kong temple at the foot of Bukit Mertajam; the locals colloquially named it 大山脚. The gaudy sign board, tawdry childhood toys and the undeniable mouth-watery aroma of street food roiled our emotions with nostalgia.

author: Heng Fey Gan
review_text: One of the best local delights for BM! The environment is much much better after the fire incident. The original white Wantan mee is one of the dishes we should go for breakfast! It is kinda rare for Wantan mee (RM6, mid size is RM7) in the northern region. The taste is unique & good! Another recommendation is the Curry Siew Mai (RM6 for 3 pcs), which tastes very unique!

author: Zhou Hai Chan
review_text: Quite crowded during dinner session. Lot of flies and the food are tasty ! 😍

author: Teh Xin Yu
review_text: Brought my mum to try her childhood favourite food. It was ok although according to my mum it is no longer near to the taste in her memory. There are many other choices of food in the stall along the food street. Most of the stalls have different vendors operating during day and night.

author: Cher Ong
review_text: This place is airy with lots of food varieties. It's much more comfortable now after they refurbish the whole area. The food here is quite good & the price is reasonable.

author: Ted Thor
review_text:
Was here for breakfast. The Penang Curry Mee (RM6) was superb. Flavourful & nice. Now you see it, now you don't. 5/5

Saw many tables order whitish, Hakka mee. But, the locals say it is their Wantan Mee. Couldn't resist trying. Order 1 bowl (RM6). Taste wise, very light. Noodles were geat, nice soft but firm texture. The 2 PCs of wantan are some small, like 5 cents coin size. Definitely prefer Hakka mee elsewhere. So, only 3/5.

The iced coffee (RM3) was superb. 5/5

In the morning, about 10am, despite cooling breeze from the big industrial fan, I still sweat as I eat. Luckily it was the morning.

author: Anique Lim
review_text: Nice coffee and 3 in 1 rice cake. Fried Kuey Kak pre cook. A little bit oily, tasteless and cold. Other food is average.

author: Manyfires
review_text: Recommended - porridge with mixed roast (pork belly, chicken and duck), the mixed vege stew is so yummy we always ordered twice! The noodle soup is plain but it’s got a taste of nostalgia for me that I must have it everytime. It brings back memories of when I was little when these stalls were on the opposite side of the road at the old temple (before it was refurbished) when my dad used to bring us there for supper!

author: Jason Chin
review_text: Food court feel very hot when step into the place. from temple blessings to street food temptations.

author: WSL
review_text: Lots of Penang favourites here. Overall food is average. Koay chap was good. White wantan mee was good. Joo Heang coffee and toast bread (too little Kaya and butter) was so so...

author: sh00tinspitballsrfun
review_text: Came at dinner time during Malaysia Day long weekend. Crowded but managed to get a table. Excellent local food on both sides of the temple. Affordable and delicious food. Would definitely recommend the popiah stall in the middle with the friendly aunty as well as the muah chee stall.

author: Jason L
review_text: Had the tomyum mee here recently, but sadly, the standard seems to have dropped. The ingredients didn't feel as fresh, and the soup had an oddly sweeter taste. Despite that, I appreciated the hearty meal on a cold/rainy day. Hope they can improve the freshness and balance of flavors.

author: Desmond Duece
review_text: Quite ok, not hard to look for seats. Food normal. Some staff don't seem to be sure what languages they are using, there's a lady you can't communicate with, either Chinese, Bahasa Malaysia or even English.

author: Benny Poh
review_text: I ordered the Wan Tan Mee, Mee Tai Soup, and roasted pork during breakfast hours. Personally, I found the taste of the food to be just average. It's challenging to find a table and parking for your car. I wouldn't highly recommend going there due to heavy traffic congestion

author: Carbon Lim
review_text: I had order a Kueh Kak with a different stall not the Ah Beng Char Koay Kak was not open today, of course the taste was not as good as Ah Beng

author: Vincent Chin
review_text:
Right next to the temple, the location is also near the market, lack of parking space, too many people. Serious traffic jam.
But the food inside is delicious. Although there are many people, it is not chaotic.The decoration is very old-fashioned

author: Ong Shu Wen
review_text: Tried the Hokkien Mee (also known as prawn noodles) at this well-known spot in BM. The broth was rich and flavourful — definitely on the heavier side, which suits my taste and feels quite authentic. It’s a popular place for good reason. However, the coffee was a bit of a letdown — lacking in taste and depth. Still, if you're in the area, the noodles are worth trying.

author: Jessen Tan
review_text: Nice old house environment with modern touch. Hokkien mee is ok, a bit of sweetness tho. Reasonable price.

author: Philip
review_text:
Local BM friend recommended this place, since I only left 1 breakfast left, I called the mixed Loh Mee/BeeHun that comes with prawn and chicken claw. I tasted it without the chili paste, the broth is really good, then with the chili broth taste even better.

Coffee looks like Guinness Stout from a far, taste was Excellent or Amazing if your a caffeine addicts.

loh Bak, though taste frozen food, good to enjoy with a large group of friends

Garlic bread with half boil egg and coffee is also a must.

If you are in Mainland, don’t missed this spot…..

author: pei yik
review_text:
Hokkien mee is delicous and price was worth it.👍
Quite hard to find seats.

author: Forest Ang
review_text: This coffee shop has a small shop front but with dining area stretching to the very end of the house. Unique old coffee shop with old rusty cozy-looking atmosphere! For hokkien mee must try menu B with 2 prawns & 2 chicken legs @RM8 only.

author: Jenny Choo
review_text:
The best Penang hokkien mee I have eaten so far (yes, I dare to say this). ;)

On top of that, they serve nice artisanal drinks like cappuccino and matcha latte. Pair it with your flavourful hokkien mee, that’s the best of both (culinary) world!

author: Jessie Cham
review_text: Delicious and authentic Hokkien Mee, served in a long, old-style house by the roadside. Plenty of tables and chairs. Paid parking beside the house.

author: Oon Lan
review_text: Old house convert to Cafe the noodle delicious breakfast and koay teow soup is superb 。

author: Trisha T
review_text:
Really love the prawn soup broth.. makes a good Hokkien Mee / noodles awesome braised phoenix claws too. Chicken feet / chicken metatarsus. Careful if u can't take chilli spice, it's a great kick.
Good till the very last drop.

author: Khoo Jia Ming
review_text:
nice noodle but Bad services
Dear HOKKIEN MEE STALL, bear in mind that Penang not only have you this hokkien mee, mind your attitude

author: Oliver Tey
review_text:
MUST try the famous Hokkien Mee and the brew coffee. KTT with every sinful bits was as tasty with sizable portion served.
Somehow waited very long for the coffee. It seem The barrister had missed out our order.
Saw that apologetic puppy face on our cappuccino when served. Surprised that it's mouth opened when kaya toast was delivered a few minutes later. Seem try to apologize where our order was delayed🤣🤣
A joyful breakfast with yummy food n coffee.
Surprise there are seats in the open air back lane if you want a different ambient.

Recommend to visit when in BM

author: kathy.cheang kathy.cheang
review_text: Must try Hokkien noodle, prawn noodle with many ingredient, RM9 per bowl reasonable price. Good coffee cheap price, 3 mix signature recommeded too, taste like hokasai.

author: Jaynian
review_text: Honest review from a local. Hokkian mee is ok, though hokkian mee in the other corner of the street tastes better. The chu chang fen is good. One thing to note is that if not specifically mentioned, they will serve the big bowl. The young boss is impolite to elderly persons, a common issue for old brand business.

author: Andrew Yeoh
review_text:
There are two main stalls. One sells Hokkien mee while the other one specialises in koay teow thng. The Hokkien mee comes in a full set with a small piece of pork ribs, two medium sized prawns,  egg and two chicken feet. Taste-wise, it is quite good. The broth is thick with nice consistency and not too prawny. The broth is slightly spicy which is much to my liking. The koay teow thng comes with fish balls and minced meat balls. In my opinion, it is not great. The place is very popular. There was quite a long waiting time.
The shop is actually quite non-descript, rather long and narrow. There is a parking lot just at the corner which charges RM2 per entry.

author: 茉莉Jasmine
review_text:
If u r the 1st time having here and just pick the food photo 😂 Hokkien mee is serve with 2pcs of prawns and 3 pcs of chicken feet, RM 8 per bowl and if you want to add on one big fishball will cost RM 9/bowl.

Ordered one cup of cappuccino and they craft a cutie cat there 🐱

Egg on toast is like ipoh egg sandwich 蛋治 and you can add how much the soy sauce & pepper as you like.

author: Ice Ice Kitchen “Ice Ice”
review_text:
Coffee is completely failed!👽
Ordered coffee less sweet but end up received a cup of coffee tastes like sugar water. It has zero coffee taste. Feedback to them and they took back my coffee to modify. But still bad. Worst coffee ever I have had in Bukit Mertajam.

Half boiled eggs maybe ok.
Although the eggs are almost 80% done, still acceptable by me. However, my friend couldn’t accept. So this is really personal preference or I have already lower down my expectations after my bad coffee is served.

Guang Xi Hokkien Mee is alamak.
Was recommended by local friend to give it a try. Took me a while to place my order as there isn’t and proper queue. The stall owner don’t even look at me until I wave my hands and ask her how should I place my order. She ask me to look at the menu. I have actually decided my meals and I told her what I want. She didn’t reply me and I repeat once again. I think she is over confident with her memory. To cut short, I went over 3 times and finally received my noodle. I can easily get something better outside. Hence, no next time.

Environment is wow.
The environment is unique and I’m really impressed when they are serving both eastern and western coffees. Maybe I should have ordered western instead. Less chance to go haywire.

Conclusion ~
Read more reviews before heading down. I’ll not come back for 2nd times for sure.

author: Peter
review_text: Best hokkien mee in bm area. A lot of side dish choices.

author: Joshua Yap
review_text: Good Penang hokkien mee (RM 6) for the basic. Kopi ais was Rm2.40. Much cheaper compared to KL. A good bowl of noodles. Ample of tables and chairs behind

author: Millie Voon
review_text: A quaint breakfast place with choices of basics toast with half boiled eggs/sandwiches with brewed or local coffee, anchored by Koay Teow Thng hawker food.

author: Chong SV
review_text: Excellent food, no complaints there. My only concern is that the toilet hygiene is in desperate need of attention and needs to be addressed by the owner.

author: Kai ce Yap
review_text: This Japanese restaurant is run by a real Japanese uncle, so you can enjoy authentic Japanese food without even going to Japan. The Japanese curry ramen was delicious, with plenty of ingredients and not too spicy. The fried chicken chop with tartar sauce was superb — honestly a 10/10. But do note that this dish is part of their daily menu, so it may not always be available. You can check their Facebook page for updates on the daily menu. The queue was very long, so be prepare about it. Overall, a very satisfying and authentic experience!

author: Kennie Kheng (Kennie)
review_text: Definitely one of the BEST and AUTHENTIC Japanese noodles and rice I've ever tasted, in Penang, Malaysia some more. It's so much better than ALOT of the cafe/restaurants. I really love the authenticity and the atmosphere, feels like I've entered a small diner in Japan rural area. ❤️❤️❤️❤️

author: CS Chai
review_text:
Nice ramen and udon dishes prepared by a Japanese chef. He is the husband of the Malaysian lady boss. Both of them are very friendly.

The noodles dishes are delicious and very fairly priced, only RM10 per bowl. The restaurant is clean. A recommendable place.

author: Terry Ding
review_text:
This is, hands down, the best udon I've had in all of Southeast Asia. It even surpasses those famous udon restaurants in Tokyo, Takamatsu etc! Highly recommend giving this a try.

The secret to this incredible dish lies with the owner, a true Japanese chef who holds his food to the highest standards. According to his junior, he meticulously inspects each egg, ensuring only the finest quality graces his customers' bowls.
For a mere 10MYR, I indulged in a steaming bowl of warm udon. The dashi, a cornerstone of any great udon, was undeniably authentic, simmered to perfection with the finest ingredients. The udon itself? Pure bliss – bouncy, smooth, and truly top-notch.
The daily-changing toppings are a delightful surprise, yet always generous. Imagine a vibrant medley of fresh green vegetables, the smoky kiss of char siew and seaweed, the refreshing crunch of sliced radish, and a golden crown of fried tofu. But the real star of the show? The toasted sesame seeds. Toasted to perfection with a touch of salt, they release an intoxicating aroma that elevates the entire experience.

My takeaway curry udon was carefully packed and held up amazingly well after three hours. It was still so tasty!
在东南亚吃过的最好吃的乌冬面！厨师技艺精湛严格要求，乌冬面筋道爽滑，汤和搭配的食材都很用心，十分美味。咖喱乌冬打包了也很好吃。

author: Forest Winter
review_text: The taste is just like the ones I tasted in Japan. Authentic and very delicious. If you want to have an  idea of what a real noodle soup in Japan taste's like, then this is very close to the real thing. I wish they renovate their restaurant in future to have a similar feel of local Japan. Give it a try, you'll not regret it. Also give them a chance to improve  because while the service is good, the queue is still very long and it's not their fault. Simply the best ramen in BM!

author: MinNee Loh
review_text:
Should be the cheapest ramen in town, which is very reasonable. Ramen was delicious. Definitely will make my next visit!

The lady boss was so politely to greet us and introduce their today's menu, serving food was quite fast as out of expected. But be prepared to wait for your seat when you dine in, easily crowded with ppl.
However they currently did not served green tea yet, only some soft drinks provided.
Rmb to visit their Facebook page before you visit, they have different soup base menu everyday

author: K.T Wei Jze
review_text: This might be the best authentic japan restaurant I ever try , the pork hamburger rice is on point , same as the Miso soups.

author: Esc
review_text: This place is deserving of a five-star rating. Its delicious udon (as shown in the pictures), friendly service, and affordable prices (RM11/bowl) have contributed to its well-earned reputation and popularity.

author: ShenHua Lim
review_text: Most affordable Japanese cuisine you can find, very friendly boss. Go early you wan to taste their ramen, else you have to queue. Very busy during peak hour

author: Benny Tan
review_text: looks like a normal shoplot, a hidden gem in fact, super friendly waitresses, the foods are delicious and portion is big, worth a try...it has special menu from time to time, I'm definitely visiting here more often

author: Jason C
review_text:
Very friendly lady boss (her hubby is the Japanese chef). Order at the counter... Food is very tasty and reasonable price.

Order the M2 and the U1 dishes.

Large crowd especially in the evening. Go early so the dishes you want won't run out.

No free flow water but there's an ice bucket where you help yourself to foc ice cubes.

Table and chairs are kopitiam style. Sit at the roadside on the kerb.

author: Jong Cherng Meei
review_text: Prices reasonable. Big portions. We ordered curry udon, miso ramen, and two other types of noodle dishes.

author: Chew EE
review_text: The lunch udon was chewy with a light and flavorful broth. The evening sesame ramen was very tasty and delicious. It's the best Japanese udon/ramen in BM town.

author: Crystal Pua
review_text: Curry rice come in big portion and really worth it. Taste good. However it was quite crowded and took so long time to serve.

author: Gary Looi CW
review_text: The cheapest Japanese noodle shop in town! It tastes better than some Japanese restaurants. Although there is not much variety of food to choose from, it's still a great place to grab a bite if you want to have noodles. The seating area is a bit cramped and limited.

author: David Chng
review_text:
They serve authentic Japanese food. May even get to try Japanese home cooked food on certain days which we normally won't get anywhere else. The dishes are different daily except their Japanese & clear soup ramen & udon. I highly recommend those who need instant comfort food & quick fixed Japanese food, this is the place to go. Can be really crowded during lunch & dinner hours. I go to this place regularly & so far I have not been disappointed except on days they are not opened 😂.

Its open air sitting outside & inside. No aircon. As mentioned, quick fixed is ok. Recommended to go with friends & family not over 4-6 person. Other wise sitting together will be a challenge

author: Nantha Kumaran
review_text: The food is taste fine. The price fine. But just the serving time is taken a lot. I think the kitchen arrangement need to making improvement whether by using system or order by using system. Otherwise still same condition messy on the arrangement.

author: Claus Yew
review_text:
Cheap, quality and delicious! Finish the soup everytime and later not thirsty at all!
I will eat everydays if open near my house in island.. UmaMon meccha meccha dai suki-!!

author: C J
review_text:
Japanese ramen with only RM10 each. I order Curry Ramen and the taste is good!

Limited seats, with no air conditioning. Would recommend to avoid peak hours for dine in.

Owner is very friendly and cheerful!

author: Benny Koay
review_text: The price is reasonable, but the food is up to any Japanese chain standard. However, price is suitable for the local. *After 30 minutes, I were so thirsty* Their soup and charsiew were so sweet. It is definitely not my Japanese Ramen.

author: Bell Chin
review_text:
RM4 Kaya Butter Toast in a Kopitiam might should expensive, but the generous butter serving makes it worth it and tastes so good.

Always expect the place to be super crowded during lunch hour. Parking is also very difficult.

Not many things are good, but its location made it really convenient. FYI, Lorbak not great.

And of course, the Yam Rice & Pickle Cabbage Pork Soup, one of the best in town.

author: E. Wong
review_text:
Char Koey Teow tasted good,even though I prefer soy sauce CKT style. But this one CKT has Wok Hei.
Jawa Mee also nice.
Only Yum rice not as good as we tried in SP.

It is self-order beverages.The young lady who order beverages wasn’t friendly.

Hard to find parking.

author: WY N
review_text:
Sentosa Corner Coffee Shop – A Bukit Mertajam Food Haven

If you're in Bukit Mertajam and craving authentic local flavours, Sentosa Corner Coffee Shop is a must-visit. Located in Taman Sentosa, this long-standing kopitiam is bustling with locals and food lovers who know where to find good eats.

The highlight here is undoubtedly the yam rice with pork offal soup — a signature dish that's both hearty and comforting, and has become a favourite for generations. The soup is rich and flavourful, with tender ingredients that pair perfectly with fragrant yam-infused rice. It's no surprise that most tables are seen ordering this dish.

Beyond yam rice, the coffee shop houses several other stalls offering a diverse range of Malaysian hawker fare. From mee jawa, pan mee, and pasembur to fresh chicken rice, Portuguese egg tarts, and traditional dim sum, the variety ensures there's something for every palate.

Despite the busy crowd, service is quick and efficient. The kopitiam is clean, airy, and has a nostalgic charm that adds to the experience. Prices are reasonable, portions are generous, and the taste is consistently good.

Sentosa Corner is a local gem where tradition meets flavour — a perfect place to enjoy a true Malaysian food experience.

author: TAI pristine
review_text: This place is crowded with people during weekend and we have to wait for a table. The table is close to each other and we could hardly move around. First time we tried the yam rice which has little yam topping, it is just ordinary.  Jawa Mee and Pasembor taste better.

author: GWZ85
review_text: This place has amazing yam rice and the pork soup is so flavorful.  It's a really great little spot for a casual meal. The neighborhood is lucky to have such a gem of a kopitiam. I highly recommend checking it out if you're in the area.  You won't be disappointed.

author: Danielnhebe
review_text: I sit for very long and wanna order a drink with the waiter bringing water then she said you need go counter order. I wonder they hired only to take water. Service bad so decide don't wanna order a drinks then lucky chicken rice got soup to drink. Don't come here to here. Not encouraging

author: Pet N
review_text: What a great place! There’s lots to eat here and it’s clear it’s a local favourite. We had the yam rice with pork soup which required a bit of a wait but it was worth it! We loved it a lot! You can select the parts you want in your soup and the soup was just the right amount of sourness. The yam rice was really soft and yummy. Our other favourite will have to be the Pasembur. It was really delicious and when served, the items were still nicely crisp.

author: Mingsheng Lum
review_text:
Local neighbourhood coffee shop

Why you should come here ?
回答我! Why? tell me why?!

Because of the anchor tenant ⬇️
Yam rice with pork soup 🍠🍲
The other foods are also nice as well

Usually packed during lunch hours
Those are the photos over period of time!

author: Emily Chng
review_text: We visited on a Sunday, about 11. 20am. Was lucky cos we got a table without waiting. Everything we ordered came promptly, the operations of this coffee shop is efficient. BM Yam Rice (RM 10) is good. There are 2 lanes, one for take away, one for dine in. Generous amount of pork. They even top up the soup without me asking. Good job! Passembur is okay, better if the gravy is sweeter. Chee Cheong Fun is a winner. Must order. Lobak is alright, the dipping sauce can be improved. Ask for more chili as the lor gravy is quite bland. Char Mee is so so, nothing extraordinary. Drinks can be ordered from the counter. Next time I will try something else.

author: jeremy cho
review_text: Pig intestine soup very well done. Comes with pork slices, pork belly, pork blood, stomach etc. The pig trotter and the braised soya intestines also very good.

author: Evonne Ching
review_text: Good place to find Chinese style pasembur with crispy fried bits, chee cheong fun, char kuey teow, and fragrant egg & coconut tarts! Hidden gem in bukit mertajam area if you’re looking for a good coffee shop with everything local.

author: Yong Hao
review_text:
Heard abt this Famous Yam Rice from my Penang friend. Went on a Sunday morning and as expected, it was super crowded—seems like this spot is really popular with locals and tourists alike.

Of course we tried the yam rice.The yam rice was flavorful but did noticed the amount of yam in the rice was quite little, which was disappointing. Soup that came with it was really good and comforting. The 猪血 in the soup was especially nice, super smooth.

We also tried  chee cheong fan and yam cake here and both were pretty good as well. Drinks here were reasonably priced👍🏻

author: Johnny Ch'ng Wei Loon
review_text: The Yam Rice was great... The Yam Cake and Otak-otak from the Chee Cheong Fun stall is nice too... Jawa Mee was nice...

author: Hammerhead
review_text: One of the best hawker food in Penang serving authentic delicacy by local people unlike many hawker where foreigner start to over. Highly recommend their yam rice pairing with soy source pork leg/intestine. Plz do come early to avoid over crowded peak hours.

author: BIlly Lim
review_text: The yam rice here is definitely good. A very busy/hectic place. Of noteworthy is the pasembur@jawa mee.

author: Zilver Yys
review_text: Highly recommend their mango smoothie RM 6 👍, very creamy😋 Kopi O panas RM 2.20. Every foods are delicious here! Like pasembur, jawa mee, pan mee 😊

author: Lay Ying Yeoh
review_text:
Come here to try their famous Yam Rice very delicious, I like the yam rice because got yam. Portuguese Tart also taste good, very crispy.
Price is reasonable. Hard to find seat and parking here because have many people, very crowded especially peak hours. If really want to come better choose weekday.

author: Ianhung Lee
review_text:
Among those yam rice in Bukit Mertajam, i find this is one of the best. Though the yam in the rice seems lacking lately. The soup can be customised if you do not take offals and blood jelly. The price is okay for a portion.
Other than that, the jawa mee and pasembur are nice too
Parking here is somewhat difficult and depends on luck.

author: Peter Tam
review_text:
Good place to come to try multiple options. Yam rice is the most popular here but the rice had sold out by the time we came so had to settle for white rice with their soup.

Char Koay Teow was a hit too. As was the curry mee.

There’s also a Winner’s Fried Chicken that was just setting up around 2pm. We were too full to try but there was a steady stream of customers the moment the chicken was ready.

Drinks are self service at the counter to order.

Parking is a bit challenging with limited parking nearby. Be prepared to walk a bit.

author: Kee Kelven
review_text:
This was one of the most popular food court in Bukit Mertajam as they had one of the best Yam Rice and Jawa Mee in the town.
The yam rice was yummy as it had a big chunk of yam and dried shrimp in it. And the pork intestines soup was really as the meat and intestines were clean and fresh.
The sticky soup of Jawa Mee was really good and tasty.
But the foods were mostly higher in price in general compared to other food court in the town. Especially the cheapest beverage is RM2 and required us to order and pick up ourselves.
I guess it was why the food court was not as crowded as it was back in a few years ago. The food was still good but the place was packed with too many tables and food was higher in price.

author: Gan SB
review_text: “So far, this dim sum is among the best I’ve had. The dishes are fresh, flavorful, and well-prepared, with a good balance of traditional favorites and unique specialties. The portion sizes are big, and everything comes out hot and tasty. Service is efficient and friendly, making the whole dining experience enjoyable. Definitely a place I would recommend to anyone craving quality dim sum.”

author: Super 8 Rescue
review_text: Very nice choice of food. It's clean and bright. The staff are nice. You can see food being prepared behind glass. The kitchen looks clean and the chefs wear a hat. It's price is good. I really enjoyed my food here. Highly recommended

author: Eric Tee
review_text:
I've tried the main shop on the island before, but this was my first time visiting their branch on the mainland. The environment here is a significant improvement - it's much cleaner, air-conditioned, and the ordering system is more efficient. You simply tick your orders on a form and pass it to the staff, unlike the island branch where you have to self-service at the dim sum station.

Food-wise, both branches offer above-average dishes, but the prices are on the higher side. Some standout items include the char siew bao, signature siu mai with king prawn, siu mai with fish roe, and salted egg yolk custard bun. The Hong Kong-style cheng fun with two big prawns was average. Overall, a pleasant dining experience with room for price adjustment."

author: Linda Anwar
review_text:
This is my first visit. My first impression when I walked to the seat was not good. The seat was worn out, it kinda ruin the image of the restaurant. Time for a repair.

Then came the porridge. It was mildly warm, at most 45 degree only with lots of fried stuff. At least put some effort and heat up the porridge to 80 degree. But I will not order again because I prefer my porridge without the fried stuff.

I will visit again to try different items.

I like the system where the order was served to our table. Maybe a qr code would be better. I don't need to wave and wait for eye contact when I need to add order. Dim sum is something that can't be order all at once as I don't like to eat cold food.

The price is reasonable.

author: Lena
review_text: The food is not bad, the service is very good, the air conditioning is sufficient, it is clean , and it is easy to find a parking space.

author: Thomas Tam
review_text: Food was okay. Service started quite fast but got very slow when the restaurant got busier.

author: Dx 7
review_text:
A long que in the morning. Come after 10am, less crowd. The food is good, mostly are just average, while a few dishes is above average. The prawns here are large and juicy and fresh.

The pricing here is expensive. Price like high end restaurant, but unfortunately the food does not meet the high price tag. The service and atmosphere here is very good.

author: ahwei
review_text:
overall quite good experience having dim sum here. visit on sat morning, waiting time around 10mins. spacious seating place inside which occupied 2 shop lots. air-conditioning restaurant.

staffs are friendly and service is good.

steamed dim sum taste good, and served hot. 流沙包 is fried type, slightly crunchy skin which is unique, but at the same time it is slightly oily. others that we ordered are ok.

parking available, remember to pay on mbsp parking app.

author: Layar Jaring
review_text:
Was around here at lunch time and dropped in to try. Naturally being alone limited my choices. But kudos to the comfortable seating. Well spaced tables with attentive waiters made a comfortable lunch. The place had a good air con going so the temp was nice for a relaxing eat.

Both the dish I ordered was superb. The crispy prawn rice flour roll was a surprising dish. The filling had a crispy prawn centre covered by rice flour and steamed. Looking at it you would've thought it was a simple chee cheong fun but the textural contrast that the crispy interior filling gives to the soft steamed rice flour roll is incredible. The gravy is also superbly flavoured giving the whole dish a thumbs up from me. It's a dish worth coming for.

The siew mai is huge. Unlike the some joints which serves small anaemic portion. This one is generous is size and flavour. The best it it comes freshly steamed and hot. So be patient and expect a 5-10min wait.

I had a great meal and look forward to coming in a group to enjoy their full gamut of choices.

author: Kean Chin
review_text: One of the best Dim Sum restaurant in town. Food is very good, just a bit pricy.

author: Yen Wei Chan
review_text: good service and atmosphere, the waiter even free us this tasty jelly! Highly recommend!

author: Kee Kelven
review_text:
A nice place to have dimsum here. The environment was clean and bright with air conditioning, the service was good and friendly. The price of dimsum was slightly higher but at least it served in big portions.
Some of the food were freshly made upon order, so required some waiting time.

author: Jacob TAN
review_text: One of the very popular dim sum place in Bukit Mertajam. There is usually a line of customers waiting to go in. The dim sum is very average in taste. None of the dishes which we ordered are exceptional. Service is quite slow and service are quite confused with the drinks which we ordered but service staff were polite.

author: Jolyn Chong
review_text: A very chill place for good dimsum. The ambiance and staffs were attentive. The presentation of the dimsum does bring out the flavours and nice textures. Most importantly, the dimsum was still hot upon served on the table. Although it’s a bit pricier than others dimsum restaurants, but definitely worth a visit for those looking to try something new!

author: Doreen LSW
review_text:
Tried this popular dim sum place after hearing many good reviews, but it didn’t quite live up to expectations.

The dim sum variety was decent, but most dishes were average in taste — only the char siew pau was worth mentioning.
