It gets very busy on weekend mornings, so do come early, preferably before 9am, to get a table.

There are separate counters for steamed and fried dim sum, and you can also order fried noodles or beehoon from the staff.

Overall, an okay experience, but the food quality could definitely be improved.

author: Sandy Khik
review_text: Very good food and service here. We are frequent customers and recommend to everyone.

author: Jeff See
review_text: There for the first time. Really enjoy the food especially my friends from Singapore and Indonesia were very happy and satisfied. Food really tasted like fresh from the oven, or from steamer or from pan. Just the right touch for everything served. It's been a while I didn't have that kind of dim sum from the yesteryears in Canada.

author: KH Koay
review_text: Nice dimsum. The dimsum is cooked/steamed by order, some waiting time is needed, but not too long.

author: Hamann Eng
review_text: Hygiene place with air conditioning.  Delicious food with reasonable price. Food portion consider big for fried noodles/kuey tiaw/ rice. Good customer service with fast serving.

author: kk teoh
review_text:
A relatively new dim sum/yum cha place in Bukit Mertajam.  Located quite near St Anne Church.  Air conditioned and easy to park.  Good service from staff.

I believe the dim sums are steamed to order, which explains why it takes a while for your order to arrive on your table.  As a result, food is fresh and the dumplings relatively large compared to many other local dim sum outlets.  This is also reflected in the more expensive price, which is justified considering the service, quality and ambiance.  We also ordered a ying yong which cost RM15.90 (medium) which came with 3 fried fish cutlets.  The ying yong was OK, and portion decent.  However, it lacks wok hei and could have been more fragrant.

Overall, while the quality of the food is good, it does not have as much variety compared to some other dim sum outlets.  So, if you are looking for a huge variety, then this is not the place to go to.  But if you are looking for the traditional offerings such as siew mai, har gau, wu kok, chee cheong fun, etc., yup, this place is not too bad, albeit slightly more pricy.

author: Uncle Hong 1
review_text: After renovated was comfortable of chair with soft leather seat, inside have a air-conditioning dining area with no have any charge fee that was great. The food tasted good and delicious but for me this times wait around 20 minutes at 10pm that's decent. Order method just seat and waiting for waiters come for order except Curry Mix Rice. Overall, the environment, vibe, food and price not bad at all, that desrve to rate 5 stars.

author: Saravanan Baskaran
review_text:
The place had gone through a renovation, looks clean and modern but the utensil are dirty and rusted. Tried sharing to the staff but they were too busy. The "new" chairs are so different level. Plastic chairs feel softer and cleaner.

I used to visit here frequently before the reno, taste was good. Now I got no comments. From a comfortable environment, now it's tight and stuffy...

author: Andrew Yeoh
review_text: This nasi kandar shop is one of many of the Pelita chain. The shop is quite big. They have the usual Pelita set up. There are many types of curry to choose from. Nasi kandar and roti are available for breakfast, and nasi kandar and mi goreng for other times. The nasi kandar here is just average standard.

author: Clayton Dass Chalodass
review_text: Very bad service, sitting for the past 30 minutes and they can't clean the tables

author: Evon Ong
review_text: Order for nasi goreng no bawang but still have.  The staff here so terrible, can't even understand the order. We order Milo ais but he still wrote limau ais. We double check the order because the staff look so confuse. Then he only let us see what he wrote. The end it wrote wrongly then he only start correct the order. No more next visit. Alert!

author: Rashid Ismail
review_text: Next to highway heading northern. Best nasi kandar  then continue back journey.

author: LeePing Phuah
review_text:
Very poor food taste and quality
Papadam masuk angin
Inform waiter no chili and no pedas still end up with spicy plate of noodles.

author: Meera Yalangovan
review_text: The take away mamak mee goreng I bought just now totally disappointed me. Usually pelita auto city food is delicious compared to other branches but today it was not my day. It gave a crab curry smell and feel puke after eating. There is no mamak mee goreng smell and taste. I am not sure on how to attach picture here. Please improve on food tasting. This is totally disappointing.

author: Kumar Perumal
review_text: Very hot inside. Lunch not even tasty. Dont come upon the name. My lunch was ruined

author: hazman z
review_text: Nasi Kandar Original. Their reputation speaks for itself.

author: Enrique Wee
review_text: I only come here for their tandoori chicken and garlic nan of which I love. Prices are very reasonable. Clean and attentive waiters.

author: YoRHa 2B
review_text: I love the food here, especially the Briyani, delicious! The environment is clean and comfortable. The price is reasonable. Service is average though. If there's one thing that they can do better is service. Overall, I am very satisfied with this place and I will definitely be back to try some of the awesome curries!

author: krishnasamy samy
review_text: Tasty food. We went at breakfast time on Monday morning, less customers. Services good. But location is a problem, like it is in the centre of busiest area. If caught at peak time, the road is very jam. Nearby this restaurant is mcd outlet. So parking will be a problem at peak times.

author: Fazlie Ab Aziz
review_text: Not advised to be here late hours after 1 am. If you are seeking the best quality of freshly fried ayam goreng with nasik panas², I  recommend you guys go to chai leng park branch. But If you just wanna eat roti canai roti telur or just having a drinks this might be the right place.

author: Hello Indo
review_text:
i have no comment with the food and environment but the service is
among the worse I've encountered when taking order keep insisting on giving me food that i dont want and when i want the chicken breast part,keep insisting on the part with wing,bro just take my order la.honestly disappointed 2 times the charm third NEVER!

author: Saiful Yusoff
review_text: Buy chicken soup with 2 slice of bread... what was pack 1 slice of.bread cut into 2 piece & the chicken soup only contain very little portion of chicken. Very poor food serving for take away customer. Not worth it to pay rm5.95 for.chicken soup & rm 1.40 for the bread.

author: Mohanasundaram Sinniah
review_text:
Food portion is small (raw foods are expensive) fried chicken piece is too small, and doesn't feel worth it. Asked for mee goreng mamak, but came mee goreng basah. Teh tarik too much milk.
We used to go a few times, but this time around nothing great.

author: Jessie Teng
review_text: Roti is good but the staff were rude! The place was very dirty. Most of the tables were uncleared. My brother raised hand asked for waiter for few times and got no responses!

author: Muhammad Asyraf
review_text:
One of the worst Pelita.. Roti Canai not well cooked, half boiled eggs, either over or under cooked.

Many staffs but none show interest with customers.

author: rafflesia sh
review_text:
Food is ok only
Service is slow; not enought staff
The tables is not cleaned that fast after a customer finish eating
I had to order my own drink
Service slow
Roti canai is not smooth

author: Esther Hew
review_text: Had an Ipoh Ho Fun with Coffee set & toast. Food arrived promptly & it was yummy. Coffee was great! Ho Fun portion is very small for the price charged & not much shredded chicken. All the waiter & waitress had very good manners & customer service was top notch.

author: summer rogue
review_text: Service by the staffs were excellent. Food tasted superb. Everything was beyond expectation. The best kopitiam.

author: Debbie Voon
review_text: Local cuisine and has the taste of Penang. The fried chicken and rempah fish are my favorite. Love the milk tea and coffee too!

author: Angeline Lee
review_text: First time here easy to park and I love the vibe.  The girl even offered a chair for my dad who wasn’t feeling well. Their turmeric rice is flavorful and the coffee is really good I like their royal coffee. Maybe they can provide handle in the toilet for disabled people the toilet quite small so I can't get inside it to help my dad. Other than that everything was superb

author: Goh Ching Hong
review_text: Delicious food , nice environment , friendly staff. Will visit again

author: Jay Chong
review_text: A local breakfast coffee shop. ordered few dishes. Fried chicken cutlet was good, the fried chicken drumsticks flavor could be stronger for me. Both tom yam rice and ginger rice was just nice. Portion is big enough for one. For the drinks, cold drinks are not allowed to adjust the sweetness which is too sweet for me. The services were excellent. Overall it’s a nice place to having breakfast or lunch with family and friends.

author: Kai En Ng
review_text:
An Unforgettable Dining Experience!

From the moment we stepped in, the ambiance was warm, elegant, and inviting. The service was impeccable — attentive without being intrusive, and every staff member made us feel genuinely welcomed.

We tried the chef's tasting menu, and every dish was a masterpiece. The flavors were perfectly balanced, presentation was stunning, and the ingredients were clearly top quality. The [insert signature dish here] was a standout — melt-in-your-mouth and absolutely unforgettable.

What truly set this restaurant apart was the attention to detail, from the perfectly paired wine selections to the little touches like palate cleansers and a hand-written thank you note at the end of the meal.

Whether you're celebrating something special or just want to treat yourself, this place is worth every cent. Highly recommended — we’ll definitely be coming back!

author: Jun
review_text:
I personally think this restaurant has it's own unique style and taste

The price in my opinion is abit expensive but it's totally worth it on what your ordering 🤤. I ordered the Nasi Lemak and the chicken piece is huge 😱

The Restaurant is Halal certified so for the Muslims who are interested, can try out this place.

The service is super fast, I just ordered a few minutes and then the food is already prepared.

Overall the environment is clean and comfortable. Hope some of you guys can try out this amazing place 😁 👍

author: Andrew Yeoh
review_text: This SBK outlet is located in a rather quiet part of Taman Perda. They serve Malaysian morning breakfast favourites like nasi lemak, curry noodles, and toast. There is a wide range of beverages to choose from whether hot or cold. The food is tasty. The coffee is also very good.

author: Peck Kim Loh
review_text:
Absolutely fantastic experience!
From the moment we walked in, everything was top-notch — the ambiance was warm and welcoming, the staff were incredibly attentive and friendly, and the food… absolutely unforgettable. Every dish was beautifully presented and bursting with flavor. You can really tell that high-quality ingredients and care went into everything. Whether you're going for a casual night out or celebrating something special, this place hits the mark. I’ll definitely be coming back. Highly recommend!

author: KH Koay
review_text: Turmeric rice is nice. Coffee is OK. A good place to visit especially when it rains, because the parking is covered. Not recommending its QQ noodle, portion is very small, and roti canai is hard.

author: Chuah Keat Lee
review_text:
Superb service and delicious food.

We orders the turmeric rice with deep fried chicken. The rice portion were decent and the chicken was delish! My wife had the sambal prawns - it was yum! I ate the toasted black bread and half boiled egg. This was decent.

The waiters and waitresses were attentive to us. Some were able to speak English and some can't speak English well. Those who couldn't, tried to speak professionally anyhow 👍🏻

My only gripe is the price. Each dish cost nearly RM20. The toasted bread and half boiled egg was RM12! (I wasn't that hungry, therefore, ordered the "cheapest" and smallest portion) Go to any coffee shop, it cost less than RM5.

author: mohamad arif
review_text: With nice place and nice food. Surely great to come with whole family

author: Tan Gary
review_text:
Preparation need to speed up. Understand when there is big crowd but when subside it still took some time to serve. Nevertheless servers are polite.

Food tasted good, spice and curry has it’s own unique flavour. Curry chicken a bit of a let down. Meat did not cook well. Called to return and prepared a second time on the same bowl still resulted with a stiff chicken drumstick.

Would like to complement the drink. Pack enough power to stir your taste bud. Thumbs up for serving cold drink without ice to preserve the flavour instead of being diluted with ice.

Overall, good enough to make me think of another visit. Price was acceptable. But really need to work on the curry chicken. Not everyone can stand the spotted stain blood when cut it up.

author: Khai Shuen
review_text: Food here was sooo good the sambal taste really nice. A little bit expensive but the portion was big. Drinks and coffee was so aromatic

author: Gary Looi CW
review_text:
This is my first time visiting n here are the things I tried: Nanyang Fat Spread Sugar Toast set, Cold Royal Black Coffee with Milk, n Tumeric Fried Rice with Ayam Goreng.

The fried chicken is huge! The toast set comes with soft boiled eggs. The price is reasonable although slightly expensive.

The service crew are very attentive! They'll guide you to an available table, give you a menu n an order chit. Payment at the counter after you're done ordering.

author: Lee Hui Tang
review_text: Having breakfast with family’s ~ we enjoying our food very much … environment quite comfortable n good service provided.

author: Ah Rui
review_text:
Curry is cooked with milk instead of santan. nice curry despite a little bit spicy for me.
overall nice food served. service nice, the staffs are friendly and helpful 👍
they came over and explain food menu patiently , thank you 😊
The drinks we felt a bit too sweet, hopefully can prepare others option for customer, like sugar level / sweetness level of the drinks
😉

author: YING PEI TAN
review_text: A well-known brand of coffee for a long time. Feeling amazed by this concept store which initially I thought was just a kopitiam. The food is good especially the  whole grain bread with butter kaya. Sweet and wonderful taste as a breakfast for a bread lover like me. The noodles are OK, but the best is no doubt their coffee.  Cold coffee without ice and full of flavour with very little sweetness. Amazing! Same went to that in hot. Looking forward to try their roti canai and other menu items. The price was more to cafe pricing, as we spent about RM20 per person. Seating will need to wait as it was quite crowded at the weekend. However, their service and management were really systematic and fast.

author: MRay Chan
review_text:
One of the best place to have your caffeine.
The Nitro Nanyang Cold Brew was a bold and refreshing pick-me-up, with its smooth, rich flavor that hit all the right notes.
It’s a great experience. Food is good, and the menu offers a wide variety of delicious and mouthwatering food.
Nicely presented. Staffs were also proactive and friendly.
RonChan25/7/2024

author: Hana Teoh
review_text:
1st time here. Restaurant is clean and cooling. There is a prayer room for the Muslim. Staffs are friendly and easy to approach.

Food is delicious. Pricey but big portion (for myself and family).

We order smoke lamb rib platter (10/10 excellent), stuffed cheese burger (8/10 common but tasty), brisket chicken burger (10/10 damn good), children set (7/10 small portion) and  butter soda (5/10 too sweet).

The lamb rib platter was RM73.05 (245g).

author: aqilah yahya
review_text:
I’m glad I waited patiently for the hype to die down before visiting this restaurant. I came in on a Saturday afternoon, and it was pleasantly quiet with only a few customers. The restaurant offers its own parking, and there were plenty of empty spaces when I got there, which was a nice bonus.

The interior has a vibey, laid back ambiance with cool neon decorations and plenty of seating. Service was moderate, but understandable since they prepare food fresh upon ordering. I ordered the smoked beef burger to dine in and it was delicious! The crispy fried onions added a great crunch and elevated the overall flavor. The BBQ sauce was nicely tangy and complemented the smoky taste of the beef. The patty itself was thick and juicy, though I wish it had been seasoned with a touch more salt to really bring out the flavors.

My only complaint is the plating. I would have preferred the burger served on a plate rather than wrapped in half a burger wrapper and placed vertically in a box. This made the bottom soggy, and my first bite lacked sauce since it had all pooled at the bottom, making the initial experience less enjoyable.

Overall, I had a great time and thoroughly enjoyed my burger to the last bite. I’ll definitely be coming back to try more of their burger options. LOVE!

author: Nur Ayu Abdullah
review_text:
This is my second time eating at Woodfire. The first was in Ampang, and the burgers were excellent, and satisfying to eat. So I was looking forward to enjoying the burger at this branch.

However it was a disappointing experience. The burger I ordered was stuffed cheese burger and it was nothing like the one I ate in Ampang. There was too much sauce until the burger became soggy and there was no shape of the burger itself. I couldn’t eat the burger properly and ended up eating the bread, patty and condiments separately because I couldn’t hold the burger to take a proper bite. The patty was ok but couldn’t taste it properly because of too much sauce.

Hope the restaurant can improve on the burgers as I’m willing to come back next time and try again.

author: Hanif Iqwan Abd Maulud
review_text: Tried their brisket burger, it was really delicious. The beef patty, beef bacon and brisket were juicy but the seasoning wasn't deep enough to reach inside. Overall the food was superb. Parkings are seem limited in busy day or holiday. The dining atmosphere was enjoyable because the seats were clean and it was very cold inside. Really recommended for trying

author: SoloJoe
review_text:
Diner decor, that felt old and new,
Surrounded by Neon signs and colorful food displays
Plenty of seating , including large booths.
Air con needed to be colder.

Food:
5/5:
Lamb ribs: cost is determined by weight.
I chose the 245 grams
The meat was tender, flakey and smoky with just the right amount of fat. First time experiencing lamb ribs, and definitely not the last

4/5
Smoke brisket
More on the leaner side, but the fattiness blended well. Excellent texture and tenderness.

5/5:
Curly Fries. Crispy and seasoned with BBQ powder. Super addicting

The Pit Masters knows how to smoke their meats.
The Best I have tried in Penang
Great work 👏🏻👏🏻👏🏻⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

If this review was helpful, please give it a 👍

Happy Eats

author: Mizna Mujees
review_text:
This was our first visit here. We ordered a smoked beef burger, a steak platter, and a lemonade — all of which were really good. The atmosphere was very cozy and pleasant.

However, one thing that disappointed us was that the burger was served with plastic cutlery, which made it quite difficult to cut. We also asked for an extra plate, but were told that they don’t provide additional plates.

The concept is great, but the staff’s attitude really needs some improvement.

author: Zahid Patel
review_text: This place was a reccomdation whilst we were in Penang, and boy did it not dissapoint! I'm a meat lover so I got the Brisket Burger which was extremely tender and explosive with flavours! My Mrs got the Nashville Chicken Platter which was equally as delicious! Juicy and the batter was spicy as expected! We had to order another Brisket Burger and some Lamb Chops for takeout :P Highly reccomend this place if you're in town! Thanks Aiman for the reccomendation :P

author: Poopmaster
review_text:
Excellent burgers. You get what you pay for.
The music in the house is too loud though. You want the food to be the center piece, not the music.
Turn it down a little so diners can have their intimate moments. With the burgers that is.

author: Liz Ali
review_text: Great food overall — juicy burger, tender brisket, and the Mad Hen chicken that nearly set my mouth on fire 🔥😅 Just a small request: please provide proper forks and knives, especially for the brisket platter. You can see the aftermath in the pic 😬🍴

author: Cher Ong
review_text: Atmosphere is quite good especially during the hot sunny day. They provide parking lots. If u visit on weekdays, shouldn't be a problem.  Ordered the gourmet chicken 🍔  & also smoked chicken 🍔.  Patty is huge but in terms of the sauce they used, I'm not a fan. Sauce are more to the sweet side & it's loaded with sauce. Make the whole burger tastes greasy. Even when I brushed off the sauce, the flavour is still bold. They don't have set so price is on the higher side when u add on fries & drinks.

author: HARSHAAN ARUMUGAM
review_text: (31/8/25) I tried the Stuffed Cheese Burger (beef), Mushroom Burger (chicken), Nashville hot chicken platter, and a chocolate milkshake. Both burgers were average – the cheese burger had too much sauce, making the bun soggy. The Nashville chicken tasted good but was too heavily coated in spices for my liking. The chocolate milkshake was the best part – rich and creamy. Serving time was around 15 minutes. The atmosphere was nice, but the toilet could be cleaner. Price-wise, it’s definitely on the expensive side – mine came to around RM90. Overall, maybe worth trying once.

author: Charlie
review_text: They have a huge selection of burgers, milkshakes, and other sides. The burgers were flavourful but a little greasy and can be messy (because they are generous with their fillings). Not to worry, there are sinks in the restaurant to wash your hands.

author: Liyana Zahid
review_text: Nice restaurant with a cozy ambience. Parking is quite limited, but we were lucky to get a spot within the restaurant area. We tried the brisket burger, vanilla shake, Nashville hot chicken platter and a kids meal. The brisket burger was tasty and well done. However, the Nashville hot chicken was a bit disappointing in flavor, and the drink was too sweet for our liking. Overall, a decent experience with some room for improvement.

author: Irum Pervez
review_text: The burgers were really good, especially the crisp y Smoked burger. Their Nashville is good but spicy! Couldn't find a place to sit - fully packed. The order delivery is quite smooth even if you get a later number. Overall, worth trying!

author: simone food.channel
review_text:
[holiao]
1) Overall - Hamburger shop, self service counter, spacious air cond seating, plenty parking, nicely decorated, food and drink selection are burger, milkshake, beef brisket and more from Woodfire Penang - Burgers, Ribs, Fries, Shakes
2) brisket burger - Tender, smoky, thick brisket packed between soft buns, rich in flavor and perfectly juicy. Balanced with fresh toppings and sauce, though could use a touch more seasoning. Satisfying and hearty for meat lovers.
3) Mushroom burger - Earthy and umami-rich, the shiitake mushroom delivers a bold, meaty bite. Nicely grilled with juicy texture, complemented by fresh toppings and a soft bun. A great vegetarian option that doesn’t compromise on flavor.

author: Elaine T
review_text:
Feels like the whole place was too hyped up on social media… the food was just so-so…
We had the Nashville fried chicken, all we can taste was the spice but no flavour. Burgers were soggy from the sauce and they disintegrated when we hold it up. Milkshakes were just pumps of sugar syrup but no milk nor other taste. The fries were a sad bunch: we were supposed to get curly fries but we got fries that are not curly, but probably the ones left in the fryer after the curly ones got served. The brisket was also too tough to eat.

not enough seats, too loud to talk, not enough parking too.

author: Digital Transformers
review_text: Hands down to the best burger in Penang! Ive tried couple of others famous gourmet burgers in Penang but Woodfire simply stands out. No viral marketing, just quality product speaks volume! Kudos to the team keep up the taste consistency!

author: Mamu Vinyl
review_text:
Food:
1. Brisket beef burger is marvelous. Very greasy.
2. BBQ burger is mediocre. Ok
3. Nashville Chicken is super hot. Not suitable for kids. But ok for adults.
4. Cheesesteak is ok.
5. Beverage mainly on sodas including Barbican.

Service:
1. Poor. I'm puzzled why charge Service Tax 7% on a self service restaurant?
2. No cleaning at the hand washing area.
3. No tissue provided with the menu ordered. This is unacceptable. You ate a greasy burger without tissue supplied. You need to manually take the tissue at the washing area.
4. Dine seating is uncomfortable. The table is too low.

Atmosphere:
1. Parking is ridiculously planned. Should make a parking box or customers will park scattered and consume unnecessary space.

author: Brandon Butler
review_text: Absolutely Epic huge food. Brisket is tender and delisted. Cheesesteak is a messy delicious feast. Burger is just amazing to look at. Biscoff milkshake must try. Nashville hot chicken tenders are crispy and tasty, but beware they really are HOT. Proper hot. Overall it’s a must try, especially when you get tired of local food after being here for a while. It’s not super cheap but you can eat good here for reasonable price if you don’t go all out like we did. Just a cheesesteak by itself is already a meal and it’s good value for money compared to other places around Penang.

author: Farhana Ismail
review_text:
They have limited private parking space. We arrived a few minutes before opening times and there were others who waited too. The ordering system was the same as fast food restaurants. We came on Monday noon and the food took a pretty short time to get ready.
We like the burgers especially the sliced meat part. Not overwhelmed by sauce nor mayonnaise, the patty with the accessories including fried onion already tasted good. The matcha milkshake was nice too, less sweet. The price was reasonable. The dining place was clean and comfortable. There's also a toilet.

author: Matthew Somerfield
review_text: We had so much anticipation visiting this place in Penang, however we were sadly disappointed, I got the lamb shank the taste was ok but the lamb was swimming in oil and very chewy, my wife got the Nasi Kandar and she was not impressed at all by the food. However this may be not our flavour as many people coming and going. So might be a personal taste.

author: Arnab Paul
review_text: Crowded, but worth it. There was a 30 min+ line of locals on Sat afternoon, but it moved fast. Plenty of open spaces inside. I got the bhindi (steamed okra), cabbage and goat curry. Of course, an assortment of curries were ladled on top! The food tasted fresh and was finger-licking good. Highly recommended.

author: Michael Arthur
review_text: WOW. What an incredible dining experience. The flavors here are STELLAR. Yes, it’s heavy and it’s oily, but you will love it. I did!! One of the best meals I had in Malaysia.

author: Akinobu Ray
review_text:
Great Nasi Kandar. Queue to get served. If it's raining, bring an umbrella and if you are allergic to the sun like a vampire, bring an umbrella. The queues can be long but don't be deterred.

Didn't try the lamb shank goreng(fried) but will do it next time.

The lamb curry is flavourful and just nice spicy. Fried chicken drumsticks a bit dry but tasty all the same. The taste of the food leans towards the sweeter side of neutral hence only 4* from me.

Place is relatively clean and ample seating since they expanded to yet another shop house. For the ice cream people who melt in the heat, there are limited air conditioned dining spaces.

Overall, a great place to experience Nasi Kandar in Penang.

author: Zazirash
review_text: Having dinner at Deens Maju felt like joining a Penang ritual — queue first, eat later. The line was crazy long, but with good company it didn’t feel like such a drag. Staff kept things moving and were friendly despite the chaos. When the plate landed, it looked like a masterpiece, drenched in kuah campur. Taste-wise though, it was more hype than punch — the curry felt a bit watered down and the flavours didn’t wow me. In Malaysia, queues don’t always equal greatness, but the vibe here still made it an experience worth having once.

author: Faiz Soudagar
review_text:
Deen Maju never disappoints.
There’s something special about the food here the flavours are beautifully balanced, that slight tartness mixed with spices hits perfectly every single time. You can really taste the care and consistency in every dish.
One of those places where the food just speaks for itself. Absolutely love it and will always come back!

author: Nizzam
review_text:
✅ Ayam bawang relatively delicious
✅ Flavours are beautifully balanced
✅ Place is relatively clean and ample seating
✅ Shorter waiting time
✅ Above average price tag
💢 Its a long queue all the time even weekdays
💢 Limited and paid parking

author: K.H.
review_text:
Visited at night, ayam goreng bawang sold out.
Fried chicken is also nice.
Kuah campur with rice is delicious.

author: Ofi
review_text:
The queue is long but fast service.
The room was big, so you'll get table.
Went there at 8.30 pm and still a lot of people to wait.
The taste was good. My first time tried nasi kandar so i can't compare how good this nasi kandar is.
Overall was good!

author: Jonathan Hisham
review_text:
Still the best Nasi Kandar in Penang if not Malaysia. The curry taste is still going to make you smile with happiness and feeling satisfied to the last drop. Queue is always there but it moves fairly quick. Just know what you want when the guy ask you what lauk you want. Pricewise still reasonable. I took 2 large prawns and still below RM 20. If I taken this at other mamak, for sure will charge me RM30 to 50 on average.
Tips- you can still order what you want after you sat down to eat. They will bring it over to you in a jiffy. So changing minds is allowed here. Enjoy!!

author: Isaac Fuente
review_text:
We went here on our first day in Penang, the food was amazing, a queue (which is always a good sign), but goes quickly… no more than 10 minutes.

If you’re in Penang, and want to try Nasi Kandar, this is a must

author: William ORourke
review_text: Amazing! Best to visit on an off hour so you don’t have to wait. We were surprised at how friendly service was and welcomed. Be sure to order the combo dish with all the proteins and sauces with a carrot/apple juice.

author: Kim Soon Chua
review_text: We decided to try something different whilst we were in Penang.  And Nasi Kandar was the choice.  We heard so much about this redtuarant that we had to try it.  We went there at 3.30pm and a long queue had formed. We waited for 1 hour before it was our turn to order.  So much for trying something different.  We had the ayam berempah which was good.  The meat was tender.  We also had the  sotong which was in my mind average.  The curry sauces were standard Indian fare.  Overall, not worth the long queue.

author: Vibricia P
review_text:
Deens Maju is one of the most popular nasi kandar spots in Penang. You’ll often see long queues, especially during lunch and dinner — a clear sign of its popularity among locals and tourists alike.

While the food is flavorful and portions are decent, it may not be to everyone’s taste. If you prefer subtler spices or cleaner flavors, it might feel a bit heavy or overly rich. The curries tend to be bold and oily, which some people love — but it wasn’t quite my thing.

Deens Maju is clearly loved by many — but food is personal, and for me, it was just okay. Good to try once for the experience, but probably not a regular stop.

author: Finniss
review_text: Worth the hype. Probably the best meal I had in Penang. Generous with the gravies. Delicious meats and a large selection to choose from. I enjoyed the Quail eggs. A must try in Penang.

author: Zul Shinoda
review_text:
About

Deens Maju Nasi Kandar is a must-visit destination for anyone looking to experience authentic Penang cuisine. Located on Jalan Gurdwara in George Town, this popular eatery is known for serving some of the best nasi kandar on the island. Situated just a short distance from the bustling Komtar area, Deens Maju is conveniently accessible for both locals and tourists exploring the vibrant streets of Penang.

Nasi kandar, a dish rooted in Penang's culinary heritage, is a flavorful rice meal served with a variety of curries and side dishes. Deens Maju has earned a stellar reputation for its perfectly spiced curries, tender meats, and generous portions. The restaurant is particularly famous for its fried chicken, which is crispy on the outside and succulent on the inside, as well as its rich, aromatic curry sauces that complement the rice and sides beautifully.

author: N A
review_text:
Tastes light and delicious.
The price just OK
The best Nasi Kandar that I ever tried.
The queue quite long even the inside not full.

author: Mohd Ilyas
review_text: A strategically located eatery in the city center. Tasty dishes with plenty of variety. Limited parking — expect a short walk. Queues can be a bit long but manageable. Elderly and pregnant women can wait inside and find a seat first.

author: Marcus Goh
review_text:
passes by without much queue at odd hours, decided to try out due to good review.
good tasting food, nice open space to dine.
hands washing point available for those who prefer to touch their food.

author: isey cherr
review_text:
Deens Maju definitely serves one of the best nasi kandar I’ve had so far (both me and my wife agree!). The taste is perfectly balanced – not too spicy, not too sweet, just right. Came on a weekday and didn’t have to wait long. Parking is convenient too, just across the street at the private car park.

If you’re a fried chicken lover, my advice is to take extra – it’s really tasty! The sotong is also top notch. Service is fast and efficient, and cleanliness is well maintained. Overall, a must-visit nasi kandar spot in Penang! 😄

author: Poh Tuen
review_text:
The prices at Hameediyah are approximately 20% higher than at most Nasi Kandar establishments in Penang. Personally, I found the flavors somewhat bland, despite my preference for food that is not overly salty or sweet. The spice level is mild, and the aromatic curry lacks the richness typically expected. I recommend adding salted egg to help balance the subtle flavors and enhance the overall taste. This reflects my personal experience.

*** Dine In ***

Qty Item Price (RM)

1 White Rice 2.00
1 Regular Onion Chicken 12.00
2 Mutton Curry @ 10.00 20.00
1 Lady’s Finger (1 plate) 2.50
1 Salted Egg 1.70

Subtotal (6 items): 38.20
Net Total: 38.20

author: Melissa Rabar-Swenson
review_text:
We were recommend to come here from a local bar tender fit the food.  He was not wrong, we were so pleased to actually come here. Our first few days here were not impressive due to hot spot tourist traps and less authentic places, so this was a blessing.  Then the and guy recommend us to go next door to the coffee shop for true local coffee and breakfast.

Anyway back to Hameediyah  - chicken, delicious, basmati rice, amazing, the sauces and graveys were nice, little spice and full of flavour 😋 we shared our meal and we were SO full. They really piled it on.
Service was lovely and they guided you in all of it.

author: Joshua Chia
review_text: First time trying nasi kandar in Malaysia and totally impressed. The dishes are all deep in flavour and and very rich. So good we ate here twice during our short trip in Penang. Be sure to order the Ayam Bawang. Staff were very friendly too

author: Dale Rowan
review_text: Absolutely loved it! Food is amazing.  Staff really helpful as we didn't speak the language.  Cash or QR code only no card. No alcohol but mango lasi was good. Strongly recommend lamb which had generous lamb shank, and honey chicken.

author: ShuiHung Tan
review_text:
Hidden menu from Spooky till 🎃

After sampling Hameediyah’s famed dishes, it’s fair to say the culinary experience was a real treat for the taste buds. The biryani burst with aromatic spices, while the murtabak was every bit as comforting as its reputation suggests. Yet, one can’t help but note that the pricing left a rather odd taste.

Apparently, the bill varies depending on whether you can present a MYKAD or MYPR—meaning locals get one price and foreign visitors another, despite identical portions. This distinction isn’t exactly advertised upfront, which could catch travellers on the hop. The real twist came with the Mango Lassi, mysteriously charged at a higher “fresh Indian mango” rate from what seemed like a hidden menu. None of the staff could give a clear answer or show the price anywhere in the shop, which felt more than a little eerie.

A cracking meal, but transparency on pricing would make the experience far more palatable.

author: Harold Piel
review_text: Amazing food experience: looked at menu and was a bit overwhelmed. The cook dude just called us over and said he’d show us the food, and build a plate to our needs. Results outstanding! You got to give this a try.

author: donny ho boon tiong
review_text: On 01Nov25, Saturday, I brought my family and my daughter mother/grandmother in law to our 1st outing to Penang. Also our 1st time at Hameediyah Restaurant. The food was great especially rendang beef, fried bitter gourd, captain chicken and malay rojah. The serving staffs were friendly and attentive. We have a enjoyable time there.

author: Raymund Gerard
review_text:
This was recommended to us by a local. The food was very good and there was so much of it! It's not cheap but you also get a lot of food. We went in the evening and the line was much shorter than during the day.
The staff were friendly and quite helpful as this was our first time experiencing Nasi Kandar.
For people going there for the first time, you select what you want and pay in one shop, and then they bring the food to you in the dining area a few doors down.

author: Keegan Talbott
review_text: The overall taste of the cooking is considered really good, very tasty and the herbs made them aromatic to the max. This is not my first time patronizing this shop. But today is another level, Rm28 for a piece of ¼ Mutiara Chicken is the biggest let down when comes to the texture of the chicken meat, was as if cutting off from a lamb shoulder. Color of the meat looked like a mummified chicken. I thought was chewing a Wrigley's gum. Beef was leathery though it managed to beat the chicken. Glad enough to have ordered their fried bigger gourd, acar and papadam which managed to bolsterd the rating.

author: William Chu
review_text: The oldest Nasi Kandar spot in Penang operating since 1907. Meats are very tender. Portions are big, lots of meat, variety of dishes to choose, and different curries. Ordered and paid the dish at one shop, and the waiter helped carry the plate of food to the shop next door to sit and dine. Very clean food and very clean tables.

author: Steve Capen
review_text: One ofy favorite meals in all of SE Asia!  The flavors were incredible and the staff were absolutely outstanding, highly recommend 😋😋

author: Mike G
review_text: I had murtabah daging and it was AMAZING. Nasi kandar also top notch. These guys know what they're doing, the flavours are extraordinary. A meal here will be a high point in any trip to Penang 😋

author: Marina John Gantie
review_text:
Located on Campbell Street, Hameediyah Nasi Kandar is one of the most famous and long-standing nasi kandar spots in Penang. There's almost always a queue, and for good reason — the food is absolutely worth the wait.

The variety of dishes available is impressive. On my visit, I spotted some unique options like rabbit curry and fried baby sea crab alongside the usual crowd-pleasers. You can choose between plain white rice or nasi briyani (fragrant yellow rice) as your base, depending on your mood.

The process is a bit unique: you select your dishes at one shop, pay there, and then you're redirected to another unit to dine. Over at the dining area, you can order your drinks, wash your hands, use the toilet, and settle your drink bill separately at the counter after your meal.

Overall, the food is amazing and full of flavor — rich curries, vegetable dishes, and aromatic rice that truly hit the spot. It's no wonder this place remains a favorite among locals and tourists alike.

Highly recommended if you're in Penang and craving a truly satisfying nasi kandar experience!

author: Ryan
review_text:
As mid as it comes. They try to get you to buy most expensive meats/seafood.

I asked for extra gravy/sauce but didn’t get that. Chicken was served cold. Beef was dry. Such a disappointing experience. Having tried multiple Nasi kandar prior to this place, I don’t think I’m wrong in saying it no longer deserves the reputation it once had.

The price is also more than it should be for what it is.

author: Sha Zamrinor
review_text:
IT SHOULD TASTE LIKE PENANG.
NOT KL.

I came to Hameediyah with my friend and my mother, expecting the comfort of a good plate of nasi kandar. Instead, what I got was an experience that felt half-show, half-food — and only slightly satisfying.

The queue was long, as expected — but that’s not the problem. What really threw me off was the behaviour of certain people in the line. There were customers more focused on filming themselves than ordering their food. Loud TikTok narrations. Tripods set up in the middle of walkways. People posing with plates while others waited patiently behind them. It was disrespectful, disruptive, and honestly, exhausting. If you came here for makan, you had to push past a content-creator circus just to get to the counter.

When it was finally my turn, I stood in front of a wide range of lauk, trying to decide. Classic kuah campur for me — I like the chaos, the flavour, the mess. The prawns caught my eye — fat, glossy, drowning in orange curry — but I hesitated. Pricey, intimidating, and I didn’t want to be disappointed. So I passed.

Taste-wise, Hameediyah sits in a strange space — somewhere between KL’s polished, curated tourist scene and Penang’s unapologetic bare minimum. It tries to hold onto heritage, but feels semi-delivered. Safe. Predictable. Sanitised, even.

Then came my mother. No chaos, no confusion. She stood at the counter and said clearly:
“Kari kambing. Sayur. Jangan campur.”
No extra instructions. No need for the gravy drama. Even the abang hesitated — like her request went against some kind of nasi kandar rulebook. But she didn’t flinch. Her plate was focused, grounded, and quietly bold. It reminded me that sometimes, less truly is more.

We also shared a murtabak, which unfortunately, was the low point of the visit.
Murtabak should be judged by how generous it is with filling, how thick it folds, how the meat spills at the edge.
Hameediyah’s wasn’t a textbook — it was a primary school exercise book. Thin, underfilled, dry. Definitely not worth the price tag. I’ve had better from pasar Ramadan stalls under plastic tents, wrapped in oily brown paper.

To me, a good nasi kandar should haunt you after the meal. It should cling to your fingers with spice, leave your shirt faintly smelling of curry, and stay with you for hours — in all the best ways.
But Hameediyah didn’t do that.
It felt… semi-delivered. Like someone had wrapped up a memory and served it reheated.

Come here if you want to say you’ve been. Take your photos, maybe even enjoy a decent plate. But if you’re looking for that true, finger-staining, gravy-sticking-to-your-spoon experience — the one that tastes like a messy plate at 11am in Penang or Butterworth — you’ll need to keep looking.

author: Steven Teo
review_text: This is my second time dining at this restaurant. I felt the food does not live up to the hype. The curry and gravy lacked of flavour and is not as good as many other nadi kandar that I have visited. And it's quite pricey too. Overall, I will say it's average.

author: Fathin Yusuf
review_text:
Trying the oldest nasi kandar restaurant in Malaysia! Service is fast even though long queue. Bought lamb shank RM55, tiger prawn 2 pcs RM90 and two sets of nasi kandar (rice, thick curry soup, lady finger), beef murtabak and drinks. Total RM167.80.

You can dine in here as they were a lot of tables (3 floor shop). Overall is a good experience!

author: Lokman Black Jr
review_text: Nice curry for curry hunters. I love it so much. The price is affordable for everyone subject to the selection of foods. 1 thing I feel so annoyed about is that they will recommend the high price of foods without telling the price. They suggested to me ayam piru without telling me the price which cost me RM45 for 2 pcs of ayam piru!!!! So be careful not to repeat the same mistake like I did. Ask the price 1st before proceeding with the meal. That's the only thing I feel bad about about this place. The rest just enjoy your food and I believe you'll love it so much.

author: Ummairah Mahmood
review_text:
Yummyyyyyyyy! Had to queue for almost an hour to get my hands on Nasi kandar but it was all worth it..!

A must try! My fave is the Ayam goreng bawang!

author: Sh Cheng
review_text:
Super crowded during peak hour.
Select your dishes, walkover to another shop for seating, the restaurant will serve your food there.
Good experience at their HQ.
Be ready to pay.

author: YippieYaYa
review_text:
Visited Foh San for dim sum, and overall, the experience was quite normal. The food was just so-so—nothing particularly memorable in terms of taste or variety.

However, one highlight was the service. The elderly lady server was very nice and friendly, which made the visit more pleasant. The restaurant itself is spacious, but the food didn’t quite live up to its reputation.

Worth a try if you're nearby, but don’t expect anything exceptional.

author: Eunice 유니스 Chong
review_text:
Huge, clean and well ventilated place. You order from a menu instead of having someone pushing the cart like old school method. The price of the dim sum is the same as how the building looks- extravagant!

Siew Mai is RM7.60 (above average) but the siew mai has very small bites of scallops, mushrooms, and prawns.. Fishball (RM6.90) is huge and soft. I guess the locals are right about this place- it caters mainly to tourist.

Chille sauce has sour (lime?) taste with some garlic aftertaste.. One option for sauce only.

author: Wai Man Cheong
review_text: As a kid I remembered coming here and was always happy to visit. Nowadays the food was okay. Not bad but nothing outstanding. If you want a quick dim sum it’s okay but don’t expect to be overwhelmed.

author: Karmen
review_text: Have been here many times. Every time I’m in Ipoh. It’s a spacious, clean and efficient place. I would recommend this place for dim sum for tourists. The quality of the food is above average and service is efficient. Range is pretty good for food but very limited for drinks.

author: Banuaji P
review_text: Nice place to hangout and enjoy some dim sum. The dimsum is good and they have many choice of them. Its not cheap but you can tell with the building. Its big.

author: Lee Mun chew
review_text: Hey there! I think this is the famous Ipoh tourist dim sum shop. It’s always packed with people, especially on weekends and public holidays. But I managed to come in on a weekday, so I didn’t have to wait for ages. The food was really good, overall. And the environment and design are so traditional, it’s like stepping back in time.

author: Janelle
review_text: Delicious dim sum with plenty of variety to choose from! You’ll need to take a number as there may be a queue, but overall the wait was quite quick. 🥢😋

author: The Genesis Family
review_text: Come early to get queue number, long waiting is expected at this Ipoh famous dim sum spot, certainly lives up to its reputation. Be prepared for a bustling atmosphere and potential queues, but it's part of the experience. Their dim sum selection is vast and generally delicious, with classics like har gow and siew mai always fresh and tasty. It's a classic, no-frills setting focused purely on the food. For an authentic and satisfying dim sum breakfast, it's a consistently good choice.

author: oscar w
review_text: came here as their famous counterpart across the street has long queue. service is very prompt amd attentive the moment you step into the restaurant. friendly waitress will come over and recommend promotional items. overall the dishes are value for money but taste wise not too memorable. still decent dimsum to have though in a comfortable atmosphere.

author: Andi ArcoStringsAsia
review_text: Nostalgic dim sum place.. The dim sum is good but I feel the savory offerings has too much msg & has a sugary taste.. Being premium priced, they should focus on refinements in their dim sum dishes.. Service is prompt but I still prefer the plates to be empty before collection. While I still prefer the old days of Foh San ( near the old association) , it is still a must visit place in Ipoh.

author: Ng Wan Keat
review_text:
Once a bustling hub of authentic dim sum in Ipoh, this restaurant was once synonymous with delectable flavors and vibrant mornings. However, time seems to have taken its toll on the establishment. After years of opting for other dim sum spots, we decided to revisit, drawn by nostalgia and the promise of spacious seating when other restaurants were packed.

The experience, however, was underwhelming. The airy dining area, while clean and uncrowded, lacked the lively atmosphere of its prime years. The dim sum offerings, though presented in standard portions, lacked the flavor and charm that once set them apart. At a higher price point, the tasteless dishes failed to justify the cost.

While it remains a convenient option when other places are full, the restaurant's faded glory serves as a reminder of its better days—now more of a last resort than a must-visit destination.

author: Yeoh Ts
review_text: The pumpkin pork rib porridge was really comforting and warming, cooked till super smooth and silky. The dim sum siu mai and har gao were just so-so for me.

author: Chi Ling
review_text:
Best char siew pau I’ve had in a long time. Slightly fluffy pastry all the way through.

The yam taro pastry was super fantastic too and thoroughly recommended.

author: Paul Leong
review_text:
Foh San in Ipoh is a bona fide town institution — the kind of dim sum house that generations have visited, where the building itself feels like part of the city’s culinary heritage. The space is grand, bustling, and unmistakably old-school: large round tables, trolley energy even without the actual trolleys, and that signature din of families, tourists, and regulars all converging under one roof. It has the atmosphere of a place that has always been there and probably always will be.

But when it comes to the food, the experience is… fine. Their standard dim sum offerings — siu mai, har gao, char siew bao, chee cheong fun — are competent, familiar, and reliably executed, but nothing particularly memorable. It’s exactly what you’d expect from a long-standing establishment playing to a broad crowd: serviceable and comforting, but not pushing boundaries or standing out from the pack. You go to Foh San for the nostalgia and the institution-status charm; the dim sum itself is standard fare, and that’s perfectly in line with what the place intends to be.

author: Balee Tong
review_text:
Service is good for a typical dimsum place. Bright and enthusiastic. But so so if the price is considered. The venue can get a bit warm during busy times.
Xiao long Pau had thick skin and bland soup. Siumai & hakau was good but not worth the price. Lomaikai, lopakkau & wu kok was good. Ribs was good but more bones than meat. Overall the food was so so, and overrated considering the price. For the same price bracket I prefer dimsum station (not in ipoh).

author: Susan Yong
review_text: Food quality was dropped compared last time. Dim sum very normal. Nothing to shout out.

author: Mauyeeyee
review_text:
They have an extensive menu and lots of dishes they don’t serve in Australia, I wanted to try them all! 😄

My favourite dishes were Crispy Shrimp Rolls, Pan Fried Chinese Chives Dumplings, Glutinous Rice with Chicken and Wolfberry Cake. 😋

I loved about their great ambiance with spacious interior, high ceiling and lots of natural lights. The open air seating was welcoming, the restaurant was well ventilated with multiple fans around.
I will return for my dim sum fix when I visit Ipoh next time~ 🙂

author: Arrieana Tolentino
review_text: The place is spacious and the service was quite good but it could be better. On the other hand the food was not worth the price and the size of the dim sum all was small and it is expensive,but the beef ramen was quite good and also I hope they make some changes to their food because i think place like that people with expect more from it. From what I can say my experience it was not worth it

author: Kenneth Khoo
review_text:
We travelled from Taiping to Ipoh with high hopes of enjoying some delicious dim sum, but our experience was just average overall.

The **Siu Mai** didn’t quite meet our expectations; it lacked the depth of flavours we were hoping for. On the other hand, the **Har Gao** was decent, with a nice balance of shrimp filling and thin, delicate wrappers.

One highlight was the **egg tarts**, which were delightful with their flaky crust and creamy custard filling. The **BBQ pastries** were also commendable, offering a pleasant blend of savoury flavours. However, many of the other dishes fell into the standard category, lacking the wow factor that often accompanies dim sum.

The service at the restaurant was commendable. The staff was attentive, frequently topping up our tea and promptly serving and clearing our table, which added to the overall experience.

The ambience of the place was quite charming, reminiscent of a traditional tea house, providing a nice backdrop for our meal. Interestingly, while we had heard that this spot is usually bustling with diners, it was relatively quiet during our visit, with only a few tables occupied.

In summary, while there were some enjoyable dishes, the overall standard of the dim sum did not live up to the hype. It’s worth a visit for the egg tarts and BBQ pastries, but don’t expect an extraordinary dim sum experience.

author: Cher Ong
review_text: Huge dim sum place with double storey seating capacity. U can dine comfortably as it's very spacious. Service isn't on par. Those aunties are chit chatting & eating when they're on duty. This is a bad impression for customers. They're not as crowded & popular as last time. I used to quite like this place but after this round not anymore. The dim sum is not fresh. Bad quality control. Taste also below average & price is high. Cashier has no basic manner as well.

author: Houston Loh
review_text:
I bought the multigrain sourdough walnut & cranberry bread and the apple pies. The prices are a bit on the high side, but the bread is tasty, healthy and generously filled with walnuts and cranberries. The apple pies are my personal favorite, the filling isn’t too sweet, which I really like and you can taste the delicious diced apples. The only disappointment was that the pie wasn’t served hot enough.

Overall, I enjoyed everything and will definitely try other breads and pies in the future.

author: Karina Adianto
review_text:
This bakery looked like it was an old establishment which survived and stayed strong for a long time.

For our surprise, they had many varieties of breads with unusual flavors. We were intrigued to try everything but unfortunately, we were in Penang for a short time, so we didn't get the chance to come back to try their other freshly made breads.

We bought:
Graham cheese bun - whomemeal flour soft bread with generous cream cheese filling.
Custard choux - thick yellow custard (consists lots of eggs), slight salty crusty choux. Complemented each other well.
Kiwi muffin - with poppy seeds, slight tanginess, not too sweet, moist.

Definitely will be back to try their sweet corn cheese twist & lemon tart. Eyeing on those when we visited last time 😆🤭

author: WaterMelon Foodie&Traveller
review_text: A local friend brought me here 10 years ago, and I finally came back for a second visit. Saw some reviews saying the cinnamon roll is a must-try, so I gave it a shot — and it was really good! The curry puff and walnut sourdough were great too, definitely worth trying! Plus, there is a huge foodcourt just 5 minutes walking distance… where u can try the chendol too.

author: Kee Kelven
review_text: It was my first time visiting this bakery, and it quickly became one of my favorites. The bakery has an old-school look and is filled with the amazing smell of fresh bread and pastries. They serve all kinds of baked goods, including sourdough, muffins, cinnamon rolls, tarts, and croissants. My personal favorite is the cinnamon rolls, which are really soft and rich in cinnamon flavor and sweetness. The bakery is always crowded, and everyone has to pick their bread quickly before it sells out after the staff puts it on the racks.

author: John Chong
review_text:
Old School Bakery.

I found this place on google map and the reviews looked good.

So I went down to pick up a few buns and a loaf of bread.

The bread and pastries were surprisingly fresh and good and very reasonable.

I loved the curry puff, chicken pie and Egg Tarts.

I bought a loaf of Sliced Multi-Grain Bread.  It was fresh and soft even after 3 days.

My only regret was not buy more stuff !!!

author: Teh Xin Yu
review_text: Old school bakery which is around for more than 20 years in Penang. You definitely feel like walking through the time tunnel once you entered the shop. You are first welcome with the fragrant wheat smell as the bread was baked freshly in the shop. There are varieties of choices for bread, pastries, muffins and they also have sourdough now! All the items look tasty and fresh. Some of the items was cheap while some are slightly expensive. For example, their sourdough bread are less than RM10 but some of the basic bun such as coconut bun are RM 4. My parents personally feel the coconut bun are a bit underwhelming as the bun might look big but the coconut filling was actually not many, it is not filled up in the middle of bun. Instead, you can see clearly in the picture the darker green colour was the shredded coconut filling while the lighter green part is the bread. The coconut filling is one small circle in the bun. Will probably revisit to try their other items such as baked pastries, sourdough bread and wholemeal bun but definitely not this coconut bun. Also, the architecture of the shop is interesting as the shop owner did not change much of the shop exterior and interior structure, the building has the British colonial era vibe. It is super hard to get a parking there, it is easier to park inside nearby New World Park paid parking lot, and walk to this shop which is only 3 minutes walking distance away.

author: John D'Cruz (Kajangfood)
review_text: A bakery that I have been patronising for over 20 years. I used to make it a point to pick up bread and buns when I’m in Penang to take back to KL. It’s certainly good quality and value for money compared to KL prices. Recommended to visit if you’re in the area.

author: ZS Lee
review_text:
The best cream puff, banana pie & chicken curry puff I have ever had 🥹😭
Penang’s pride !!!!
Highly recommended !!!

author: Mary Liew
review_text:
The taste of apricot bread is ok, not bad. BUT then while I was chewing the bread, I found a strand of hair attached to the bread!
You can see the hair is holding the pieces of bread I chewed halfway. Quality and hygiene control is very bad! I went outside for better lighting to see the strand of hair and the hair colour and length wasn’t even mine. Feel so disgusted already 😣

author: Lim EV
review_text:
Greeted by whiffs of freshly baked bread and pastries… delightful as we were lost for choices what to buy. Obviously forgot to take photos of all the goodies we bought but I will list them down.

6 cream puff - delightful light cream and decadently sinful

4 egg tarts - bigger than my palm

1 butter raisin bun - thick gluten sins

1 butter purple potato bun - a bit healthier but that is just me justifying my purchase

1 sourdough cranberry loaf - oh so good

1 English muffins - received nod of approval from wife and everyone that was in the bakery

1 cheese corn bread - daughter ate it quietly no sharing

Total damage 80.10.

Well worth it as it accompanied us from Penang back home, and we had them for breakfast till 2 days after.

author: JW
review_text:
Best place to buy fresh bakery in Penang.

Traditional type of bakery.

Affordable and many choice.

author: Mitchell Lim
review_text: Old school bakery been around for eons. Their bread/buns have quite a bite (not eating air). Prices have gone up a fair bit in recent years. Taste, nostalgia..

author: Ronnie Chew
review_text: This bakery sells delicious breads. All types of breads. I've tried quite a variety and it's pretty good. My favourite is dates and walnuts. The apricot bread however is quite rough and dry. I don't like it that much. Walnuts and dates to be should be the best. My personal opinion 🤗 Don't go during opening time at 10am. There's so many people waiting to go in, it's quite ridiculous. I saw that crowd last week thinking I'll buy my favourite bread but I kept going. I'm not crowding with them. Go around 10.30. It may not be as crowded. Your favourite breads would not be ready if you go too early though so be warned. Call first to check availablity.

author: Wong Jennifer
review_text: Freshly made and no preservatives breads. Personally , I Like the English breakfast muffin and graham cheese bread the most.

author: Moon Kum Weng
review_text: Am regular customer who frequently buy breads from Continental. They have a wide range of loaf breads, muffins, sourdough, corn bread, banana bread, egg tart, cinnamon rolls, white bread, raisin breads, etc. Enough variety for the young and old. Both healthy and not so healthy. Owing to the huge sales daily the prices are very competitive. Thus, this bakery is very popular with people who consume breads regularly. Parking is an issue around the shop. Most customers will just stop outside, quickly run in & pick the breads, pay and drive off.

author: Sern Teh
review_text:
Love the banana bread, not too sweet like supermarket sold.
Fri-Sunday have only.🫢

author: Khoo Jolyn
review_text:
Is a well established bakery. Has been around for many year. Has so many varieties of breads, buns, puff pastry, pies, kaya.
Quality of bread is good and do not skim on ingredients. Prices are much cheaper than many other bakeries in town.
Open from 10 am to 5 pm. Best time to grab your choices of bread is before lunch time, or else some popular ones will be sold out.

author: KC Ee
review_text: one of the worst bakery today, weird wholemeal breads only, no normal buns like kaya tuna sambal kari etc

author: Yeoh Yuan Ya
review_text: The staff there had a very poor attitude. When I called to ask about placing an order for pick-up the next day, their reaction was as if I owed them a million dollars. Very very bad experience and when i go and take my order wah their reaction was so bad and so blur do not know what to do. Overall i did not recommend anyone come to this bakery and suggest everyone not to come. You come and buy their bad attitude with money

author: Roonie W
review_text: This place is awesome. Selling alot of veriety of bread. The only problem is that space of parking. You have to find a place to park. Unless there are persons in the car to wait. Very limited car park. The bread is very nice soft and fresh. If you are a bread lover

author: Caleb Lim
review_text: My first Ipoh chicken and beansprout meal and I loved it! Nicely cooked bean sprouts, tender chicken with some bite and the curry horfun I ordered has some oomph! The chilli sauce is also well balanced. I also ordered a 2nd bowl of soup horfun to enjoy the chicken soup. I chose outdoor seating for better ventilation.

author: Abby Y
review_text:
There are 2 ong kee restaurant almost opposite each other and we went to one of them. Spacious interior. Menu wasn't fancy but has the staple.
Hor fun was silky smooth. Tauge were juicy, crunchy. Chicken was excellent, well seasoned with fragrant sesame oil/soy sauce. Not super meaty, which I prefer. Curry chicken was different to the usual, and a meh.

author: Nothing Impossible
review_text: We went to the Oon Kee without air-cond. There were two shops with the same name. Smooth steamed chicken, with enough flavour. But lacking sesame oil taste. And they didn't provide ginger sauce as condiment. The chili sauce was spicy and love the taste. The plump, short taugeh was crunchy and flavoured with sesame oil, soy sauce and black pepper. Love it. The flavour of the rice was tasty., just too soft.

author: matt matt
review_text: I visited Ong Kee Restaurant and ordered half a chicken. The meat was tender and smooth, paired with a distinctive sauce that leaned slightly salty. The stir-fried bean sprouts were perfectly balanced — crisp yet not undercooked — and very flavorful. The oil rice carried a fragrant aroma, complementing the meal well. The flat rice noodle soup was another highlight, with silky noodles and a clean, naturally sweet broth. Overall, Ong Kee delivered a thoroughly satisfying dining experience.

author: Boonwei Koh
review_text: Decent chicken and the bean sprouts goes well with the rice. Chilli is also nice with a sweet taste. Pricing on the high side, food is served very fast.

author: Min Kuan
review_text: The service was horrible. They're in a hurry of getting you to order food and drink. The servers didn't give me a feeling that they appreciated my business. (My local friend told me local people actually don't eat Hainese chicken here.) There nothing too special about their Hainanese chicken. It's just free range chicken. Their chili sauce dip was very bland. Any Hainanese chicken place in Penang will win hands down. As for their beansprouts... they're just fatter than regular beansprouts. There's nothing so special about them.

author: DR. ALVIN TUNG
review_text: The classic Ipoh dinner! Bean Sprout chicken, Tauge Ayam, 芽菜雞! Always the Comfort food! Our meal was perfect in every way. The bean sprouts were plump and crisp the chicken was flavorful and silky and the noodles were smooth as silk. Accompanying the main characters were fish balls, fresh and al dente and flavorful fresh pork meatballs. Even the humble soya sauce for the chicken and the bean sprouts is flavorful and Rich a light and satisfying dinner always! The staff here are very friendly and attentive. This was a perfect dining experience!

author: Hao Tan
review_text: A shorter queue comparing with the other famous chicken ric shop opposite.  Chicken was tender and bean spout was crispy and sauce wasn't too salty.  We enjoyed

author: Alicia Johnson
review_text: Food was Nice and delicious, service was okay just Nice But not worth the price. Was way too expensive and the quantity of Food is very less. Can eat for once on ur own tidak as its too expensive for a chicken rice . The amount of rice and chicken we received for two people is so so less But the price is was too much . I literally paid RM 41 for two people.. once again not worth the price. And yes definitely i am not coming back.

author: Banuaji P
review_text: Nice chicken and beans prout. The chiken is soft and flavourful. The fish meatball also good. You must try it.

author: Ling Sg
review_text:
If you’ve read the reviews beforehand and still decide to go, don’t expect a clean environment or good service. This was my second visit, and whether it's here or at Lou Wang, the experience remains the same. It seems to be part of their style, or maybe their business is thriving enough that service isn't a priority.

While the restaurant (it's a coffeeshop) may not offer the best ambience, the chicken and beansprouts are iconic dishes in Ipoh that are still worth trying. I’d bring friends here, especially since it's convenient for us as we stayed nearby. The steamed rice and hor fun are good to go with chicken and bean sprouts.
To avoid the crowds and chaos (including staff shouting), try to visit early. It could be challenging, especially on a rainy day, as space is limited and ground is wet. Travel light—there’s not much room for shopping bags, and you wouldn't want to leave them on the floor given the condition of it.

author: eee che
review_text:
Touristy spot for its iconic Bean Sprout and Chicken Rice.

My Ipoh friend recommended here instead of the opposite side Old Wong chicken rice for it’s chicken rice. Trust the locals taste buds.

Chicken: these are local breed chicken instead of industrial chicken. Industrial chicken are meaty but lack firmness and tender. The chicken here are silky and smooth 👍 even the breast meat are tender.

Bean Sprouts: Fat bean sprouts give the crunchy bite and you don’t feel the raw bean sprout taste.

Fish ball soup: the fish ball are freshly hand made mackerel pike fish. No fishy taste 👅

Rice is cooked with chicken broth plus pandan leaves. Without the garlic taste as eating in Singapore. Rather go with the hor fun. Chilli sauce for the chicken rice is sweet and little spicy. You noticed there are chilli padi provided on the side. A bit pricey for locals but quality wise is worth it. 😊

author: tan SH
review_text: I like the bean spouts than their chicken, ithey tops all with pepper, so all have a peppery taste. I think they have better quality chicken than those normal chicken rice stall, when meat is not soft type, closer to kampong chickens.  Locate in tourist streets, i think local seldom eat here.

author: Winston Chuah
review_text: The food at Onn Kee Restaurant is quite good, especially the bean sprout chicken, which is flavorful and tender. The bean sprouts are fresh and crunchy, making for a great combination. However, the place can get really crowded, and service tends to be a bit slow during peak hours. The prices are slightly on the higher side for the portion sizes. Overall, it’s a decent spot for authentic Ipoh chicken rice, but there’s room for improvement in service and efficiency.

author: daezjn
review_text:
Visited on a Wednesday at 6 PM- quiet at the time, but highly recommended by family and friends. The food is reasonably priced and delicious! Their signature Ipoh-style short and thick bean sprouts are fresh, crunchy, and lightly stir-fried. The pork balls are bouncy, and the white chicken is well-seasoned with pepper and served with a tasty sauce. But for me, the real highlight was the noodles- delicate, smooth, handmade, and light. Skip the rice and go for the noodles!

Drink options include leong sui, iced Chinese tea, etc., though unfortunately, they serve drinks in disposable plastic cups instead of glass- would love to see less plastic waste. Service is brisk and efficient, and the restaurant has that classic old-school Chinese eatery vibe- no frills, no air conditioning, but well-ventilated with strong fans.

The decor is effortlessly nostalgic, with eclectic pictures, paintings, a Chinese calendar, and a traditional praying altar. The bright green walls, uniforms, and colorful tableware add to the charm. It’s also impressively clean for this style of restaurant- no slippery floors or greasy kitchen surfaces. Plus, the back kitchen even has a view of some back alley wall art! Definitely coming back.

author: Thomas Tam
review_text: Hard to go wrong with chicken rice in Ipoh I think. Also tried Lou Wong across the road and found the chicken here slightly more tender, particularly the breast meat. Rice flavour was a bit better too, though slightly soggy in texture. The beansprouts here aren’t quite as al dente as I’d like. Overall very nice and feels a little less touristy and possibly more authentic than the competition across the road.

author: KL Cheong
review_text: Very disappointed with this chicken rice shop. The staff were rude and unfriendly, which made the whole experience unpleasant. The chicken had a strange smell and didn’t taste fresh at all. On top of that, they only accept cash, which is very inconvenient. The soup and portion size were really not worth the price I paid. Definitely not coming back. Would not recommend!

author: Devina R
review_text:
BEST AYAM TAUGE RESTAURANT.
The texture of the chicken is nice. The sauce of the steamed chicken and the beansprouts are just right for us.
This is one of the rare times when chicken is better than the pork. Char siew is my order.
Once you've eaten tauge in Ipoh, you can't go back. No tauge will top Ipoh tauge that's for sure. Eating tauge will never be the same. The crunchiest and the fattest tauge ever.

author: Richard Cheah
review_text:
A Disappointing Experience at Onn Kee Chicken Rice.

I'm usually not one to write negative reviews, but my recent experience at Onn Kee Chicken Rice was a letdown, to say the least. My family visited this popular eatery, expecting a delicious and satisfying meal. Unfortunately, our expectations were not met.

We ordered the 3-portion chicken for the three of us, but the servings were surprisingly small. There was hardly any meat on the bone, and we were left feeling unsatisfied. For a chicken rice stall, you'd expect the chicken to be the star of the show, but sadly, it was a letdown.

The oil rice was another disappointment. It was plain and felt like eating glue. The rice stuck together in clumps, making it unappetizing to eat. I've had better oil rice at other stalls, and this was a far cry from the delicious, fluffy rice I'm used to.

The chilli sauce was also a letdown. It was diluted and lacked the spicy kick I'm used to. For a stall that's supposed to the specialty of Ipoh well known and specialize in chicken rice, you'd expect the chilli sauce to be a highlight, but unfortunately, it was a disappointment.

To be honest, I've had better chicken rice in Singapore, and I wouldn't recommend Onn Kee to anyone looking for a delicious and satisfying meal. Unless they seriously revamp their recipe and improve their service, I'd advise eating at Onn Kee at your own risk.

Honestly, hiring foreigners has affected the image. To make matters worse, living in its yester years of past glory, sooner and not later, you will see the name become a past history.

Rating: 2/5 stars

Will I return? Unlikely.

author: Kayden Kong
review_text: The service was very bad...cannot ask question at all...they will keep on rushing you to order...all worker attitude was very bad👎🏻...the chinese worker here most terrible...seems like we come here to eat no need to pay...the food is ok only🤮...very bad experience👎🏻...will not come again！！！

author: Sheue Lin Ng
review_text: I love the soya sauce based hor fun (order dry instead of soup). The texture of the noodles were soft and it absorbed the taste very well. Next, the pork ball was delicious too. The bean sprouts were crunchy and tasted sweet. The chicken was delicious but I think the person did not know how to chop the chicken nicely. The angle and the shape doesn't confirm to the normal on how chicken should be chopped! The chicken feet cold dish was ok only. Will skip this for sure!!

author: J Fong
review_text:
We have been a few times and it is one of our go to places for Ipoh chicken & bean sprouts. Here are some points bout this place and my dining experience:
- Seats & tables are by the roadside or in the restaurant though limited tables. There is no air conditioning in the restaurant. For a more airy seating, the outdoor seating is better.
- They have retractable awnings which will provide a level of protection if there is rain.
- Order is placed with staff who will approach to take your order. It is stock standard service as you would expect.
- Payment is by cash or e-payment.
- Chicken is of firm texture. The sauce was a bit on the oily side. Flavour wise was pretty alright.
- Bean sprouts too were a bit on the oily side. Flavour and texture wise was pretty good.
- Sometimes there may be street vendors who approach diners selling their wares.

I would come back but probably may need to tell them to cut down on the oil.

author: Sofia
review_text:
Food taste is not bad but given the prices and the fact that they gave me all bones, I do not recommend. Leftover cut up chicken wings, only 4 pieces of meat. I left it and the waiter asked me if I want to take away, I said no need. He asked if it was not to my liking? I responded with that they gave me all bones which he looked and saw. The cashier came over and also looked and saw that it was all bones but no one did anything to fix the situation. I paid 23 Ringits for 4 pieces of chicken and a cup of chrysanthemum tea plus a few bites of bean sprouts, ridiculous. Chicken also was not necessarily tender just decent flavor.

Save yourself, overhyped place. There is definitely better chicken bean sprouts out there!

author: Y SW
review_text:
Succulent chicken that cooked to perfection and paired with nice soy based sauce to give it a rich umami saltiness.

The rice is fragrant and fluffy albeit of the drier style instead of the oilier types common with chicken rice.

Both the dry and soup based hor fun(rice noodles) are nicely done. Order based on your preference, the dry version is heavier in taste.

The soy bean sprouts are plump and crunchy and is slightly undercooked giving it a taste similar to salad. This might be a bit of an acquired taste for those not used to it.

Take note there is actually a queue system and it is not free seating. This is slightly confusing as there are minimal signage to highlight this.

author: Vanessa Tan
review_text: Located in a central area popular with tourists. I visited around 6:30 pm and only waited about five minutes in line. As it was my first dine in visit, I wasn’t familiar with the menu, but the lady taking our order seemed quite busy and rushed, there wasn’t much time to look through it properly, I just made a quick choice and skipped the side dish. The chicken was smooth and tender, and the accompanying soy sauce had a unique, delicious flavor. Overall, I enjoyed the chicken rice, just wish service had been a little better.

author: YippieYaYa
review_text:
Visited Lou Wong during my trip to Ipoh and tried their famous bean sprout chicken. The steamed chicken was tender and paired well with the crunchy bean sprouts and smooth hor fun. Service was fast despite the crowd, and the atmosphere felt lively and traditional.

However, it was quite hot and crowded inside, and the food, while good, felt a bit overrated compared to other local spots.

Still, it's worth a visit if you want to experience one of Ipoh’s iconic eateries.

author: Frank Wan
review_text:
