The is a well known chicken rice cafe in Ipoh.  The cafe has no air conditioning and most of the tables are placed on the street (actually at the side of the road).  So, if you are looking for a nice place to dine, this cafe may not suit you.  Because of its name, it is quite busy even on weekdays.  The dinner session starts at 6:00 pm and close when the foods are sold out.  The staff are extremely efficient.  Foods are normally sold out at 7:30 to 8:00 pm.  Please be there at 6:00 pm if you want to try most of their signature dishes.

The foods are not bad but I found it a bit salty.  I also that the chickens are not free range chickens and hence the “taste of chicken” is rather light!  The bean sprouts are good though!

author: Anthony Boyle
review_text:
A very ordinary restaurant, I’d never go back.

I was alone so found a table easily. Server came over and threw a menu on the table. Then came back and asked what I wanted to drink. I said Beer, but they don’t sell beer, so I oped for a hot Chinese tea. The tea came out, lukewarm, in a plastic cup, with a plastic straw! Horrible.

The menu wasn’t big (despite the size of the restaurant) so I just ordered the Single Chicken and rice. He wanted to sell me beansprouts but I didn’t want any.  Food came out quickly and the chicken was cold….not just warm, but cold. Thankfully the rice was hot which made the meal edible.    The chicken tasted ok but half of it was just fat and bones.

Lots of people there, obviously tourists like me. A local would never go there, certainly not twice. I won’t go back either.

author: Chia Hau Lee
review_text:
Visited the iconic Restaurant Tauge Ayam Lou Wong — a place I felt I had to experience at least once, even though its rating has dropped to 3.6 stars from over 6.5k reviews. It’s clearly a tourist spot, but also a good benchmark to taste the “standard” version of Ipoh tauge ayam, knowing many reviews say there are better options elsewhere.

I found the prices reasonable: a 2-person portion of chicken was RM25, tauge for 2 was RM7, and the 5-meatball soup was RM5. Service was fast, and they accept e-payment, which is convenient.

Taste-wise, nothing particularly special for us, especially since we’ve had better chicken rice back in Singapore. But as mentioned, it’s worth coming once just to experience this iconic spot and see what the hype is about.

author: Ramesh Vadiveloo
review_text:
Just had lunch at Restoran Tauge Ayam Lou Wong, and it truly lived up to its reputation.

We ordered the steamed chicken, bean sprouts, and gizzard—simple dishes, but done exceptionally well.

The chicken was tender and juicy, the bean sprouts perfectly crunchy, and the gizzard surprisingly flavourful. What really tied everything together was their signature chilli dip and soya sauce—so addictive that it lifted every bite.

A satisfying, classic Ipoh meal. Would definitely come back!

author: M
review_text: Food was good. Had the beansprouts, tofu, fishball soup, rice. All around good food. Atmosphere is great as well - felt grounded and authentic. Service is good - fast and efficient. Really enjoyed the meal here before a stroll at the nearby nightmarket

author: Leong Wilbert
review_text: Had the chicken which wasnt too tender type, and also the ipoh horfun. The horfun was silky and smooth but the soup might be just a little too salty. Chicken feet was good. A good to try if you are in the area.

author: Felix C
review_text:
Overrated.
Need to call the waiter a few times when ordering and pay bills.
If you like smooth chicken then it's not to your taste. Hor fun is average taste.
You can get better chicken and Hor fun else where.

author: shan xie
review_text: A mediocre restaurant, every dish using the same sauce, taste nothing more than soy sauce. The portion is small, their chicken also  taste less.

author: BT L
review_text: My friend from mainland China wanted to try the Ipoh famous bean sprout chicken. Everything was good and my friends enjoyed it so much. Bean sprout is good and fresh but I think it’s little too much chicken fat. The ho fun in Ipoh is always good.

author: Jay
review_text: Went before 9pm, and was glad to be served the last available plate of chicken meat. Great taste, always crowded, food was served very quickly. Went on a chilly night, hence was not too bothered by outdoor/indoor seating, had to share a table as all tables were occupied during dinner time.

author: Sharon
review_text:
3.5 ⭐ for this landmark Ipoh Hor Fun.
Hor fun is silky smooth with slightly sweet soup.
However, chicken was slightly tough and a tad dry.
Beans sprouts crunchy and juicy. Overall, a very salty meal.

author: Helen Tan
review_text: On this busy food street, you can find many restaurants and local snack stores. What is popular here is their sesame steamed chicken, juicy fat beansprouts and the smooth silky horfun that slides down your throat or the fragrant slightly yellow colored chicken rice. Another tasty side dish is the mixed fishball and meatball soup. Next time, we will try the Tuck Kee Restaurant.

author: Chan Sheng
review_text: It's noisy, it's messy, service level is a bare minimum and it's hot during lunchtime. But the food is pretty fantastic overall to overcome these issues. The speciality Ipoh beansprouts are plump, sweet and juicy. Never had this kind of beansprouts anywhere else and it's certainly unforgettable. The chicken is also very well made.

author: Chun Hou
review_text: Might be well known but food is below average. The chicken is unseasoned and tough, and the sauce is way too salty to make up for the bland chicken. Service is fast and efficient, food was served up within 5min.

author: Chia Hau Lee
review_text:
Tried Ipoh Tuck Kee and the food definitely lived up to its reputation. The Moonlight Hor Fun was full of wok hei — fragrant, tasty, and truly addictive. We also ordered the fried bee hoon mixed with hor fun, which had a unique combination of crispy and wet textures. Every bite had a satisfying crackling sound in the mouth, which made it really enjoyable.

The baby squid came with a delicious and addictive chilli sauce, while the chicken feet, although nicely marinated, were a little too small.

author: Leonard Chong
review_text:
Dinner dated 13 Dec 2025.
Taste of hor fun was not the same, compared to what I had 2 years ago. Chill helped to elevate the taste slightly.
It was my fault to order the miserable 2 x small fried spring rolls. Served hot but it was kids serving.
No doubt hor fun was smooth, but it was another eaten and could be forgotten dish for me. Very sad.

author: Zen Yong
review_text:
Visited Ipoh Tuck Kee Restaurant during dinner time, and it was easy to understand why this place is always packed with customers. Despite arriving around 5:45pm, the restaurant was already full, and a queue had formed outside. Luckily, the waiting time wasn’t too long as the staff manage the crowd efficiently.

The staff here are friendly, attentive, and extremely fast. They move with purpose, clearing tables quickly, taking orders proactively, and ensuring customers are seated as soon as possible. Even with the high customer volume, they remain polite and alert, which makes the whole experience smooth and pleasant.

The environment is typical of a popular local eatery — crowded, lively, and full of energy. Even though it gets busy, it remains comfortable and organized. Tables are fairly close to each other, but the quick turnover ensures that the place doesn’t feel stuffy.

In terms of price, it’s reasonable for the portion sizes and the quality of food served. The food portion matches the pricing well, with ingredients that feel fresh and dishes that are cooked with consistency.

Now, onto the highlight — the braised chicken leg. This dish is truly outstanding and highly recommended. The chicken leg is tender, juicy, and packed with flavour. The braising sauce is rich and savory, absorbing beautifully into the meat. It’s one of those dishes that instantly stands out and becomes a must-order for future visits. The other dishes we tried were also good, maintaining the flavorful and satisfying taste that Tuck Kee is known for.

Overall, Ipoh Tuck Kee Restaurant lives up to its reputation as one of Ipoh’s top spots for delicious local dishes. The long queue might seem intimidating, but with the fast service and efficient turnover, the wait is very manageable. If you’re visiting Ipoh and looking for a dinner place that balances taste, value, and local charm, Tuck Kee is definitely worth a stop.

author: YippieYaYa
review_text:
Had dinner at Restoran Tuck Kee and it definitely lived up to its reputation. The Yu Kong Hor (fried flat noodles with egg) was smooth and flavorful, and the baby octopus dish was a standout—tender, springy, and well-seasoned

The menu offers a great variety of Cantonese-style noodles and stir-fried dishes, all at reasonable prices.

The place gets very crowded, especially during weekends, so expect a queue.

Overall, a great spot for local-style noodles and a must-try if you're exploring Ipoh’s food scene.

author: Sean Sean
review_text: Old shop, that is older than most of us. It's like a tourist spot that most will visit. Nothing much to shout about, just quite normal tasting moonlight hor fun. Remember to add chilli n soya sauce cos it tends to be less than seasoned.

author: Jason Tan
review_text: The noodles are lack of "wok-hei", really missed the old style cooking. Quite disappointed with the food quality. Having said that,  the squid 🐙 is tender and delicious 😋

author: Yvonne Lean
review_text: Loved the noodles here, and the big plus is the high number of fans and cool temps in this restaurant. Opens for dinner, and service is fast and efficient. Photos to have a better idea of what to order if you’re not familiar with it.

author: Wee Guan Kho
review_text:
The food here is really good.

The moonlight hor fun is so smooth it literally slit down my throat effortlessly !

Had the cuttlefish ball soup too, which was comforting and they are huge !

Suggest to come before 6pm as the crowd starts coming in.

author: Annie Chew
review_text: The food here is satisfactory, though it may not be particularly outstanding. I find that the Tuck Kee in the KL branch offers a more appealing flavor profile in my personal opinion.

author: Celeste Lee
review_text: We accidentally walked into the wrong Tuck Kee restaurant, but luckily realized it while ordering. The baby octopus dish was really fresh and tasty, but the rest of the dishes were just so-so. Overall, it was an okay experience."

author: 00Y
review_text: The food here is decent—nothing extraordinary, but satisfying enough for a quick meal. Be prepared to order and queue before being seated, though the dishes come out surprisingly fast once you do. The biggest downside is the limited parking, so plan accordingly.

author: LEE LEE
review_text: The KL style hokkien noodle is the worst I ever tasted. No wok hey, not flavorful. (I thought they are famous for it). Total disappointment. I came all the way from Johor.

author: matt matt
review_text: Visited Restaurant Tuck Kee in Ipoh. Ordered the Yue Guang Ho (moonlight hor fun) and Wat Dan Ho (slippery egg hor fun) — the taste was just okay. The fried chicken wings were nice. Overall, the food was alright and served quickly. The place was overcrowded, mostly with tourists, but the staff were friendly.

author: Janelle
review_text: Super delicious and tender octopus with chilli peanut sauce pair with Wat Dan Hor 🥹 Fried chicken wings are just okay, it's on the sweeter side.

author: Alex Loai
review_text: Portions was big and sufficient; the 滑蛋炒粉 is definitely one of the best (even compare to Penang)!

author: Jonathan Khoo
review_text: Soy Sauce Octopus was yummy! Excellent side dish. Fried Spring Roll was good as well (No pics, sorry). Deep fried Chicken Wing was pretty normal. Yu Kong Hor is great! But the most unique was the 滑蛋鱼面. Noodles made from fishball material, looks like Udon, but so springy and coated with savoury sauce. Go early to avoid the queue. Food is served relatively fast. One of the more special Ipoh eateries we stopped by.

author: Fong Siew Poh
review_text: After few years decided came back to visit this shop again, Overall the foods makes us disappointed and feel pricey, portion so small especially the fried Kuey tiaw and chicken feet(look at the picture the chicken feet cut into half only to makes the portion looks more). The Cantonese noodles gravy too thick, makes us eat half way to stop it. It might be not the real chef to cook and pass to the worker to cook it, corn flour is putting so much into gravy become so thick(apparently portion is bigger than kuey tiaw). Braised yee mee is tasteless and a bit bitter due to black sauce too much, got to pair with their sambal belacan to finish the noodle. Prawns in noodles smelly, it might be in the packaging and workers didn’t wash it well(it’s frozen prawn). For the whole meal me and my family only enjoy the sambal and octopus, workers  serve food so so no smiling face don’t feel welcome from them. Environment is good with aircond and clean. Hopefully the boss take note on this, as an eater we give comment and hope the quality of foods maintain all times.

author: Banuaji P
review_text: Nice place to get some noodle. Dont forget to get the Octopus one. Its so good and they chop to bite size. The noodle also good too.

author: Jia Tian Ng
review_text: Tuck Kee offers classic Chinese stir-fried noodles packed with wok hei and flavour. The moonlight hor fun with raw egg is silky and rich, while the baby octopus in soy sauce is a must-try—tender and perfectly seasoned. We accidentally ordered the Wat Tan Hor, but it didn’t disappoint. A happy mistake! Service is fast and food comes out piping hot. Great for a quick, satisfying local meal.

author: Kenny Tan
review_text: Ordered delivery from grab. The fish paste noodles were amazing. I also like the fried chicken. They looked dry but tasted quite good and not that dry. The fishballs and meatballs were good too. They came in a very tasty soup. Fried shuijiao is also very good.

author: Andrew Yeoh
review_text: This is a popular tomyum noodles restaurant in Butterworth especially with the younger crowd. They have tomyum and clear broth options. Customers can choose noodles or porridge. We chose the tomyum porridge and the clear porridge. Customers can choose the ingredients they prefer. The fried fish fillet was fresh and well cooked but rather too salty. The texture of the porridge is right. Price wise, it is on the high side.

author: Wong Jennifer
review_text:
Tasty , fresh and good fried fish fillet . RM1.5/each.

Others ingredients are ok.

The tomyam soup is good , just a bit bit salty for me. If the soup less salty , it will be even perfect .

Comes with maggi mee or bihun.

Good service from the workers. Line up to take the ingredients , then pass to the workers , once place the order with mee or bihun , the worker will spot where we are going to sit.

The food will sent to our table after maybe 5-10mins depends on orders. Price is consider affordable and worth.

Drink lemongrass @ RM3. Not very strong flavour of lemongrass but ok. The price for the drinks if cheaper a bit bit will be even better.

Parking at the roadside only.

author: JJ
review_text: The tomyum soup was slightly on the salty side, and the broth could be richer and spicier in flavor.

author: PingTing Eeo
review_text:
Loved the fried fish fillets here! They are well fried and still crispy even with the soup or porridge base, and does not have fishy/stale oil taste, which is the most common issue with fried fish. The tomyam porridge is something different I’m trying for the first time. Overall I would describe it as having some home cooked comfort food.

For those who are looking for a clean, comfortable, air conditioned place, this may not be the best to dine.

author: Charm C
review_text: Too good! The fried fish is amazing its really really good. A wide variety of ingredients to choose from as well! The soup also has good flavour and is a good late night meal to have when craving something soupy 😋 A must-try!

author: Ching Ling T
review_text: Used to be my fav tomyam restaurant. However I saw cockroach on the floor. Served with precooked maggie which is kinda soggy and hope it could add glass noodles in the menu.

author: Cher Ong
review_text: 1 of the famous tomyam stalls in the mainland. Their soup base is not comparable to many others, but they have their supporters. People who like lighter taste will love their taste. Their soup is not the thick type, quite diluted, I can say. I'm here for their fried fish. Definitely the best in town. Super crispy & fresh. Ingredients available are moderate,not too fancy, but enough to choose from. Food preparation is also quick despite the crowd. They have outdoor & indoor space.

author: Ong Shu Wen
review_text: Tried a Mama Mee stall in BM that I visited a few years back — the taste is still as good as I remember, slightly on the salty side but flavourful. The food choices are limited, but the fried fish and minced pork are must-tries, especially in the tomyum Mama Mee. It’s a popular local supper spot. Pricing is average — not too cheap, not too expensive. Worth a try if you're looking for a decent supper place in BM.

author: Syalwa Febriani
review_text: I went here for their tomyam, heard that it is quite famous and good! We can choose what to be in our bowl, there are a lot that we probably won’t be able to try them all. Must try: deep fried fish, tomyam noodle (best to eat both at the same time).

author: Daniel OFFICIAL
review_text: This Tom Yum stall is highly recommended online, but for me, it’s just above AVERAGE. The price is on the higher side at RM17 per bowl. Worse still, there’s no price list, meaning the owner can charge whatever they want without a clear reference.

author: CK Tan
review_text:
One of the famous Chinese noodles restaurant in Raja Uda. It is located near the Apollo Pasar and very limited parking space. Open during the evening.
The are offering a wide variety of noddles, such as bee hoon, mee, maggi, koay teow etc. with a variety of soups such as clear soup and tomyam.
The uniqueness of most of the Chinese noodles restaurant here in Raja Uda is the wide selection of noodles toppings that they offer, from fish balls, slice pork, seafoods, vegetables, mushrooms, etc. At Ju Heng, you must try their signature fish fried.
There is always long que, but they are so efficient and able to serve your noodles within a short period of time. There are both indoor and "outside" seating available.
The price is reasonable and very affordable even if you have selected so many toppings for your "Himalayan" noodles. Normally, we end up selecting too many toppings for our small bowl of noodles.

author: Abbey Ong
review_text: Nice hot & spicy tom yam noodle. Have a good variety of ingredients to choose from. The soup is enough spicy but not too spicy to taste. Yummy~ Went on a weekday, a very short queue, totally manageable. The food is served quite fast.

author: Ooi Boon Thai
review_text: I never liked tomyam noodles before I came to this place. After I tried it here once, I happened to love tomyam noodles since then.. it was over 10 years ago, and I still like tomyam noodles.. I used to come here quite often but since the pandemic, I rarely go to Raja Uda area and is mainly at Alma area. Whenever I go to Raja Uda area, especially dinner time, this place is a choice I'll never miss..

author: Kee Kelven
review_text:
Not a big fan of their TomYam soup flavour. The tomyam taste was not really thick and rich than the other stalls in Penang. It was like added with water because they ran out of soup for me. It was kind of disappointing to me as i was not as good as i thought.
They said the fried fish fillet was the signature but still so so for me only. It was so thin and too oily taste for me even it was soaked in the soup.
We came here around 9pm and it was still a long queue waiting to order. Their ordering system was quite confusing for me, as they didn’t have any table number but only needed to told the waitress which area we were sitting.

author: Boon Leong Chong
review_text: It's been ages since I last came here for a meal. It has been a favourite of mine back in my younger years. Today I came to rekindle that old cravings. We got a bowl of their famous tomyam mee and another one in plain broth. One of the allure for me was I can select what add ons I want and how many I want. It used to feel like a sinful indulgence where one can eat to their heart's content. I went for their fried fish fillets and a mix of other little items. The tomyam soup tasted sweet with a good tang. A very appetising recipe especially if you have a heavier palate or you're looking for a flavorful meal say after a couple of drinks. Tomyam purist will probably fight you and argue that this is not what a tomyam soup should taste like and I can't exactly disagree with them. The version here lacked that lemongrass punch and that sourish depth. My experience this time around wasn't as exciting as I'd hoped for. The taste still remain faithful but I find the soup to be too sweet for my liking now. Instead, I would very much opt for the clear broth for my next visit. The deep fried fish fillet were okay. They come in sizeable chunks and you're lucky if you get the freshly fried crispy batch. Mine however was not and so it turned out to be tough. Nothing much to comment about the other options of items as they're quite standard. Overall I wouldn't say that this is a fantastic tomyam mee but instead, a bowl of comfort food be it on a rainy day or for late night cravings.

author: Marcus Lim
review_text:
My favourite place for supper at Butterworth. This restaurant is well known for their tom yum noodles and among their many choices od add-ons.. make sure to grab some of their fried fish, you just really cannot miss it because you basically have not tried this restaurant unless you had some of their fried fish.

As for choice of noodles personally i will recommend maggie mee (thats what most people order as well) 😏

author: G A
review_text: The tomyam taste so normal and basic. 2 girls also wasnt very friendly when serving, I dont know why they look so unhappy the moment they saw me. Won't be going back.

author: Yuan P Chuah
review_text: The Tomyam soup was delicious especially their fried fish, please try the fried fish when you are eating at there. The service was fast after I had picked and ordered my food the food was served within 5 minutes.

author: Nick Khor
review_text: Quality of tomyam is getting worse, last time the taste still acceptable. The ingredients should be cooked longer time/cut to half for even heat up, this is the basic cooking skill chef should master it.

author: Allen Tang
review_text: My favourite tom yum porridge, as if Tom yum flavored porridge is common but it is not. Most people would go for noodles instead but to me, tomyum porridge offers the wow factor. Must order items are fried dory fish and tom yum porridge, they are comfort food, especially during rainy days. Lots of items to be added on, just pick yourself such as meat balls, meat slice, vegetables, most steamboat items are available to choose. A few noodle options are available.

author: Eric Foo
review_text: Pretty good Ramly burger place. They also have premium beef patty burgers and fried chicken sandwiches. Like typical Ramly burgers, it is drowned in sauce, but the coleslaw makes a nice difference from others.

author: Kesiga Morgan
review_text:
We bought Pattaya chicken burger special last night. We were totally fine and healthy before our meal but after our meal, we’re now ended at hospital for diarrhoea and vomit due to food poisoning.

Actually not only us, there are also few reviews posted regarding the food poisoning since past few months.

The reason why I’m posting this is to alert the owner. I’m not blaming or wanna ruin the business, but I thought the owner should know so you can check your ingredients, food storage, and cleanliness - something went wrong.

Please make sure that this doesn’t repeat to any other customers.

Thanks.

author: MiLaa
review_text: We tried burger ayam pattaya and burger ayam combo today. The taste was good but I would not say it was excellent. Their coleslaw is bland and too watery.  The reason why I'm giving 4 stars instead of 5 star is, at the end of finishing the burger we do have the slight puke feeling because the burger was too soggy. Otherwise it is a decent roadside burger. Price wise I'm not sure if it is reasonable because it cost us RM29 for burger ayam combo with burger pattaya.

author: Sarah Lee
review_text:
A famous burger stall located in Sg Dua which served homemade patty burger and Ramly burger.

The Ramly burger here was pretty standard- nothing much to shout about and was rather messy to eat around as it was doused with sauce.

A better option would be the grilled beef burger which was flavourful and peppery. The burger is huge and comes with a 150gm patty. The beef patty was slightly overcooked but paired well with the sauce.

Heard that queue can be quite long during peak dinner hours.

author: Faruq Mokhtar
review_text:
Surely one of my favourite burger stalls in Penang. I wouldn’t say it’s the best burger in terms of taste, but it’s delicious nonetheless.

The most important part is that it’s reliable and the taste is always consistent. Definitely my go to burger all the time.

author: Henry Tan (Xuan)
review_text:
It’s my go to place for Ramli burger whenever I feel want to have one. 1 thing special about their burger is they will give coleslaw instead of cabbage.

And I found 1 thing nice for people that want slightly lesser carbo 😂 you can ask them not to put bread, or there is another option which is burger cincang, they will put slices of burger meat, hot dog and egg, then top with coleslaw’ and some veges, plus cheese and sauce on top 😍

Nice burger stall to go 👍🏻

Btw it’s a roadside stall so no place to dine in.

author: Justin Vaughn
review_text: I am only traveling here a few days so I had this two days ago and this is a MUST try. Great burger for very fair price. The flavor is so good! Im going back tonight even though I just went two days ago.

author: Desmond Boon
review_text: Not worth the wait.. so overrated and the way they handle burger and squeezing almost whole bottle of cheese is just crazy.

author: Jerem Chang
review_text: There's usually a long queue here, but it's worth the wait. My personal favorite is their grilled beef burger.

author: Daniel Ooi
review_text:
This shop provide call order.... But if having few order in 1 call, u have to call 1 by 1.
The owner/seller will end the call once 1st burger was done, then u will need to call again.
They actually end call very suddenly.... Without saying bye or anything else, they won't asking that's all.....
Food is good, but service like really poorr..... I know they having a superb sale, but they seems like not actually appreciate customer..... That's what i feel.... Kinda sad

author: AMRI SYUKRI
review_text: I order 1 with vegetables and 1 without. After this i got 2 without vegetables. Long to wait my burger although i already order 20 minutes from Whatsapp and still wait some more minutes.

author: edmund goh
review_text:
It may not look like much but the taste is good. Its a regular Ramly butger which should look messy and taste great.
Taste better than the plain burgers served by big M..
Burger special recommended.

author: Arkib Ilmu
review_text:
Taste wise its average. The queue time is super long.

But to be honest it's a gamble to eat here. Sometimes it's okay, sometimes you will get bonus diarrhea the next morning after eating the burgers because all the dust and dirt from the road gets mixed into the food.

Would recommend eating elsewhere for better and cleaner foods.

Service isn't the best either. Customer service quality is out of the window with occasional rudeness towards customers. Probably became like this because they have too many customers now and won't mind losing 1.

author: Funny George
review_text: Very bad attitude, I didn't know that customers pay after the burgers are done over here. So, I directly scanned QR Duit Now and paid the money after making orders then they are very unhappy and didn't even said 'thank you'. What's wrong with I paid first? Am I wrong?

author: eleq
review_text: love the fried cken burger .. have to wait quite some time for the order to be done

author: Law Yin Zhi
review_text: Best burger I have eaten in Penang. Came back for it again!

author: CP Goh
review_text: Expect to wait for 20 minutes plus at least ... do recommend to order it in advance via call to avoid unnecessary waiting ...

author: Khye “Joshua” Khoo
review_text: This is one of the best street burger stall that can compete with Big Names, their burgers is nicely cooked, well-seasoned and price is very affordable! Always long queue and orders is plenty. Expect to wait >30mins if long queue, but I think the waiting is worth it for their burgers.

author: elcoco enjaco
review_text: We ordered one beef burger special and two chicken burger specials.  They were both delicious and IMHO the best I've had in Penang. We didn't have to wait long even though they were quite busy. This was due to their well thought out system. I couldn't believe how reasonably priced their menu is.

author: Hao Yan
review_text:
Food was nice but the staff was rude.

Im just asked twice “berapa ringgit?”, the staff speak very quickly and impatient tone then said again “aku sudah ckp dua kali dah”, I just heard “brahbrah setangah”

Hey bro, I already speaking Malay nicely with you hang ni beri aku sikap ini!?? If I already knew the price I won’t asked the amount again for double confirm..

author: Pablo Marisol
review_text: Quite a number of choices around the hawker centre. Overall the food is moderate, but still okay for a quick meal. The fried rice was not bad and probably the better dish among what we tried. A decent stop if you want variety, though nothing particularly standout.

author: Ryan K
review_text:
I’ve been eating at here specifically Joyce Pan Mee stall since my primary school days back in 2017, and now as a university student close to graduating, this place still hits the same. (8 years and still going) Joyce’s pan mee never fails to impress, It’s simple, handmade noodles shaped to perfection with that familiar taste that never gets old.

It’s a humble, family-run stall where the wife is the heart of the kitchen and the husband quietly preps fresh vegetables by her side. The whole atmosphere feels nostalgic — every bowl reminds me of the old days. Honestly, Joyce Pan Mee singlehandedly made me eat so much till I became fat, but it’s worth every bite. Consistent, comforting, and full of heart.

author: Wong Jennifer
review_text:
Few different type of food choices. Somehow hard to find parking at the roadside especially peak hours. Paid mbpp parking lots from 8-6pm. After 6pm, free mbpp parking lots at roadside.

First time Tried 珍记 fried rice 排骨王炒饭 RM10. Taste normal and a bit salty. Rice and Meat portion is ok , but the pork taste normal, no surprise.

Environment is clean. Near to USM.

author: Chen Walter
review_text:
Good old school vibes , as a Singaporean couldn’t really find much of a place like that, But special shout out:

KANG JAPANESE CUISINE:

Had the Unagi bento set, lovely unagi with 2 tempura ebi & 2 Takoyaki balls , lovely Japanese rice drizzled with Tare & a pellet cleansing salad which is sour yet sweet & a very nice hint of umami, totally worth a try when you all come down and dine here.

For the sides I ordered a set takoyaki ball, lovely crust outside with a very soft batter, drizzle with mayo and bulldog sauce that compliments the heavy flavours of the takoyaki really reminds me of Japan.

My partner ordered the cheesy chicken katsu curry rice, Moist Chicken with a very crispy outlet breading , The side of the most tastiest Japanese curry I ever had, nice savoury with a hint of sweet, containing potatoes and carrots.

Price wise is very worthy with a huge portion size.

author: Mingsheng Lum
review_text:
Local nasi kandar
If your near sg dua / USM. Try ~
Aim for their fried chicken 🍗

This food court have many others local Chinese food for everyday meal

author: Swee Ping Lim
review_text: This hawker centre houses about 20 food stalls, covering some of the most popular foods in Penang. Overall the food quality is good and the price is reasonable. Sometimes it can be difficult to find a car park, especially during peak hours.

author: Michael Ooi
review_text: Decent sized food court with quite a variety of food. What I liked about this food court is that it has some less common food - i.e. not limited to the regular stuff like Koay Teow soup, Wantan mee, Curry mee... Instead, you get stuff like Japanese rice set, gourmet fried rice, Thai food, Sarawak kolo mee, special dumplings, cuisines from China, et al. I've tried the Mala noodles, which was ok. Chongqing dried noodle wasn't bad either. The Tai Lok Mee was good. Mutton satay was awesome. Everything was reasonably priced.

author: Eric Tan
review_text:
A lot of variety of food but the quality is averaged only, in taste versus its value.
We ordered Pan Mee Soup, Hoo Tau Bee Hoon, Chee Cheong Fun, and Siow Bak Rice.

This time around, we ordered Xiao Leung Pao plain + Malak, Vegetarian Dumpling, Fried Pork Gyoza, Bitter Gourd Soup, Hockien Mee, Chee Cheong Fun, Fish Meat & Dumpling Soup, and Otak².

The Hockien Mee is so diluted and inconsistent in taste. A few days ago, we came and the HKM was superb, but this time, it was so diluted and sweet.

The notable dishes are the Fish Meat & dumpling soup. Previously, the Siow Bak rice was good but was overwhelmed by its sauce. Half a portion of the sauce is sufficient rather than wetting the whole rice and plate.

FOOD          : Non-Halal
LOCATION : Beside USM (Sg Nibong)
CHOICE      : Good
TASTE          : Good
PRICE          : Satisfactory
AVG.VALUE:  RM5.10 - 18 per plate / set

author: R K
review_text:
Review only for 2 specific things.Otherwise is not bad.
Pineapple juice was so diluted that it was hard to taste any Pineapple at all.
the Normal popiah was soaking wet. Not sure if that is supposed to be that wet.

author: M miss
review_text:
Pan Mee tasted bland. Chee Cheong Fun was average. Good food was the Pork trotter vinegar, Chinese dumplings and Japanese dishes... but the quality is not the same, sometimes it tastes good and sometimes it doesn't.

The music on TV is too loud. It's too noisy, making it uncomfortable to have a meal in such a loud environment.

author: Teoh Sin Yee
review_text:
Quite nice:
-Cantonese style loh mee (beside fried rice stall)
-Siew Mai (Surprisingly fresh)

Can eat but no wow factor:
- Cheese Prawn rice set (beside chicken chop stall)
- Taiwanese chicken chop rice
- Rice set with soup (beside wantan mee)
- Nasi kandar
- Pan Mee

Just small list that I've tried.

author: LeanGuan Seow
review_text: This bustling coffee shop is a lively spot filled with a wide variety of hawker stalls, making it a great place for casual dining. Nearly half of the stalls serve Chinese cuisine, offering everything from northern to southern flavors. Among the top picks are the wantan mee with its springy noodles and savory sauce, the tender and flavorful chicken rice, and the Sarawak kolok mee—light, fragrant, and satisfying. With so many choices under one roof, it’s perfect for group dining. Affordable prices and quick service make it a favorite neighborhood go-to.

author: Hui Ying Tan
review_text:
I have tried most stalls and these are my honest opinions on what to order

Quite good
Wan tan mee (morning till afternoon only)
Mala Xiang Guo
Chee Cheong Fun
Japanese bento stall
Ah zhen fried rice stall
Soup stall
China fish fillet stall (酸菜鱼）

Okok
Fish head bee hoon
Sarawak kolo mee

What to avoid (not good)
Penang laksa
Yong Tau Foo
Pan mee
Hokkien mee

Going to try their other stalls and update my review here accordingly.

author: CK Tan
review_text:
This is one of the very popular kopitiam next to the USM. Many hawker stalls providing wide variety of local foods and snacks. I particularly like the Zhu Chong Fun, every visit must order the small plate.
I noticed some of the food quality is not maintaining recently, even the famous stalls. Penangites are picky eaters, they should have maintain the food quality.
Pricing is hiking with recent inflation, eating out is no longer a cheaper option.
Parking is available around the kopitiam, but it is a real headache, as the parking space is limited.

author: Koyushi
review_text:
Varieties of hawker food meams spoil by choices.
Its rather a big food court but narrow between tables to table at certain sections

Overall you almost find all hawker food under one roof  its worth to visit.

author: Kenn Mullen
review_text: If you havent tried the char koay teow here before, you are missing out. Its got such a rich flavour and hits all the right notes. Smooth buttery texture mixed with a nice consistency of noodles make it such a wonderfull experience. There is no better char koay teow than here. I dare you to tell me one better. I have yet to try anything else in this food court other than the fried chicken (not bad) but if you see this and havent tried it PLEASE DO!

author: bl tan
review_text:
Premium price food court, just wonder the students and university area the food price can be like George town food price.
The environment is better and chilled, maybe that is the reason food price so high.

author: Kelvin Ying
review_text:
Local kopitiam. Been frequenting here especially when i don't know what to eat because near to where i stay.

The nasi kandar is quite famous. Many customers like their fried chicken. Pan mee is popular especially during breakfast time.

There is also a soup stall in this kopitiam, which is easy for me to get my soup-craving fixed. Personally recommend their seafood set meal, fried lou xu fan and Kowloon bubble waffle. Chee cheong fun, bun and siew mai also good choice when looking for something light.

author: Lee wei ching
review_text: Bali drink is not cook with Bali, but is make by Bali powder only, not recommended to order this drink, the food portion is small, suitable for kid

author: leong tatt lee
review_text: The Nasi kandar curry taste is ok. Price ABOVE average. Satay taste normal.

author: Kevin Yeoh
review_text:
Oh my god. This place serves really good nasi kandar food and I kinda regret not visiting this place earlier. The biryani and the dishes are mostly good. So far, the only dish not worth buying is the lamb shank as my colleague ordered it and feedback that the meat is hard, so it is not worth paying RM48 for the lamb shank!

Price is more on the high side. For example one piece of fried chicken cost RM11 but strangely mutton curry also cost RM11, I always thought mutton will be more expensive. 🤔

Seats are aplenty as you can also go to level 1 if the ground floor seats are fully packed. Parking is also plenty around the shoplot area.

All in all, still worth visiting. Taste really good compare to other famous nasi kandar stalls around Penang.

author: theErn
review_text: Yusuf Restaurant Vervea is a two-story malay restaurant that sells local malay food located in Batu Kawan Penang. The restaurant sells Nasi Kandar, roti Canai and many more. The food is nice and the price is reasonable. The nasi kandar cost around RM12. One of the unique: use the lift go to the second floor and it has free WiFi. Overall, it is good.

author: Farahanani Azri
review_text: It's hard for me to say anything i ate is good but this one won my heart. Didnt realize i finished the whole plate with murtabak too. Kuah campur and everything is tasteful instead of you tasting nothing when u mix it. Best one to get is ayam bawang, peria goreng, bawang goreng, kambing kurma. Try their murtabak daging with its dipping its so good. Good ambience with aircond and clean restaurant. Drinks are delicious and service is fast. Would repeat again here.

author: sally
review_text:
Restaurant is convenient and comfortable (aircond), with lift to 2nd floor.

I want to suggest to add more tables and chairs. Restaurant is spacious but not enough seatings (during peak hour lunch). So you can see empty space but not enough tables & chairs.

Food is okay and price is also considered affordable.

author: Zalikha Ishak
review_text:
Yusuf Restaurant Vervea is a true gem in Penang, easily earning its spot as one of the best places for nasi kandar and nasi briyani in Batu Kawan. Their nasi briyani, in particular, is a standout – incredibly flavourful and fragrant, a delightful aromatic experience with every bite.

When you visit, I highly recommend trying their signature nasi kandar and, of course, the nasi briyani. Don't miss out on their excellent side dishes, especially the ayam masak bawang and ayam masak rose. Be sure to add some of their crispy bawang goreng and a generous pour of kuah campur to complete your meal.

Beyond the fantastic food, the restaurant itself is a pleasant surprise. It's noticeably clean and boasts a nice decoration, creating a comfortable dining atmosphere. There are plenty of tables on the ground floor, and if it gets busy, you can head up to the upper level where even more tables are available. Convenience is key here, as they also provide surau facilities and clean toilets for patrons. Parking is a breeze, with plenty of parking spaces available around the restaurant.

Be aware that the queue for lunch can be quite long, a testament to its popularity, but it's definitely worth the wait. All in all, I absolutely love Yusuf Restaurant Vervea and will always make it a point to come back whenever I'm in Penang.

author: Kai ce Yap
review_text:
This restaurant is a cozy mamak spot. The nasi kandar is good, and the roti canai is very delicious, crispy and nicely done. However, the kuah isn’t that tasty. As for the Maggi goreng, the taste was a bit weird for me, kind of like it had a taste of peanut, which I didn’t quite enjoy.

The price here is  high, likely due to the area and the nice environment, it feels more like a high-class mamak.

If I compare it to Ali Khan and Nasmir:

Nasmir is my No. 1 choice, good taste and value overall.

Ali Khan is cheaper, but the taste is just average.

This place has the best environment, but also the highest price.

author: Nur Aniesha
review_text: Good food , happy tummy❤️ my fav tandoori and nasi ayam bawang so goooood. spacious & comfortable☺️

author: wiyuna teoh
review_text: Nasi kandar kuah campur  with sotong, egg & fried bitter gourd …curry was flavorful…for murtabak taste good too…more seating available at 2nd floor

author: Lee Youn
review_text:
We recently visited Yusuf restaurant and had a wonderful experience! The food was absolutely excellent — fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented. The atmosphere was warm and welcoming, making it a perfect place to relax and enjoy a great meal.

A special thanks to Mr. Yasir and his amazing team for their outstanding hospitality. They were very cooperative, professional, and made our event truly special. Everything was perfectly organized, and we really appreciate their efforts.

Highly recommended for anyone looking for great food and excellent service! 👏🍽️✨

author: candice chong
review_text: Air conditioned restaurant selling nasi kandar. If you seek for halal food in Batu kawan area, can have a try .

author: Meng p
review_text: Our first stop in Penang, really good food and plus point is this place is air-conditioned. Price also reasonable.

author: Aurelia
review_text:
For someone who does not really like the strong taste of briyani, I think the briyani is really delicious. 💜 My husband, who loves briyani, said it's amazing 👏

Can request kuah campur asing for those that doesn't like banjir like me 😂 The sotong is nice, not liat at all.

Idk how much each of these cost, but for 4 adults and 3 children (food & drinks), it was about RM120-ish, not so bad imo.

Overall, the place is quite clean, but the service is a bit slow when there are a lot of people.

Can come here again :)

author: shafik karim
review_text:
Overall good restaurant, most comfortable queue-time i spend throughout my holiday in Penang.
Closeby to Outlet, so after shopping can eat nasi kandar here

author: Bamin Razali
review_text:
Came in the evening. Unfortunately, food was cold. Wud taste better if theyre hot or at least warm. The fried bitter gourd and fried onions were marvelous, tho !

Teh Ais was fine, not bad.

Comfortable joint with AC.

author: RAVINDARAN V RAMAN
review_text: First time eating here and the food is quite good. The food in my picture looks not the best because I packed the food to the hotel. It's fried chicken with kuah campur and mutton curry. When the food is good we come again and again

author: Emi Mustarudin
review_text: Used to be a very great place for authentic food but somehow the food quality is getting bad,not all of course. We have encountered 3 times undercooked chicken ,salty vegetables and smelly cabbages. Hope the owner can  have an eye on the cooks . All the best!

author: DEREKWAH
review_text:
The curry is fragrance
So rich and flavourful
I like the rice serve in warm
Only the bad thing is the shop lot of fly
If can settle this problem will be more nicer

Overall price vs quality is definitely wort to come again

author: Ahhkhai Studio Official
review_text: A bit expensive, but not well cooked and the hygiene a little disappointed, the housefly is everywhere, not same as the first time I went here for lunch

author: Sam Tan
review_text: Food may be good, I'll explain why. We were asked to leave at 1 pm on the 1st floor cause they are closing the section without a good explanation. And we just managed to take our seat around 12.45pm. I do not understand why they do that. We have to finish up our lunch in a hurry and dun even have chances to taste the food well. Overall, very bad service cause the restaurant is not respected their customer.

author: Mek Nani
review_text:
I aimed for pasembur and my hubby and kids really craved for nasi kandar ..and we were very lucky that this restaurant really served to our craving.
The beautiful interior design, the cleanliness and the friendly staff really impressed us.

author: Jason Tan
review_text:
I’ve been to this place twice now, and both visits have been really enjoyable. The food quality is consistently impressive, and everything I’ve tried so far has left a positive impression. One of my favorites is the unagi dish — the eel was fresh and perfectly prepared, with rich and well-balanced flavors. The whole plate had depth and character; it wasn’t just another plain healthy meal.

My friend ordered the Kampung Rasa ones, and agreed it was another standout. The sambal had just the right level of heat — not overly spicy, but still full of bold, flavorful notes that complemented the other elements on the plate. Then there was the salmon dish, which was another highlight. The salmon itself was fresh, nicely cooked, and the skin was perfectly crispy. It paired wonderfully with the tartar sauce, creating a great balance of texture and taste.

If I had to point out one flaw, it would be that the rest of the salad came without any dressing, which made it feel a bit plain. A light passion fruit dressing or something with a bit of tang would really lift it up.

The environment during both my visits was quiet and relaxed — a great place to chill and chat with friends. However, since I came during workday rushing lunch hours, so I wasn't enjoying the vibes much. Overall, this spot offers quality food, fresh ingredients, and a calm dining atmosphere. Definitely worth visiting again!

author: 01234568 i
review_text:
Nice sandwich/salad place around the neighborhood.

Ordered the salmon bowl which is discounted on Fridays, leans more to the healthy side at the cost of some flavor. Salmon was slightly dry, but the accompanying sauce was quite good.

Service is good and friendly, decor is nice, environment is decent but gets a little noisy when the weekday lunch crowd arrives.

* This establishment provides rewards in return for reviews or social media posts, but the food and service is very good regardless

author: LI YUEN TANG
review_text: Every time I visit Batu Kawan, Sandwish is always a must-stop for me. Love the cozy ambiance and the welcoming vibe, it feels like the perfect spot to relax. The food is consistently delicious and satisfying, definitely one of my favorite cafés here!

author: WeiPeng
review_text: Hidden gem! Love this place. Many choices, Healthy Rasa Bowls, Pasta using premium ingredients, even the olive oil. The portion is big and you can't find this price in KL. Highly recomended!

author: Teoh Soo Chong
review_text:
Truly enjoy these delicious Chipotle chicken sandwiches with crunchy nachos from SANDWISH Borelis, Batu Kawan, Penang  👍🙏😍😃

Thank you
Teoh Soo Chong
22 Oct 2025

author: Vivian Hera
review_text: First time trying out this place, the food looks appetizing. I ordered custom bowl and it was delicious and healthy, the ambiance was very relaxing too, will definitely visit again next time 👍

author: Lim CY
review_text:
My favourite spot for sandwiches and poke bowls, with branches in Batu Kawan, Bayan Lepas and Georgetown. The sandwiches here are generously portioned and made with fresh, quality ingredients. My go-to is the avocado/egg/sweet potato sandwich. It is wholesome and well-balanced in flavour.

The poke bowls are equally satisfying. I have tried the salmon, spring onion chicken, and tofu bowls,  all were flavorful, fresh, and packed with generous portions of toppings. They also offer Daily Savings items from Monday to Friday, making imore affordable.

author: Ilah Rusli
review_text: Went there few times.. so far all good. I love the sandwich and poke bowl.

author: Chick Doctor
review_text:
Awesome place! Very generous portions, delicious (healthy) food, and nice vibes!

Must come ❤️ New fav in this area!

author: Jacqueline Tew
review_text:
The food was served very quick and looks good!

However, I would like to add that the honey mustard chicken we ordered (which was a recommended menu item) was underwhelming and not what was expected. The chicken was cold and slightly overcooked. I believe it would taste better if the chicken was crispy and hot from the pan/airfryer.

The staff here are friendly and helpful (ie. explaining the menu ingredients, checking on availability, during payments). They are doing their best to give the customers a good service. Of course, the ambiance of the cafe is comfortable as well.

As this is their soft-launching era, I trust that the team is continuously improving and perfecting their menu. Worth to give them a chance 🫶🏻

author: JC C (CuteDracul)
review_text: Very high quality food with generous portions and surprising affordable. Love this place!

author: Goh Su Teng
review_text: Perfect environment for a gathering or dine-in, cozy. Food arrangement look appetising. Service crew is nice

author: Datcanraw Chandrarao
review_text: Great service, the sandwiches are hefty, reasonably priced and has balanced taste. Underrated store in Batu Kawan

author: Loh Woei Kang
review_text: Nice sandwish and salads. They provide calories for all their foods sonyou can control you calories intake for your meal!

author: Jheems (陳國敬)
review_text: Healthy food and good atmosphere in the restaurant to enjoy one meal with your love one

author: Bong-Ki Jung
review_text: The salad in the poke bowl was honestly terrible. It felt like it was spoiled — mushy, with no freshness at all. It seems to depend on the staff, as some carefully choose fresh ingredients while others don’t seem to care whether the vegetables are fresh or not. I ordered this meal to eat healthy, but the texture was unpleasant and the lack of freshness in the vegetables was really disappointing.

author: Eric Chan
review_text:
Okay, let's be real, sometimes you just crave a good sandwich. And that's where Sandwish in Batu Kawan comes in. This spot is a total gem! Their sandwiches are stacked high with fresh ingredients, and the bread is seriously on point. I especially loved "the ms avocado and honey mustard chicken”, the chicken was so tender and crispy”!

Beyond the sandwiches, their pastries are a must-try. I indulged in a “tiramisu croffle" and it was pure heaven. The service was super friendly, and the cafe itself has a really chill vibe. If you're in Batu Kawan, definitely check out Sandwish!

author: Choo
review_text: A cozy cafe to have the breakfast. You can opt for wheal meal bread for the sandwich, come with add-on option. Overall it’s slightly pricy.

author: Hemma M
review_text: We had to wait for 15 minutes as I went with my team during lunch hour. I had the vegetarian poke bowl which is an huge portion and it was good. The lychee drink tasted refreshing as well. A recommended place for those looking for a healthy option around Batu Kawan.

author: Tan Minhwa
review_text: Sandwish was truly an amazing experience. The service was fast and nice. The place gave such cozy vibes and really made my day unforgettable. This is definitely a five star cafe and I really recommend this place.

restaurant: Ming Qin Charchol Duck Egg Char Koay Teow
author: C L
review_text: This charcoal duck fried kuau teow very nice and got the "wok hei". Taste good and the duck fried egg is delicious. Price is reasonable. No need long queue and fast serving. Got plenty place to sit. Parking also ok either park inside or opposite just nearby. Just the prawn is abit small of compare those in the island but the taste is definitely good.

restaurant: Ming Qin Charchol Duck Egg Char Koay Teow
author: kk teoh
review_text:
One of Bukit Mertajam's Michelin award eateries, this place has been drawing crowds locally and outstation.  It is located along Jalan Betek in an unassuming location, which looks more like a car respray workshop.  This also means that when the eatery opens at 6pm, there is some space for parking.

We were fortunate to arrive when the crowd has not built yet on a Wednesday evening.  Ordered two plates of regular char koay teow with duck eggs, which came to RM9 (at the time of writing).  The dishes came relatively quickly.  The char koay teow does not look much like the typical Penang char koay teow as it is darker and not as spicy (even though we mentioned that we are OK with chilli).  Visually, it does not look appetising, but surprisingly it tasted really good.  It had lots of wok hei, presumably from the use of charcoal fire, and the pork lard pieces were crispy and delicious.  The eggs were perfectly cooked and the runny egg yolk added a different layer of umami compared to normal char koay teow.  Portions were also adequate and we left feeling satisfied.

You also have the option of adding side dishes, though we chose not to do so.

A nice place to eat and will return as long as prices are maintained.

restaurant: Ming Qin Charchol Duck Egg Char Koay Teow
author: Garry Reviews
review_text: Location is wide open space with plenty of tables. There are 2 sections of seatings 1 is an air conditioned room with about 10 tables while the open space area has lots more tables. Ordering is simple, there is a small table with the menu with pictures displayed and prices. However everything is in Chinese but a simple point and showing your digits is sufficient unless you have special requirements like extra egg and sides, could be a challenge if you are not proficient in the Chinese language. Depending on the crowd, it could also take quite a while to be ready. The CKT is average, not too salty or oily. Decent wok hei with small prawns and teeny bits of lap cheong. The octopus however takes the limelight I would say. It was cooked perfectly with soy sauce and oyster sauce, served with some coriander which provides a crisps and sharp fresh contrast to the savoury dish. The sauce is salty and addictive to complement the tender octopus. It doesn’t matter which part you eat, they are all tender, not rubbery or chewy. The head of the octopus, kind of satisfyingly pops when chewed. The chilli sauce that accompanies it is delicious and enhances the taste a little bit to the already delicious dish. Overall it’s a good meal to try for these two dishes. A single toilet is available at the end of the air conditioned room. For these 2 dishes, octopus rm28 and Ckt rm10.

restaurant: Ming Qin Charchol Duck Egg Char Koay Teow
author: Dizi Concerto
review_text:
Separate additional menu for egg, clams, sausage? Surprised and couldn’t believe. RM4 for only a few clams? Beyond ripoff. Only RM1 differences between small and large portion? Obviously you will feel better to get the large portion but what about people who just want to eat less?

Now now, I wouldn’t complain at all if the foods are tasty. Which they AREN’T at all!!!!

And not to mention the waiting time. We waited an hour or maybe more. Which is till acceptable if it is tasty! Problem is it is NOT tasty and very felt ripoff!!!

restaurant: Ming Qin Charchol Duck Egg Char Koay Teow
author: Ong Shu Wen
review_text: Tried a Michelin-listed restaurant in BM, and I must say the Char Kuey Teow was impressive — the charcoal frying gave it a strong wok hei that even beats some I've had in Penang. The lala was flavourful at first but became a bit too sweet and overwhelming after a few bites. On the plus side, the restaurant has a spacious parking area, and food was served quickly. Overall, it’s a must-try spot if you’re in BM.

restaurant: Ming Qin Charchol Duck Egg Char Koay Teow
author: ALTUS WEALTH
review_text:
Delicious CKT with duck egg. Compared to many places, this one tastes so good and wok hey. Remember to ask for duck egg. Can get crowded at some hours. Have been here many years, even before they were awarded. Family business from humble beginnings.
Try the seafood sides. Surely will come back.

restaurant: Ming Qin Charchol Duck Egg Char Koay Teow
author: Ks T
review_text:
Attracted to there by recommendation from internet source.
Saw they won many prizes and having recognition by Michelin star.
Have been told to wait for half an hour when I ordered.
Perhaps initially set the expectation too high, sorry to say that the food for me was indeed, so so only... Don't really feel the difference of duck egg or difference by charcoal... Or maybe my tastebuds "degraded"?...

restaurant: Ming Qin Charchol Duck Egg Char Koay Teow
author: 茉莉Jasmine
review_text: Get a try because of the Michelin rated. Personally feel the char koay teow is overrated.... The taste is so so and didn't meet my normal char koay teow expectation. Maybe for others the taste is suit them but not for me....

restaurant: Ming Qin Charchol Duck Egg Char Koay Teow
author: Yu Gen
review_text: Already craved for Penang/Bm Ckt for a long time. Cooked by the shop owner daughter, the taste and colour are much heavier and darker than other ckt in Penang. It also more greasy and wet compared to Penang's style. The portion for big and small has no difference, so better order normal size is enough. The wokhei taste good, only have lapcheong, beansprouts, jiucai, no siham in the ckt.

restaurant: Ming Qin Charchol Duck Egg Char Koay Teow
author: Martin C
review_text: I noticed the rating was under 4, and that actually made me more determined to leave a good review because this kind of traditional food shouldn't be overlooked. Ming Qin's charcoal-fried duck egg char kuey teow is genuinely delicious. The charcoal aroma is something you can hardly find outside anymore. The duck egg was cooked perfectly - yolk slightly runny but not too watery - and it coated the noodles so well. The kuey teow was full of flavor with strong wok hei. I ordered the large with two eggs, and before leaving I even packed another one to take home.Truly one of the rare places that still keep this traditional taste alive.

restaurant: Ming Qin Charchol Duck Egg Char Koay Teow
author: Chun Kheong Chong
review_text: A not bad spot for those who are craving for charcoal duck egg char kuey teow. It is very flavourful with a balanced level of spiciness. The flavour is rather consistent for each strand of noodles. You will also get to taste the pork lard as well. Not too salty. Combo with iced nutmeg juice will be the best after meal with gives you a refreshing feeling. They have plenty of parking and you don’t even need to worry about it. The traffic here is quite fine too.

restaurant: Ming Qin Charchol Duck Egg Char Koay Teow
author: Dan Tang
review_text:
Charcoal fried Kuey teow in Penang.... very popular with locals. Spicy octopus is also very delicious!!
Only open in the evening...
Recommended.

restaurant: Ming Qin Charchol Duck Egg Char Koay Teow
author: Pang WS
review_text:
One of my favourite spots for duck egg char kuey teow in mainland BM. I do enjoy their kuey teow's wok hei. Pair those with the steamed octopus for a perfect combo.

Table wait and queue would be subject to weekends/holidays season.

Ample but limited parking available within the premises.

restaurant: Ming Qin Charchol Duck Egg Char Koay Teow
author: Eunice Ang
review_text: So far the best char kwy teow I had , someone brought me there and I would say the taste is so good and wok hey.  I grab another pack after I reached hotel! Hehe

restaurant: Ming Qin Charchol Duck Egg Char Koay Teow
author: Nubert Sawarimuthu
review_text:
Very good and tasty CKT….. will definitely return when I’m in BM next

Wok Hei 👍
Portion 👍
Taste 💯

Overall- 9/10

restaurant: Ming Qin Charchol Duck Egg Char Koay Teow
author: J Luke
review_text: This is a Michelin Star Charcoal Duck Egg Char Koay Teow with Siham/Cockles. Dammmmmmn Gooooood 👍👍👍👍👍👍

restaurant: Ming Qin Charchol Duck Egg Char Koay Teow
author: Beng Lee Tan
review_text: 🚫carcinogenic because no have wok屎， taste very very good, must try ya!!! But, very very small portion, can eat 2 plate 😂might due to CNY Lantern Festival (Chap Go Meh) or CNY special price, no have much people, after back from washroom already serves the food

restaurant: Ming Qin Charchol Duck Egg Char Koay Teow
author: Dyi Wong
review_text:
This Michelin-star char koay teow is next-level goodness, with that rich duck egg flavor coating every strand of noodle. It’s the kind of taste that wraps around your taste buds and stays there, with just the right balance—not too salty, but still packing all the flavor.

Is it the absolute top best? Maybe not *the* best, but it’s definitely in the hall of fame for char koay teow. If you’re a fan, this one’s worth every bite—it’s one of those dishes that makes you proud to be Malaysian!

restaurant: Ming Qin Charchol Duck Egg Char Koay Teow
author: Kock Sing Tan
review_text:
We reached the restaurant on weekend at about 8pm. There were plenty of parking spaces at the roadside. There was no queue time for the table. We chose the airconditional seating.

First of all, we needed to order at the fried koay teow stall. Serving within 20 minutes, although the server said waiting time was 45 minutes. Fried koay teow was delicious but not that great. It had wok hei but not enough. Prawns were too small and had too few ingredients. It's just slightly above average. The skills were normal only. RM7 per serving. 3 stars

We needed to collect an order form from the fried koay teow stall for drinks and side dishes but very strage, the drinks and side dishes were not belonged to the fried koay teow stall. We were told to bring the order form back to our table and fill in. Then, another server would come to our table to collect the order.

The side dishes octopus was the star of the night. It was very special, fresh and juicy. We never try before such a delicious octopus. RM25 wasvaluede for money. 5 stars

The side dishes steam lala with onion ginger was delicious. The sauce was so addictive. RM28 per serving was value for money. 5 stars

The four fruit desert 四果汤 at RM10 per serving was the best we tried so far of its kind. The ingredients were so rich and many varieties. The soup was not too sweet and just nice. 5 stars

We came for fried koay teow of Michelin but ended up finding other gems.

restaurant: Ming Qin Charchol Duck Egg Char Koay Teow
author: Super Fragrance
review_text:
Ordered large ckt for 8rm. Wait time was 10min.

Kway tiao was actually well fried and very tasty in a savory way. However it has one fatal flaw. Their pork lard. This is the first time i had pork lard totally ruin the dish. The oil they used to fry the lard must has been reused so many times that the lard just has a  stanch of oiliness and after consumption it feels very greasy. Such a shame whole dish ruin.

Other things to note is large plates only comes with daoge and a bit of lup cheong and small shrimp. There is no hum nor fried egg.

author: Destry Sagita
review_text:
On my mom's phone like usual to make a review since she's not the kind of person who makes reviews. But anyways, we went to BM Yam Rice Kopitiam on our last day (which was the day we were going to go home) in Penang, 7 October which was yesterday for lunch.

Ordered the signature yam rice with pork soup (there were two bowls of pork soup, one with what i think is what usually is, pork belly, a type of pork cut i don't know and meatballs.)The other bowl had some weirder cuts (that i don't like but my parents love) think there was pork intestine but i forgot the pork cuts/parts of the rest in that soup. The bowl of pork soup i had (that i ate most of it on my own too) was the one without pork intestine (my parents shared that bowl of soup) and IMO of my taste buds, it tasted pretty good. The pork soup had some chopped pickled mustard greens (i think that's the English name) too but they didn't taste very sour (which i liked since i often find the pickled vegetable too sour) and they made (at least, i think they were the cause) the soup a little sour-ish, which tasted good in the soup, not too sour but just sour enough to be refreshing in a way. The pork itself in the soup tasted great too. And the pork soup was a great combo with the yam rice. The yam rice was a little salty but it was really good, i don't quite know how to describe the taste but i really liked it, especially paired with the pork soup. Oh yeah, we also ordered the braised tofu and egg which were good too. I had specially drank some of the soup and ate some of the pork and a little of my yam rice before picking some pork (and a meatball) and a half braised egg and placed them in my yam rice before chopping the egg with my spoon and mixing the yam rice with it and with the pork and meatball too (it tasted great!)
I don't know how much it costed since my parents were the one that paid and they forgot how much it was. But anyways, i'd say this place was a pretty solid 4/5 out of 5 stars, though i put it four stars since i only went there once (oh and that time was also my first time eating yam rice, so yam rice had a pretty good first impression on me from this place) Anyways, i would recommend this place to people going to Penang and haven't decided what to eat yet (and especially if they haven't eaten yam rice before or like yam rice)

And yep, that's all, it's a little long but oh well, overall, it was a great experience (and as usual, i was the last one to finish my bowl, since i like doing everything and maybe especially eating at my own pace)

author: Xiao Xuan
review_text:
Michelin rated food! But it’s more of a local delicacy, simple yet comforting food.
Most importantly the pork does not have any weird porky taste, all the innards is prepared well. The pork blood jelly is very nice, given four large pieces! The meat pork ball is yummy too!
The yam rice is surprisingly very tasty! Fluffy fragrant rice, paired with yam so yummyyy
The chili sauce given and the soup is very good. The soup is very light yet flavourful.
The hygiene can be questionable but well no one had any diarrhoea. Service is quick, pay when food arrive.
Would come back again!

author: Choon T
review_text: Yam rice in BM is very similar to 猪杂汤 in Singapore. Flavours were authentic and the braised pork trotters were very good too. The chilli paste with the dark soya sauce was perfect to go with the ingredients and rice.

author: Ong Shu Wen
review_text: Tried the Michelin-recognised yam rice shop in BM — definitely a must-try. I went around 10am on a Friday and it wasn’t crowded yet, but it started filling up soon after. The place is spacious with plenty of seating. The yam rice was fragrant and flavourful, truly worthy of the Michelin mention. The pork mixed with salted vegetable soup was also very tasty. However, the vinegar pork trotter wasn’t really my thing. Portions are generous and prices are very reasonable.

author: Ivan Beh
review_text: The yam rice, pork ball and soup is nice, can’t find it in KL, worth to wait (almost 30 to 45 minutes)

author: JH Tang (Jia)
review_text: Just came back for my kid’s favorite yam rice — still tastes just as good! The soup is clear but full of flavor, with soft pork and yummy meatballs. The price is okay, and the food quality hasn’t changed. A nice place for a warm, comforting meal that brings back memories. 😋😋😋

author: Sharix Ng
review_text: Best yam rice in Penang Mainland! Sometimes might need to take longer time for the food served due to peak hour, but good food worth the wait

author: Mel Teoh
review_text: The best yam rice I had so far! The rice has been cooked with fresh yam and tiny dried shrimp mixed in it. You can see the melted yam in the rice! Also the soup is unlimited to refill!!! Tastes sour and umami with the pork meat in the soup which packed with lot of flavours in the soup. Heard from one my friends said this is the Michelin starred restaurant. Not sure is it true or not but for me, this restaurant is worth to try out their food!

author: batutour -
review_text: BM Yam Rice is a 40-year-old traditional kopitiam in Bukit Mertajam that truly deserves its Michelin Guide recognition. Run by three sisters who took over from their father, this establishment serves exceptional yam rice cooked with shrimp paste, paired perfectly with their signature pork soup featuring pickled mustard greens. . While the non-air-conditioned environment might get warm during peak hours, the authentic flavors, especially after 12PM when the soup reaches its peak taste, make it well worth the visit. Their braised dishes, including pork leg, tofu, eggs, and sausages, are prepared fresh daily, maintaining consistently high quality that keeps both locals and international visitors coming back.

author: Sam Shee
review_text:
Long wait in a large warehouse of a coffee shop with the most amazing yam rice!

Pretty affordable with plenty of large round tables and plastic seats, with relatively quick service for a full house. Staff are curt and the place is warm, but it's a eat-and-go type place so don't expect to get too comfy.

author: Ray Sim
review_text:
Food rating note:
Average - 2.5/5
My comfort food - 5/5

Similar to pig organ soup. Nice soup and fresh ingredients. Their chilli is great. Slightly ex.

Recommended items:
Soup with pork ingredients - 4.1/5
Braised tau gua - 4/5

The meal average at 4/5

author: EG
review_text:
First time trying Yam Rice and it is surprisingly good! The soup is a bit on the sour side, not my thing but it's unique for sure.

Overall it's affordable and will definitely come again!

author: Super Fragrance
review_text:
Ordered yam rice plus mixed pork soup for 13rm. This isn't preferred by locals clearly from the lack of customers.

But i prefer this as their yam rice is definitely superior due to the salted fish. Soup was sour in a great way. Pork were generally okay some more porky than the other for example the meat ball but okay.

But the show stealer is definitely the rice with salted fish it was pretty homogeneous meaning u don't get a bit of only super salted fish, instead the taste was consistent throughout.

author: oXRYSTALo Ong
review_text:
BM Yam Rice Kopitiam: A Delicious Dive into Dannok Dim Sum in Bukit Mertajam (4/5 Stars)

Rating:

• Food: 4/5 (Delicious and authentic Dannok Dim Sum, with standout dishes like the Yam rice, pig organ soup, and braised pig trotter)
• Service: 3/5 (Friendly and efficient, but could be more attentive)
• Ambiance: 4/5 (Casual and welcoming atmosphere, perfect for a relaxed meal with friends)
• Value: 4/5 (Reasonable prices for the quality of food)

Overall: 4/5

Alright folk, Recently, Donkey & I with a group of friends made the trip to BM Yam Rice Kopitiam, a popular Dannok Dim Sum spot located at 7, Jalan Murthy, 14000 Bukit Mertajam, Pulau Pinang, Malaysia.  We were eager to try their authentic Dannok Dim Sum, and we weren't disappointed!

The highlight of our meal was definitely the pig organ soup, which was flavorful and comforting.  The braised pig trotter and braised intestine were also incredibly delicious, cooked to perfection and bursting with flavor.  But for me, the star of the show was the Yam rice.  It was simply divine!  The unique blend of flavors and textures was truly satisfying, making it a dish I would highly recommend.

The atmosphere at BM Yam Rice Kopitiam was casual and welcoming, perfect for a relaxed meal with friends.  The service was friendly and efficient, and the prices were reasonable for the quality of the food.

Overall, I would highly recommend BM Yam Rice Kopitiam to anyone looking for a taste of authentic Dannok Dim Sum in Bukit Mertajam. The pig organ soup, braised pig trotter, and braised intestine are all worth trying, but the Yam rice is a must-order! Their service was ok too.

author: chiauwon chen
review_text: Self service order. U need to order your foods when u enter the shop. Yam rice is delicious. Pork soup is tasted a bit sour, yummy. Pork soup u can choose pork liver, tongue, stomach, blood, heart, kidney. No worry to choose kidney it's no any smelly taste. The chili must put some having with yam rice. It's taste best. Soup is free add on.

author: Prettyme Yu
review_text:
The pig organ soup was nice. Braised pig trotter and braised intestine was delicious.

My son especially loved the braised intestine.

Ordering very systematic. You just need find a table, then go to front to order. They will give you a number.

Serving quote fast despite a lot of ppl.

Place a bit rundown tho.

author: Jason Leong
review_text:
I've been coming to this yam rice shop since I was young, and I am truly happy that they got recognized by Michelin. They absolutely deserve it. Some people might say they've had better yam rice elsewhere, or that this place is overrated, and that's okay – everyone has their opinion. But in my mind, this is the hands-down best.

The yam rice - steamed with dark soy sauce, loaded with yam and crispy shallots; The soup - packed with flavor, made with fermented vegetables, a variety of pork cuts (meatballs, organs), and finished with a sprinkle of fresh coriander (It's so delicious, you can get free refills, and trust me, most people do!); and, to complete the experience, there's a unique condiment – a chili paste mixed with dark soy sauce – that adds a complex touch while everything complements each other perfectly. They also offer some side dishes like braised tofu and egg in dark sauce, and braised pork knuckles.

Don't expect fancy decor. The place is old-school and hasn't changed a bit since they moved to this premise. You come here for the amazing, affordable food, and that's it. With their delicious dishes and reasonable prices, anyone visiting Bukit Mertajam should definitely check them out.

author: CH Yong
review_text: Not crowded on weekday mornings. I enjoyed the rice and pork parts.

author: Nik K
review_text: Best yam rice eaten so far. The sourness of the soup was just nice and also they are very generous in the portion of meat given. Offals and pork cooked to perfection. ordered for 2 pax, and it was so good that we ordered an extra again. Great amount of yam can be seen with the rice. Situated in an old kopitiam, though not very well maintained, but the place is clean.  Highly recommended

author: Doraemon
review_text:
Kitty and I were on a road trip tfrom thialand hrough Malaysia, and we were excited to finally make it to Bukit Mertajam. We had planned our lunch stop at BM Yam Rice Kopitiam, a place known for its authentic Penang cuisine. We later learned that it had even earned a Michelin "Selected" recognition, and it was famous for its yam rice.

Walking into BM Yam Rice Kopitiam, we were greeted by a lively and bustling atmosphere. The air was filled with the delicious aroma of yam rice, and a flurry of chatter and laughter from the locals filled the space. It was clear that this was a beloved institution in Bukit Mertajam.

The atmosphere was welcoming and friendly, and even though it was a bit noisy, the fans kept the place cool enough for a comfortable dining experience.

We couldn't resist trying their signature dish, the yam rice. It was a revelation. The yam rice was cooked to perfection, boasting a strong shrimp flavor and a satisfyingly chewy texture. The accompanying pork broth was a delightful blend of briny and sweet, enhanced by the tangy depth of pickled cabbage. We also ordered the pork trotter, which was tender and flavorful, the braised tofu in soy sauce, which was a comforting classic, and the mixed organ pork soup.

The service was efficient and friendly, and the staff made sure we had a pleasant dining experience. We were surprised by how affordable the prices were, especially considering the Michelin "Selected" recognition.

Overall, we enjoyed our experience at BM Yam Rice Kopitiam.  It's a great choice for anyone in Bukit Mertajam seeking a taste of authentic Penang cuisine. The yam rice is a must try, and the other dishes we had were equally delicious. The atmosphere is a vibrant reflection of the local culture, and the service is friendly and efficient. However, the noise level could be a bit overwhelming for some.  We highly recommend this kopitiam for a delicious and authentic Penang food adventure.

author: Rudy Gerard Chong
review_text: Finally tried this well-known local coffee shop after a late lunch at the delicious nasi campur 2 stalls down, and it is worth the hype. Good thick creamy iced coffee for RM2.70. Was taken aback at the cost of their roti kahwin at RM5, but it was a good size compared to regular coffee shops, with 2 stacks toast generously spread with kaya and butter. The bread is either thinner than usually or pressed thin, which makes the serving look small, but is in fact hearty. The low roofed open dining area of the astaka is surprisingly cool despite the hot day, so its a good choice to bring friends for a lazy afternoon tea time if you don't feel like splurging at an air-conditioned cafe at premium prices, though they do close by 4pm.

author: Hiroshi Kazuhiro
review_text: The toast bread is delicious and the coffee as well. But not the nasi lemak. I don't recommend you to take the nasi lemak. The kopitiam is at the old flat neighbourhood. So it's a bit rundown. Don't expect good environment and ambient.

author: racheal Ooi
review_text: Such a shame, really. The tehC peng(both tarik and non-tarik) here is one of the better ones — smooth, fragrant, and not too sweet. Their eggs and toast are classic and done just right too. But the attitude of the staff (possibly the owners) just kills the vibe.
