review_text: I went there on a date with my boyfriend and really enjoyed the experience of dining there. The atmosphere was relaxing with a beautiful view and our waiter Nick and waitress Tina were friendly and helpful. Most importantly, the food was delicious!

author: Edison
review_text: Nice lounge cum bar with instagrammable spots for photo taking. Friendly vibes from the staff especially to Zila & Coline who were hospitable and affectionate during my multiple visits on my four days tour to KL this week. The duo warm customer service has made me a repeated customer these few days. Thank you for making my stay here a memorable ones.

author: L J (Mrs Pauer)
review_text: Stumbled upon this restaurant and we were pleasantly surprised! We chose to sit in the air-conditioned section for dinner and the food was served very quickly. The taste was great and portions were satisfying. There’s also a snack station available, which was a nice touch. Really appreciate that they have a surau provided as well. Overall, a comfortable and enjoyable dining experience. 👍✨

author: Syaz Subhan
review_text: The food was decent and the shop was clean. It’s definitely nice to have a halal restaurant right in the middle of Jalan Alor. They even have a prayer room, which is a big plus and super convenient. That said, for the same price, I’d probably choose a restaurant in a mall where the food quality is better. But if you’re there for the Jalan Alor vibe and atmosphere, then the price is acceptable. We paid the food around RM150.

author: QITING LIU
review_text: The seafood pot is generous in portion and the soup is extremely delicious; I had two to three bowls. Other stir-fried dishes also come with abundant ingredients — the water spinach and salted egg yolk chicken are particularly tasty, which deserve high praise. So delicious! The environment is nice too.

author: Elyn Chew (Lyn)
review_text:
Can’t believe that Jalan Alor not only has grilled chicken wings, but also nasi lemak seafood platter and Thai-style grilled fish!

During dinner time, it’s really crowded! Luckily, the restaurant is very spacious, and you can choose to dine outdoors, indoors (with air-conditioning), or even upstairs in private rooms (with karaoke).

We ordered their special National Day menu – the nasi lemak seafood platter. The portion was generous, and the seafood was really fresh! The sambal was super fragrant and spicy – a love-hate relationship for me 😂. The four of us ate to our hearts’ content and left very satisfied!

The grilled fish came in a Thai-style clear tomyam flavor – sour, spicy, and really appetizing! Everyone agreed it was delicious, especially since the fish meat was lightly pan-fried before being added to the soup, making it fresh and flavorful.

While waiting for food, you can also check out their snack corner – there are all sorts of titbits, candies, and ice cream to nibble on!

Since it gets really crowded on weekends, taking the MRT is a good option – it’s just a 3-minute walk away!

author: Selina Tan
review_text: Had a great time at Boleh Seafood Pot! The seafood was super fresh, especially the crab we got for free with our RM250 order 🦀🔥 Love the variety 8 kinds of seafood in one pot! The place is spacious, has karaoke rooms, and even free snacks. Perfect for group gatherings. Will definitely come back!

author: Anton Ego
review_text:
I was really disappointed with my visit to Boleh Seafood at Jalan Bukit Bintang. The food was not great at all — definitely not delicious as expected. On top of that, the cleanliness was very poor. I even saw a cockroach while I was there, which made me lose my appetite.

With so many better food options in Bukit Bintang, I would not recommend this place. Hopefully the management improves both the hygiene and food quality.

author: cathe rina
review_text: The ambiance was warm n inviting and the service top notch. It was fantastic dine in here.Food also superb higly recommended good job.

author: YEK YEE LING
review_text: Halal food available here. There’s a wide variety of seafood to choose from. I really like the seafood hotpot and salted egg sotong. I accidentally came across a free crab promotion for spending RM250 — I chose the chili crab and it was really delicious! Don’t forget about the unlimited ice cream and snacks. I’ll definitely come back again. It’s also an easy place to get to after shopping in KL city, just a short walk away.

author: Sheren
review_text: Thumbs up for their crab and chicken chili! Definitely wanna go back here if i go to KL

author: NurAfryna irdyna
review_text: Efficient and can accommodate with aircon place. Very nice ambiance and will recommend for others to try out! Came here a few times, and food is good! Come come and feast!✨

author: Pinky
review_text:
Recommended!!
Big portion and halal
Local Malaysia food taste good!

author: Dabbie Yap
review_text:
Amazing seafood spot right in the heart of KL! Boleh Seafood Pot serves a super satisfying seafood hotpot packed with prawns, squid, clams, mussels, and even deep-fried Siakap — all in a spicy, tangy broth that hits the spot. RM250 gets you the full set plus a free crab!
Great sides too (Salted Egg Sotong, dry butter Chicken, etc.), free snacks & ice cream, and even karaoke rooms for groups. Just 2 mins from Bukit Bintang MRT. Highly recommended!

author: Mah Yan Mei
review_text: Delicious seafood in KL! The Boleh Seafood Pot is a must try! Super fresh and flavourful. We also had Black Pepper Crab, Fried Garlic Kangkung, Salted Egg Sotong, and Buttermilk Chicken, all cooked perfectly. Highly recommend!

author: Wilson Shum
review_text: Had the whole fish pot that has prawns and clams and a few other bits and pieces in it.  The broth was so flavourful.  Even for me who don't like coriander cant stop eating it.  The fried fish had really nice texture and everything is super yummy.  Way better than beauty in the pot.  The dessert and snack bar also super good, the mango passion fruit soft serve helps balance the heat of the meal.  Highly recommended.

author: 傅絲斐
review_text: Fresh seafood, tasty dishes, spacious seating, and a free snack bar. Only 2 mins from Bukit Bintang MRT!

author: hazem ght
review_text: Idk , the price doest match the quantity, the said the meal cost 128 for 5 to 6 person , the rice is bearly enough for 1 person , highly not recommended to come

author: Ai Nuraidah
review_text:
I ordered nasi goreng pedas, tofu, kailan stir fry, all the food are nice
The service was ok, we didn’t wait for so long to get our food .

author: Nurhafizah Ahmadi
review_text: Best ever service😉 I have ordered for iced nescafe but the ice was very less. Without asked, abg waiter came to me and brought extra iced🥰 so nice

author: Eron Damaska
review_text: This restaurant has a very nice and lively vibes especially at night. The food is outstanding! Beat spot for hangout and chill with friends and family.

author: fara dzanufiya
review_text: in the middle of alor street , the food is really good especially the mini hotpot so good. definitely will come back and recommend to others

author: Siu Bernice
review_text:
Been here a couple of times, and today I ended up here again because my visitor *insisted* we makan here. 😂

As usual, the place was hot, packed, and buzzing with people hunting for food. You’ll also get tissue sellers going table to table — some quite persistent.

Food options? Endless. Biscuits, buns, noodles, CCF, durian, drinks — you name it, they probably have it. So many choices, you’ll definitely find something to try.

We had the vegetarian curry mee, the famous CCF, and the Bintang Cham drink and Teh.
Verdict: honestly, all quite mediocre for me. Didn’t finish the food. CCF is RM2.80 per piece, curry mee RM11.
(BUT this is just my personal taste — plenty of people around me were happily eating, so don’t take my word for it. Go try and judge for yourself!)

We also ta-pau’ed the miniature wine chicken pau, Bun Choon egg tart, nian gao, and yam kueh.
The nian gao was good — I like the original version without yam or sweet potato. The egg tart was good too.

Go try this place and eat your way to a happy tummy  !!

author: Debbie Li
review_text: I didn't understand the hype about this food court. We ate at the most popular Ahfook Yong Tau Fu stall and found it to be grossly overrated by YouTubers. Yes it is cheap but the quality of ingredients is low and the whole thing was really tasteless. I also tried the fabulous popiah. It was just ok and lacking in complexity of ingredients and crispness. I think I've had better ones in Singapore. The triple layer lava cake - fun to eat but very oily and lacks depth of flavours. I have to agree that the taste and atmosphere here is authentic Malaysian. It's hot, cheap and bustling. Maybe it's still worth one visit just for the experience. But make sure you get there early before lunch because some of the popular stalls did sell out when we got there at 1pm.

author: Jackie
review_text: Managed to score a clean, cool table tucked all the way inside this huge and humid hawker centre near Bunn Choon (egg tarts). Tried the vegetarian laksa as there was no queue. Didn’t taste like the laksa I’m more familiar with and instead had an Indian curry taste.Still, it was rather nice. Uncle’s Fresh Coconut here is a must try! It’s huge, icy and refreshing, and best of all, the metal spoon to scoop the tender sweet flesh at the end of the meal was the best desert on a hot afternoon. The Yong Tao Fu was okay but the freshly made chee cheong fun that went with it - I can eat 5 servings and ask for more. Just a simple drizzle of soy sauce and sesame oil and it’s like so soft yet chewy, light not stodgy like most rice noodles. Heavenly yum yum.

author: The Travel Hunter
review_text:
I recently visited ICC Pudu Food Centre and was thoroughly impressed by the wide variety of authentic local dishes available. Among the many options, I tried the Lala Bee Hoon, Curry Niang You Hu, Hainanese Coffee, and Fried Fish Rice, and every dish left a lasting impression.

The Lala Bee Hoon was light yet flavorful — the clams were fresh, and the broth carried a natural sweetness with a hint of seafood richness. The Curry Niang You Hu stood out for its aromatic, creamy curry and tender stuffed fish pieces, a perfect balance of spice and comfort. The Fried Fish Rice was another highlight — crispy on the outside yet juicy inside, paired beautifully with fragrant rice and sambal. To complete the meal, the Hainanese Coffee was strong, smooth, and perfectly roasted, delivering that classic old-school kopitiam flavor.

What makes ICC Pudu Food Centre truly special is not just the food, but the vibrant atmosphere — a perfect blend of tradition, efficiency, and community spirit. Prices are reasonable, portions are generous, and every stall feels passionate about what they serve. This is truly a five-star destination for anyone who loves authentic Malaysian flavors.

author: Ricky Hwan
review_text:
To anyone who enjoy eating n all kinds of delicious food...Is a must come place...
Is a very crowded place on the weekends n just have to wait for seats...
There's really alot of stores around with lots of delicious food to choose..so is good to walk around first before deciding 😋 on what to eat...

author: Alvin Lim
review_text:
Cheap and good. Just have to bear with the "sauna like" environment.

Amidst the seemingly chaotic vibe,  there is a "system",  like how the cleaners quickly clear up the tables and how the diligent drinks stall workers go around taking orders and delivering the right orders!

There are many many stalls and can be overwhelming but I have my own favourites.  Really enjoyed the yam cake, the steamed promfet fillet and the seafood rice porridge! Also the very yummy spring roll (popiah) with very  nice "textured" filling and cost less than Sgd$1 per roll!

You must walk all the way in and you will find the stalls with the authentic hawker fare.

Also, some of the stalls have very (PRC) kind of sign boards. That's another indication of authenticity of the fare they are offering.

Breakfast hours only (most stalls closed by noon).

For Singaporeans, take note that there is table service and you do not need to return tray! Amazing.

author: James Shiju
review_text: A bustling hotbed for locals here to congregate for breakfast and lunch mainly, due to its large concentration numbers of food stalls offering a wide range of mainly local Chinese local hawker fare. A wide range of choices to select depending on one's inkling. Overall all the ones that I tried were pretty good and authentic. Despite their busyness, the operators were still relatively polite and friendly, partly I supposed due the the competition of a few repeated food type stalls. The ordering system here is self service and pricing is reasonable. I came at a non peak time, and was able to find certain seating spots were more airy at the edge with openings (no hemp in) than those internal spots. I supposed, one would not have such luxury at peak and packed times, as this place is obviously very popular among the locals and visitors. The set up here is quite basic, with the attention focused on the food. I was quite surprised that the floor is just cement screed finished and not tiles for eater facilities, though overall the place is considered quite clean and tidy.

author: Lee Zhao
review_text:
Visited this bustling local hawker center for lunch. The ambiance is classic and busy—lots of energy, plenty of tables, and you get the true experience of local Malaysian food culture here.
The Food: I ordered the Ginger Rice Wine dish with Prawn and Pork (RM13.00).
• Value (3/5): At RM13, the price is a little on the higher side for a hawker stall, so expectations for flavor execution are raised.
• Ingredients (4/5): The ingredients themselves were generous and looked fresh—good portion of sliced pork, decent prawns, and a nice, thick, savory egg gravy.
• Flavor (2/5): This is where it fell short. Despite being a 'Ginger Rice Wine' dish, the dominant, warming, and pungent flavors of the ginger and wine were almost non-existent. The food tasted surprisingly "normal" and lacked the punch and character a signature item should have.

author: Jasper Lei
review_text:
Huge selection of food choices
Pretty great ventilation and over not hot at noon timing

-  YTF was awesome
- Fried fish soup noddle was great w thick yellow wine taste
- Wanton Mee with melt in your mouth charred fatty char siew is heavenly

- Nasi Lemak pretty average with extremely oily fried chicken dripping oil on the rice 😂

author: Chong Yin Koon
review_text:
The Imbi pork noodle kennot.  Too bland and expensive for the quality of pork.  The other stuff like apam balik and keng cheow Hailam coffee are awesome.  I will try the Hailam chicken rice and Teochew fish noodle next time.  Oh yeah, the water here quite dirty.

Service of table kinda slow at times because lack of manpower.   Understandable.

Atmosphere.   Weekday is good (before and after the peak rush hour of lunchtime).  Weekend is overcrowded and hard to find table to sit down and eat.

author: Teng Sook Yin
review_text: First time visited this huge and obviously very popular hawker centre. Very impressed with the variety of food available. Eventhough there was a huge crowd, there was no problem finding a table. We tried the beef noodle and curry noodle Both were good. We bought the dumplings for breakfast the next day. They were very delicious with lots of meat. Yum yum. Will definitely go again, even went round to check which are the popular stalls (with long queues). Haha...

author: pui kuen Yap
review_text: One of my favorite breakfast spot. Simple breakfast make you happy. How ever many people will said ICC is a tourist place but is a good place to have a good foods.

author: tm sii
review_text: A huge food court which is very crowded and humid particularly during weekends, patrons are attracted by the large numbers of stalls offering a wide range of food choices to fulfil one's taste buds. Certainly a place for food lovers who like vibrance and don't mind the heat and queue even for a table. Best to come during week days. Private parking nearby costs RM5 per vehicle.

author: Eason Wong
review_text:
Great choices of local foods and drinks with authentic taste. Must visit place for foodies who want to explore local hawker foods.
The venue cleanliness and hygiene need improvement.

author: Lucas Chan
review_text:
Hawker centre. Nice melting pot for local food, so much variety. Except that there’s no aircon but well ventilated, room temperature. Clean place.
Advisable to come early as it will be crowded during peak hours.

author: darren Chia
review_text:
Great for breakfast and brunch. Most of the popular stalls start early and may sell out before noon, so it’s best to come early. Prices are reasonable, and you get to enjoy hawker food in a cleaner, more comfortable setting . Weekend mornings are crowded, so expect some waiting time or sharing tables.

Overall, ICC Pudu is a must-visit for foodies looking to enjoy classic Malaysian flavors under one roof.

author: Lee Kokliang
review_text: This was the worst tim sum I have eaten. Didn't expect such poor quality. The food was cold, especially the prawn Chee Chong fun which was hard, obviously it was frozen and put to steam for a while. Told staff to re-steam. The chicken feet was hot on the outside but could feel the cold inside. Siew Mai meat was too hard. Won't be back. The staff were busy playing handphones and not interested in work. Anywhere else in Malaysia is better.

author: Ngọc Hải
review_text: nice staff, good food especially hainan chicken rice and milk tea, milo. I want to eat the sticky cake but 8.30am it open and we come in 7am so they dont serve. It may be hot because not all area has air conditioner. Food really cheap at about 30rm for all this but just paid in cash or touchngo wallet no card

author: Sean T
review_text:
ICC Pudu is really a hidden gem for food lovers. The HK roast here is absolutely delicious – the char siew melts in your mouth, tender and flavorful, while the noodles are perfectly bouncy and coated in an awesome sauce that ties everything together (see picture!).

Auntie Mei’s crispy Popiah is another highlight. It’s super crispy on the outside and packed full of fresh, tasty ingredients inside. Every bite gives you that perfect crunch and flavor (see photos).

And don’t miss out on Wang Fatt’s drinks and snacks – the iced Hainan coffee is rich and refreshing, and it pairs so well with their toast bread, which is crispy on the outside and soft inside (see photo).

Overall, ICC Pudu is a fantastic spot to enjoy a variety of delicious local eats all in one place. Highly recommend checking it out if you’re around the area!

author: Eddy Hoo
review_text: The food here seriously is not up to rated ratings. We (me and my family) came here to try out those by food recommended. Seriously, it didn’t come near to what rated. The air quality here is also bad, seems smoky and warm. Means their exhaust ventilation system either is not functioning/ not maintained (services) or the kitchen hood exhaust wasn’t design to cater for this situation. From I can say, it is OVERLY rated. I can understand and agree that everyone has different taste buds. The food taste is normal nothing special but there are many varieties (choices).

author: Tan Adrian
review_text:
I’ve been to KL several times and always wanted to try this place. This time, I finally came with my family and the elderly — but unfortunately, it turned out to be a huge disappointment.

I strongly urge everyone not to order their claypot rice. It completely lacked fragrance and flavour, the rice was bland, and the lap cheong (Chinese sausage) was of poor quality. Honestly, they’re not professional at all in preparing claypot rice — it just didn’t have the authentic taste or aroma expect.

The only saving grace was the sambal stingray and sotong, which were quite decent and had good flavour.

However, the seating area was cramped, making it uncomfortable to dine in, and the staff were unfriendly. Overall, the experience was disappointing from both the food and service side.

Definitely not worth the hype or revisit.

author: HoodlumHavoc Gaming
review_text:
Food is excellent! A must try when visiting KL.
Try the chicken claypot and the grilled fish.
You may be seated outside, and they may have long queue sometimes, depending on day and events.

Not sure but auntie who is like the boss is a little annoying. We were trying to ask for additional spicy sauce or flakes. But she declined and talked to there guy at there language (not sure what they are talking sbout) but it seems they are making fun of our request because the fish sauce is already a little spicy, we just wanted more spice. But it seems they made fun of our request. (But again not sure what they are talking about, i can only be sure that she declined and said no no no).

KL is humid and hot most of the times, so if you are not the person who is comfortable eating outside (humid with street noise, people walking, cars around) this might be uncomfortable for you.

Just be ready when you dine here coz experience is not the usual dining experience.

Lots of options around who offers almost same menu so you may wsnna try others too if you want.

This is our exp, you may have diff exp. Just sharing and being honest

author: Timothy E.
review_text:
One of the best claypot rice in the heart of KL! The flavour, texture and that smoky taste are sooo good.

Also tried their Portuguese grill fish - super tasty and worth a try. Prices are pretty decent too. If you’re around Petaling Street hunting for good food, this spot is a must-try!

author: Manjit Sangha
review_text: Just absolutely brilliant food, like a biryanis but much better. Crispy spicy delight with an egg on top wow, cooked for all to see, fantastic. Had clams and a prawn dish just so fresh and once I stirred the clay pot the rice with crunch and soft texture was divine. 10/10.

author: Dao Viet
review_text: So, the hype was way too much. Hardly any chicken, one lonely slice of Chinese sausage for decoration, and the rice—well, let’s just say it couldn’t decide if it wanted to be cooked or raw. All fame, zero substance. Honestly, it doesn’t even come close to a simple claypot rice you’d find in Saigon’s Chinatown. Final verdict? Worth a try just to say you’ve tried… but once is more than enough.

author: Emily
review_text:
Came here for dinner at 8pm, crowded and had to queue for around 15mins. It was hot and humid. Better bring a portable fan. We ordered a large set, comes with claypot chicken rice, tomyam seafood platter (added petai for rm5), stir fry vege with bean sprouts and a peanut soup. Also ordered 3 drinks, coconut, honey lemon & lemon juice.

Total bill was RM113. Overall, it wasn't that great, just average. The only thing special here was this shop only opens at night. Will I come back here to eat? Nah, but you could come try it and just get to the touristy feel of having local food.

author: Siewyen Ng
review_text: Claypot rice is nice and tasty. Grilled lala and stingray not so nice. Food serving is fast. Staff not so friendly and need to sit outdoor.

author: Grace Tay
review_text: It was average… we ordered medium claypot rice with vegetables as sides. The queue moved fast, and we also got our food rather quickly. However it’s not very memorable ; grilled stingray were available too but we didn’t order

author: Beatrice Zhang
review_text:
Food was average, the service was too bad. The queue was long, we waited around 20 minutes to be seated. The staffs were really loud. We consisted of 9 person so they needed to combine the tables for us but one of the owner slamed the chair for us instead of putting them nicely.

It was raining heavily. Then one of the staff tried to adjust the tent roof right above where we sat and splashed water right to my friend. He didn’t wait for us to finish eating to adjust it, nor did he apologized afterwards. Another staff apologized for his behalf instead. The owner just laughed and didn’t say anything to us.

Definitely not recommended.

author: Simon Koo
review_text: Great food and prompt service. Ordered the claypot chicken rice for 2-3 pax and a stir fried vege. The small piece of salted fish adds aroma  to the claypot. Take note that it's more hawker style with functional table and chairs, Not for those who prefer restaurant style settings.

author: Evan L
review_text:
We noticed someone reviewed that they had to wait 20 minutes for their claypot rice. Honestly, we would’ve happily waited that long, usually that’s a good sign the rice is cooked fresh in the claypot, not just pre-cooked rice with some raw chicken thrown in.

But sadly, that wasn’t what we got. There was no crispy, crusty rice at the bottom, which usually means they probably used pre-cooked rice. On top of that, the rice didn’t have much flavour, even though they poured quite a lot of dark soy sauce over it.

We ordered the medium-sized claypot (RM25, June 2025) but only got a few small pieces of chicken and just a couple of thin slices of Chinese sausage - it felt a bit stingy. The server didn’t even ask if we wanted salted fish, which we thought was usually part of a proper claypot rice. She only asked if we wanted to add an egg.

Overall, the claypot rice just didn’t live up to expectations. It seems like the place is more popular with tourists than for the quality of the food. They did have other options like BBQ stingray, but we didn’t try those.

author: Eugene Chia
review_text:
You have to Q and order outside before they seat you.
The food came faily fast around 5 minutes.
The Claypot chicken rice with lap cheong is fragrant and the taste is ok.
1 sour plum drink + mix vege small + Medium claypot chicken rice rm38
Reasonable la d price in a touristy area.

author: Magga Andika
review_text: I ordered claypot chicken rice, but sadly it wasn’t served hot. Looks like the rice was pre-cooked and just reheated with the chicken. The flavor didn’t come out as it should, and even the egg took quite a long time to cook.

author: BeerBiie WCK
review_text:
The Portuguese grilled fish was quite good, with a lovely aroma of chili oil and spices. I ordered the stingray, and it tasted excellent, and the squid was fresh. This menu I recommend.

For the clay pot menu, I recommend adding Chinese sausage (gunchiang). The sweetness of the sausage perfectly balances the savory flavors.

As for the vegetable dishes, I found them a bit bland.

author: Yan Wai Wong
review_text:
Came here on a Sat night 10pm. A little of a queue.
Im surprised by the crowd.
Spent RM60

Claypot rice turned out super underwhelming. Didnt taste any salted fish at all. Rice did not have flavour. Rice not very charred. Please do not bother to try this place.
The veg was ok, seafood was so-so.

author: Chef’s
review_text: I can’t say this is the best claypot rice, but the chicken marinate with favourite is amazing, juicy and tasty make me keep going well with the rice.

author: Voon Wong
review_text: Hong Kee Claypot Chicken Rice in KL’s Chinatown is known for its signature claypot chicken rice, best enjoyed with Chinese sausage and a crispy, charred rice bottom. Cooked over a charcoal fire, the dish has a smoky aroma that enhances the tender, flavorful chicken. Pair it with their refreshing grass jelly drink for a classic combo. While some diners praise the rich flavors, others note inconsistencies in the rice texture and service. The no-frills eatery offers both outdoor and air-conditioned seating, making it a convenient stop for a traditional meal in the heart of KL.

author: Meera Nair
review_text: Finally tried Hong Kee Claypot Chicken after having it on my list. The claypot rice was decent, though I personally prefer a stronger char. Not something I’d go out of my way for, but it’s a good late-night option since they’re open till 11pm.

author: Ngọc Nga Hồ Trương
review_text: First time visiting Hong Kee and the claypot chicken really impressed me — so flavorful and delicious! Definitely coming back for more! 😋

author: Benjamin Wenisch
review_text:
I having a business trip and stay around this area, It was very crowded the first night, and I tested it on the 2nd night.

Apart from tourist spots, and it use charcoal to cook, taste is just 3/10. Nothing special.

The workers try to scam me when they come to collect money, show me a paper written RM34, after questions them, show me another paper written RM19.

Overall it was a good experience, but no next time, consider an overrated food stall.

author: Will Tan
review_text:
Food: 5/5 Stars
Fried chicken was almost impeccable, truly crispy outside and tender inside. Rice was fragrant and well cooked, with peanuts and anchovies just nicely fried, as well as the fresh yet chilling cucumbers. Of course the mouth-watering sambal was the soul of the whole cuisine. Surprisingly, not thirsty after the meal. Highly recommended!

Environment: 3/5 Stars
The seating arrangement was quite congested and pretty noisy. However, overall it was clean, neat and cosy.

Service: 2/5 Stars
Dishes serving was swift. However, waiters were impatient and didnt bother to explain too much about the menu. Also kept rushing us to pay the bill even before we finished the food.

Parking: 1/5 Star
Extremely difficult to find parking around.

Price: 4/5 Stars
Prices were reasonable, and only subject to SST (no extra 10% service charge).

Overall: 3/5 Stars

author: Siti Fairuz
review_text:
Finally made the trip to Village Park in Uptown! The famous Nasi Lemak definitely lives up to the hype—it is perfectly balanced. The sambal isn't too spicy, sweet, or salty; it sits right in the middle and pairs perfectly with the rice and fried chicken.

We also ordered the Rendang Kerang (cockles) to share, which was amazing and had a really balanced taste as well. The Kaya Toast and soft-boiled eggs were standard, a decent add-on if you want variety.

I arrived around 11:30 AM and the queue took about 15–30 minutes, but it was absolutely worth the wait. Despite the crowd, the service is efficient and the food arrives very fast. Highly recommended!

author: Enzo Wong
review_text:
All the hype for nasi lemak is basically alright.
The chicken is not so tender which is easy to eat and taste good with the crips and spices they use. Sambal is very lemak. Rice is normal with spices. The price is surprisingly reasonable on normal hours. Serving is fast.

Downside i guess is that the place will be packed with people.

If you’re like me who likes spicy nasi lemak, maybe this is not for you.

author: Marcus Goh
review_text:
This restaurant is highly rated, so I took a taxi there to try it when I had some time.

Their Nasi Lemak is very famous, it is their signature dish.
Rice is fragrant and rich, yet fluffy and not too greasy.
The rice has a subtle coconut milk aroma.

The chicken is fried to a perfect crisp, with a crispy bits sprinkled with spices.
The meat inside is still juicy and tender.
The chicken is rich in spice flavor and pairs perfectly with the Nasi Lemak.
The portions are generous and the prices are reasonable.

The menu doesn't just include Nasi Lemak.
There are other options such as noodles and bread to suit different tastes.

Service is relatively fast, especially when taking orders and serving food.

The restaurant is clean and bright.
Because it's very popular, there's often a queue.
There are many tables, but it can get crowded.
You likely have to share a table with strangers.

The location isn't very convenient and not near city; need to take a taxi to get there.

author: The WAT31
review_text: Staff is very helpful and attentive, ensuring we get a seat quickly and food too. The nasi lemak rice is fluffy and fragrant, each bite is mouth watering. The cutleries, came warm - which is very surprising and showcases high standards to customer, brilliant! The fried chicken is packed with flavour, each bite crispy while tasty, wanting me to keep eating it. However, the sambal was not to my preference as it was too sweet, maybe give us some spicy sambal too? Customer service and food are very satisfactory which hence explains the 5 star.

author: Lim SC
review_text: Finally visited the talk of the city when coming to nasi lemak. Anticipated the queue and crowd even at 11am Friday working day. However queue moved fast. Service was prompt. The nasi lemak was good, sambal too. Fried chicken was crispy outside tender inside. The only little weak was the atmosphere - tight sitting places to cater for the crowd. Be prepared to seat with strangers on the same table. Well what to compliant as sharing table with stranger is an norm in Malaysia street food culture.

author: Winnie Quek
review_text: Not a nasi lemak person but I thoroughly enjoyed the food! Tried both kambing and ayam. Ayam wins hands down! The chicken is tender and flavourful, combined with the soft and fluffy rice makes it really good indeed. Would recommend changing the hard boiled egg to sunny side up.

author: Bernard
review_text:
Woke up early one sunday morning just to make a trip to this famous restaurant, for a plate of their signature Nasi Lemak and its worth our effort.

Plate of fragrant rice arrived fluffy with each grain clearly separated yet still
moist - not sticky or soggy, and lightly infused with coconut milk and pandan.

The star was the Fried Chicken - A whole golden-brown leg, its skin shatteringly crisp with flecks of spiced crumbs, while the lightly seasoned meat inside stays tender and juicy. The sambal glossy and rich, tying the rice and chicken together beautifully.

On the side, crunchy ikan bilis and peanuts provide that addictive bite, while the egg balances the richness. It’s a plate that feels generous, comforting, and bold all at once for us.

We ordered their Fried Noodles and Bee Hoon as well, and although they were
not signature dishes, both were well fried and balance in flavours.

We didnt like their Bagadil and Potato Curry Puff (Pastry was ok, but fillings had an overwhelming turmeric flavour) though.

Overall, we will return just their Nasi Lemak and Ayam Goreng, next time round when in KL again. Good to reach before 8am on Sunday, as we did not encounter any queue and found seats immediately by ourselves as no service staffs attended to us, due to full capacity.

However, its better to approach their service staffs for seats, as ordering procedures are rather confusing after that.

author: Chung Cheong Wong
review_text:
Very nice Nasi Lemak! Fried chicken drumstick is juicy and tender. The best is the sambal chilli. Not too spicy and have a fragrant aroma of spices.

Service is very fast despite the crowd.

author: Ryan
review_text:
Simply the best nasi lemak I’ve ever had. I genuinely struggled to pick the best item on the plate because everything was close to perfection. The fried chicken was juicy and seasoned beautifully. The coconut rice was fluffy, with distinct grains and the perfect fragrance; neither too heavy nor too light.

And the sambal, often overly sweet in many KL spots, hit the perfect balance of sweetness and spiciness. Absolutely worth the hype (and the queue… though thankfully there wasn’t one on a Monday at 1:30pm!).

A definite must-try when you’re in KL. Solid 9/10.

author: JYH
review_text:
We were mentally prepared for a long queue, but to our surprise, we got a table in less than 20 minutes! Perhaps the restaurant has expanded — there are definitely more seats now.
Despite the crowd, both the ordering and serving were impressively efficient — definitely worth a thumbs-up! 👍
Every dish we ordered was delicious, and the drinks were great too. Very satisfying overall, and the prices are reasonable.
The only downside is that they don’t accept e-wallet payments.

author: dedi berlian
review_text: I visited the restaurant during lunch time.  I was quite packed  with people queuing up.  The wait was not long.   I love seeing a crowd in the restaurant. Nasi lemak was delicious and  the fried chicken was juicy and tender. The  sambal is sweet  and spicy.  Nice.

author: Bryan Goh
review_text:
The nasi lemak is very very good. It’s worth travelling out to try it.
The nasi lemak can be had with fried chicken, which is their signature, and crispy on the outside and succulent on the inside. The sambal is sweet and spicy and really delicious.
The rendang is also very good.

author: Farrel Arkananta
review_text:
One of the best nasi lemak I had in KL. Fluffy and flavorful rice, the chicken tastes very rich, the sambal was perfectly balanced, just a really great experience.

Definitely worth the hype. Cues may be long, could be 20-30 mins of wait time.

author: Ivan Cheok
review_text:
@Food
Signature / Best selling Food - Nasi Lemak Ayam Goreng
Food Tasted - Nasi Lemak Ayam Goreng, Nasi Lemak Ayam Rendang
Recommend - Nasi Lemak Ayam Goreng 👍👍👍
Portion - Good, reasonable portion
Taste -  Excellent, aromatic coconut milk rice match with crispy quarter chicken and the famous sambal. The best Nasi Lemak I have so far 😍

@Shop
Cleanliness - Good, they install air purifier to ensure clean air in restaurant
Service - Fast (*When you're seated and need call out for order, sometimes waitor is overwhelming with crowded customer)
Price - Reasonable, RM 13 for good quality single portion of Nasi Lemak
Payment - **CASH or CARD ONLY

@Experience
Last visit - 01/11/25 at 8.30am
Number of Visit - Once a while, been here a few times.
Personal Note - The restaurant upgraded to 4 shoplot of dining area space so I observe less people queue outside. Better experience for customer. 👍

author: Fredy Lim
review_text:
At last, I have the opportunity to taste one of the finest Nasi Lemak in KL.

The nasi lemak featuring the deep-fried drumstick was incredibly tender and tasty. The sambal chili had perfect flavor and spiciness.

I was informed that sambal cuttlefish is also good and comes in large servings, but it was unavailable when I got there.

The morning was already busy with numerous food delivery drivers waiting to pick up their orders. The orders clearly show me its popularity.

One should anticipate waiting at least an hour in line during lunchtime...

The hours of operation are daily from 6:30 am to 5:30 pm.

author: Guanny G
review_text:
Finally got a chance to try this place, recommended as a top Nasi Lemak in town.

Place is crowded despite the rain and early morning for a weekday. Queue can be challenging for peak period and weekend.

Food is ordered at the table.

Taste wise, rice is fragrant and well cooked with coconut milk. The fried fish and ayam rempah was dry unfortunately. Overall, just ok ....

author: Pablo Peralta Palacios
review_text:
A local legend in KL (or PJ, whatever) serving traditional Malaysian dish, Nasi Lemak.

The place was CROWDED big time. But we still managed to get a seat and set the order for the famous NL straight away. I guess the usual would be to queue like they love here in Malaysia — national sport 🇲🇾.

So after 20/30 minutes we have the NL finally in our face (makes sense given the sheer amount of orang2).

Altho I’ve had a grand total of one (1) Nasi Lemaks in my life I would say this one is the best. And the reason is because of their fried chicken, which really was excellent.

My girlfriend (indonesian) thought the sambal was too sweet; maybe yeah but I still liked it.

author: Chien Min Tan
review_text:
After 10 over years, this is still the best nasi lemak we can have in town.
Good atmosphere with airconditioned, and well placing seat.

Waiting time is usually 15-30mins

Fried chicken is always consistent with crispy skin and tender meat, sambal is always on point.
Not forgetting the ikan bilis and kacang always fresh!

The only downside of here is the parking, but Starling Mall will be a good alternative for parking without the worry of getting summon

author: Abe R
review_text:
It was a Sunday outing and we did expect the crowd.
The Nasi Lemak:
1. Love the fragrance rice
2. Sambal was my kind of sambal. Well balance between sweet spicy.
3. Chicken - mama'mia lovely.

The table setting :
It's a mess. All the tables are squash to max the capacity which made it stuffy. I said that because if your next neighbour fart, you will be blessed with whatever aroma definitely. 🤣🤣🤣
So as much as I ❤️ the taste of your Nasi Lemak, if i suddenly crave for it, I will only grab food them to unsure the survival of my Nose

author: Tâm Như Trần Nhật
review_text:
I came here to try the famous giant roti tissue with sweet condensed milk sauce, and it was pretty good. However, I recommend coming with at least one other person because the portion is huge and can get a bit boring if you eat it alone. Since I was by myself, it felt like too much.

The food came out super fast. The price isn’t exactly cheap, but it’s still reasonable for the experience. I also tried the “masala tea,” but for me it wasn’t that impressive.

Overall, I’d give this place a solid 4 out of 5.

author: Thomas Tam
review_text:
Roti tisu was okay - it’s just big. Parts of it were too hard and chewy for my liking but overall alright for the price. Not served with nearly enough condensed milk for the size I think.

Curries were tasty but expensive.

Watermelon juice was not very sweet - either unripe fruit or watered down. I’d maybe avoid the fresh juices if you come here.

author: CHIN HOWE Tang (Howe)
review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️

Tried TG’s Bistro and ordered the **roti tisu**. The presentation looked nice and crispy, but the taste was just average — not so sweet . Service was okay and the place was quite casual, but nothing particularly stood out. Overall, a decent spot if you’re nearby, but not something I’d go out of my way for.

author: Efsun Peynirci
review_text: I had garlic bread and ginger milk tea here — both were absolutely delicious! I had my breakfast at this place, and the ginger milk tea was especially amazing. Prices are also quite reasonable. It’s located just behind Kuala Lumpur’s famous street food area and is very central. Definitely worth a visit!

author: Ngọc Hải
review_text: we came because the giant cake and it really funny and suitable for taking photos. The milk tea is super delicious but garlic chicken really dried, the giant cake is not suitable for eating hic. The nasi noodles over salty that we cant eat. Luckily the staff really nice and they acp to paid by card

author: Ashavina Arulkumar
review_text: Tried the cheese naan this time around with fresh coconut water, and it was SO good. This is my family’s go-to place for dinner or for supper as it has a very nice atmosphere and the food is really good. Service here is also top notch.

author: KK
review_text: Hot n stuffy inside the restaurant. No air con inside: Poor service. Famous for their tall roti tissue. Full of China chinese. Always got queue. Prepare for long wait for food

author: GK
review_text: Ordered garlic Roti Canai and plain roti canai. Customers came after me was served before me. The curry was extremely diluted and watery. All the staff had savour long face. While being seated on the table having coffee one of the staff was mopping the floor hit the table leg which I was seated on and did not even bother to say sorry. He completely ignored and went on mopping like nothing happened. When my food was late as I asked I was not given proper response. They were all seated just giving hand signals tht food is coming with sulky face. Went to pay at the cashier. The guy collected the card keyed in the price n chucked the card in front of me with sulky face. Went there at 5am on 26th Sept 2025.

author: Our_Discoveries5
review_text: My experience at TG’s Bistro was excellent, and it’s one of the best options in Bukit Bintang for tasty, quick, and affordable meals. The restaurant offers a wide variety of Indian and Malaysian dishes such as roti, biryani, and masala — all fresh, flavorful, and satisfying. I tried the cheesy roti, and it was delicious, especially with the accompanying sauces. The atmosphere is simple and casual, and despite being busy, the place is clean and well-organized. The service is fast, friendly, and the staff are very helpful. Being open 24/7 makes it a perfect spot for late-breakfast, dinner, or a quick meal anytime. A great experience overall, and I would absolutely come back again.

author: Peter Tudor
review_text:
I was recommended to go here from someone at mu hostel and so glad they did. Garlic naan was greating the chicken and rice was OK. Staff were friendly and helped me out ordering.
Would go again if I was in KL.

author: Ellie Oh
review_text:
🥘✨ TG’s Bistro – the place where Indian food meets viral Instagram trends!
Let’s be real—I came for the Roti Tissue, and yes, it was all drama and zero flavor 😅
Super photogenic, but definitely not the highlight taste-wise.

BUT… the butter chicken? Absolutely soft and melt-in-your-mouth. So flavorful I almost forgave the portion size (yeah, it’s a bit small).

🧄🧀 Also obsessed with their cheese garlic naan—fluffy, fragrant, and the perfect sidekick to all the curries.

If you're looking for viral-worthy dishes and solid Indian staples, this place knows the balance.

📸 Pro tip: Snap the Roti Tissue for the ‘Gram, then devour the butter chicken for your soul.

#TGsBistro #RotiTissueTrend #ButterChickenGoals #KualaLumpurEats #ellies.taste

author: Francois Cournil
review_text: Good breakfast with friendly and efficient service. I had the cheese roti option A and it was delicious. Recommended.

author: Michel Cheung
review_text: Really good place to visit in Malaysia. Decent price that is no overpriced due the viral moment. Really recommend this place. Definitely will come again on my next vacation. Staffs are very friendly.  To avoid line up come before 12pm or it will be cloudy and needed to wait in queue.

author: Johnny Tan
review_text:
Ordered the nasi chicken ayam goreng. The curries were decent. But the chicken was bone dry. Pass.

Also tried the Two Veg + garlic Naan. The naan was fresh and hot but everything else was lukewarm. Cabbage was decent. Potatoes were decent. But then, the naan turned hard after just a few minutes. Naan should stay soft for more than 5 minutes.

Overall, very average food. But good price.
Would not come back.

author: Tom Lloyd
review_text:
this is a classic malaysian indian mamak restaurant place. Serving great range of nasi kandar, best to go up get rice and pick what you like the look of to accompany your rice. I had some beef curry, brinjal (eggplant) and veg curry with biryani rice. tasty and cheap.
It seems as though this place has become internet famous in China for their roti tissue dish, with many young tourists coming to order this and take photos, so it can often be busy currently. By only trying out the large photo oppurtunity of roti tissue, you will miss o it on the many traditional excellent options of nasi kandar and other dishes they do have available here!

author: Faith
review_text: Had the roti telur and Teh tarik here. The roti canai was not as crispy as I would like, but the curry was tasty. The Teh tarik was good and not too sweet. Shop is v busy with alot of tourists.

author: Md Rijwan Razzaq Matin
review_text: The food was below par, but the drinks were the real disaster. We ordered teh panas and nesacafe ais — the most basic drinks you’d expect any mamak to get right. Instead, what we got was so diluted and poorly made that it was practically undrinkable. If a mamak can’t even handle the basics like teh panas and nesacafe ais, it’s not worth anyone’s time or money.

author: Fotoxer WU
review_text:
Here’s a lot of Chinese people here eating the Indian food here I guess because of the long pancake there.
Well, you can take a special photo here with the long pancake , and your owner is very ambitious and very kind to show you how to eat.
They taste like normal Indian food I like it but the rice could be much better

author: Fereşhte M
review_text: It's totally a Chinese vibe to come to this place and take a picture with the The longest roti tissue. 1 meter. As a non-Chinese, who is a friend with Chinese, i just cannot understand about getting a place famous without any especial taste of food. From my point of view, It's totally normal. The restaurant and roti.. but if you're Chinese and have a "red book" app, maybe you have to try it and take a picture ;)

author: Rob Verheyen
review_text: Sorry to be negative again after a bad experience in Jalan Alor a few days back. We had a good meal here a couple of years ago so we came back on this trip. This time, it was no good, not as disastrous as on Jalan Alor, but still no good. The curries were just bland, underseasoned, tasteless. They had a slimy consistency because of the thickener added. The naan was poor, too. It all had little to do with Indian food except the names of the dishes. Is there a new owner or just a new concept? Serve cheap food to ignorant foreigners on a budget who don't appreciate real food anyway? The place obviously tries to reduce costs where ever it can, even going so far as to not place condiments or even a box of tissues on the table - if you ask for some, the waiter comes and hands you one or two tissues. Service was indifferent. An okay place to sit though, relatively quiet. And owner: please don't react to this. I'm sure no-one is waiting to read your arrogant comments to negative reviews.

author: Wai Yee Leong
review_text:
We ordered the chicken kuey teow soup and dry curry chicken mee. Go early, before 8am, or the waiting time gets very long.
The chicken kuey teow soup had smooth, silky kuey teow and a light prawn fragrance in the soup. However, the soup portion was quite little and slightly cold when served, likely because the noodles are cooked in batches.
The dry curry chicken mee was good. I liked the mint and curry combination, and the calamansi worked well with the curry. The pork ball and fishballs also are recommended! Very tasty, and bouncy.
Waiting time was around 1 hour. After eating the dry curry noodles, the chicken kuey teow soup tasted quite mild in comparison. The service is good as the waitress are attentive.
Personally, if the waiting time is around 1 hour, I wouldn’t come back.

author: Evelyn
review_text: My family and I arrived at around 7.30am for breakfast on a Friday but the kai si hor fun broth was not ready so, we sat down and waited for some time. Overall, everything is good. I had dry chicken curry noodle from another stall, curry gravy was on the sweet side. Nevertheless, the taste was ok.

author: SP
review_text:
Finally got a chance to try the kai si hor fun here. It was... underwhelming. The dry curry noodle was good though.

Arrived at 7:30am and there were throngs of customers seated, waiting for the hor fun and curry noodle stall to start cooking. We waited 45 minutes for our noodles as there were about 50+ other customers waiting.

The kai si hor fun looked great when it arrived but something's amiss - soup was only half bowl, barely enough to cover its noodles. A flip of the hor fun to mix, there was hardly 5cm of broth. Really stingy and the soup was warm - must be due to mass cooking before serving.

The soup tasted rich with a strong taste of prawn. Hor fun as default in Ipoh, is smooth as silk. We ordered extra sides of pork and fish ball and they were great - bouncy texture and rich flavours.

But if I were to rate the kai si hor fun - it is 3 of 5 stars only. Because it was served warm, and wasn't enough soup.

Their dry curry chicken noodle was good though - right level of gravy thickness and kick of spiciness. Add lime, and its tanginess elevates the overall taste of the dish. I would rate it as 5 of 5.

Would I come back for kai si hor fun? Nope. Dry curry noodles? Maybe if the wait is shorter.

author: Sean Sean
review_text:
Deducted points from them as they aunty forgot my order. We came at 730am and she asked for my order and we were the first customer.. She mention that the soup will only start at 8am so we waited patiently. By 8qm, the place is already quite full ( like 20tables).

When at 8 am, I noticed the aunty started serving 2 other tables that came after us. I firmly complained about it, and she released she has mixed up the order. Eventually, we became the fourth customer to be served, even though we were first on the order.

Soup bass for ipoh hor fun is ok n curry noodle is also ok for me. No wow. It's above average I guess, since so many people come here

author: TK
review_text:
It’s a nice place situated in the housing area serving mostly the locals. It’s spacious and not stuffy.

I ordered the Chee Cheong Fan with pork… it’s flavorful and smooth. Recommended.

Their famous dry curry noodle… it’s amazingly delicious but you have got to wait (15-20 mins).

Kopi C is also very good.

author: chanvk
review_text:
The broth for the kai see horfun was very flavourful. You can taste the prawn and chicken stock in the broth.
The 'dry' curry chicken mee was thick and rich. The calamansi provided, add an extra tangy kick to the taste.
The fishball was spongy and tasty.
Too bad the stall do not have any bean sprout as a side dish. It would have been a perfect meal if there was.

author: Red Eve
review_text:
Had their famous signature 'Kai See Hor Fun' and was certainly worth the wait. The noodles were soft and silky while the broth was rich with flavour. One of the best that I've tried in Ipoh.
The curry noodles were average while the Chee Cheong Fun was below standard. Next round I'll just order the 'Kai See Hor Fun'.
Do note that they are closed on Mondays and Tuesdays and waiting is definitely a must.

author: Boey Cheah
review_text: This food court rose to popularity mainly because of the Gei C Hor Fun stall. While the noodles were decent, the wait was long and the soup portion rather small — overall not bad, but not particularly impressive given the queue time. We also tried the char kuey teow and the Hong Kong–style chee cheong fun. The chee cheong fun was smooth with a flavorful soy sauce base, while the char kuey teow could have been better if it were cooked a little drier.

author: CarolineN (PJbabe)
review_text: Had waited an hour to get my food. First time tasting their kai si hor fun and dry curry mee. The food was tasty. But to wait 1 hr? I would give it a miss if there is a next time in Ipoh. Can find almost equivalent in kl with shorter waiting time

author: Alfie Hood-Nguyen
review_text: Amazing, comforting bowl of chicken and prawn kway teow soup (hor fun), friendly staff and very reasonably priced! If you don’t want the hor fun there are other yummy looking meals to choose from other vendors there. Highly recommend!

author: Teng K.H. [simone food.channel]
review_text: It is like a small food court but the attention would be at the shop selling hor fun and curry noodle. Usually pack during peak hour, shop already full at their opening hour at 7.30am. The hor fun texture is great, smooth and soft, the broth is slightly sweet, lack of other complex flavor. The fishball was ok. I think their top seller is their dry curry noodle which we would try next time.

author: Bob Carey
review_text:
I went to ipoh for a holiday and decided to eat here.

lets just say i prefer the Teh C more.

the horfun was quite average not suprising.
and yet its overhyped with alot of people.

the broth was questionable like something is up
the noodle had a weird texture
the.. chicken. doesnt taste right like something

so i would rarely come to this when i go to ipoh again.

im heavily dissapointed on the horfun and i will never order it again.

author: Kenkeh Hi
review_text: The sar hor fun noodle 🍜 here is tasty . Visited Thursday morning 9am . I don’t have to wait very long on weekdays . They give less soup , but you can ask to add more soup . Broth is intense .

author: Lai Meng
review_text:
Super soft red bean bun. The vegetables ccf was soft and silky. Nice chicken and prawn horfun, too. Coffee was good. Staff were pleasant.

However, the restoran makes no effort to inform or through means of a notice to notify patrons on days it is closed. The lack of regard for patrons reflects poorly of the restoran. Unreliable.

author: Lazy Human
review_text: Well, don't expect service or the environment to be good. But just come here because their chicken hor fan is the best I have ever eaten. The broth, the fragrance is exceptional and please drink it all. The dry curry noodle is a must try.

author: simone food.channel
review_text:
[can try le]
1) Overall - Chinese hawker store, long wait for chicken hor fun, do go in the morning, ok service and cleanliness, food and drink selection are chicken hor fun, curry mee, dry curry mee, chee cheong fun, chicken rice noodle, kuey teow soup and more from Restoran Moon De Moon
2) chicken hor fun with fish ball - soft and smooth noodle, sweet prawn and chicken broth. tasted good. fish ball was ok.

author: jeremy cho
review_text:
Legendary Ipoh Chicken Hor fun and chicken curry mee. The wait times varies from 30 -60 mins depending on dates and timings. They often sell out by 1030hrs.

The horfun is silky smooth and just goes down like butter through your mouth. The broth is thick and flavourful. The curry is in my opinion one the best in South east Asia as a condiment to a bowl of noodles. If you are too full, you can just order curry chicken to go with your hor fun.

They deserve 5 stars and more and naysayers about price etc sadly miss the bigger picture.

author: Mark
review_text: Good chicken kuei tiao soup, great broth, nice flavour.  Must come early (by 11am) or they run out.  Curry Mee also very nice as well as dry chicken kuei tiao.  A good addition to the Ipoh food circuit.

author: K.W. Ng
review_text: Yes, their chicken hor fun is very good. One of the best in Ipoh. No regret eating here. Pls come before 12 noon, as other stall start close down at 12. The white coffee here also authentic, taste is very kaw, definitely worth the try. Chicken hor fun soup is thick and full of taste, not like other shop. Definitely a 5 star for the chicken hor fun.

author: Scenic Routes
review_text:
The second time I came here, I tried their 鸡丝河粉 for the first time. This time, I came to try their famous 干咖喱面, and they were really delicious. I'm giving it four stars because the food took quite a while. We arrived around 10:30am, and it wasn't until close to 11:20am that all the food was served, especially the 干咖喱面 took too long to arrive. However, the food was worth the wait.

I personally prefer their 鸡丝河粉, but their 干咖喱面 are also worth trying. As for the tea, fish balls, and other stalls, I find the food to be average.

I've heard that the 烧肉here is also delicious, but it was already sold out when I came here twice. Hopefully, I can try it on my third visit. If you want to try all their food, make sure to come early.

author: SeeYan Wong
review_text: We had our late lunch there so there was ample of parking space on the street. When I first stepped into the restaurant, the cold air and the majestic decoration welcomed me. I thought the food would be very pricey but it ended up satisfying and reasonable. We ordered mostly the small portion but it wasn't as small as we assumed. The portion was quite big. In addition, the taste suited each of us well.

author: Lim CY
review_text: We visit the restaurant from time to time. The food is decent, though it tends to be on the oily, salty side with heavier flavours, quite typical of some Chinese dishes, I think. It’s the kind of indulgence that’s nice once in a while, hits the spot.

author: Jessen Tan
review_text: Overall food ordered is delicious. Huge portion with reasonable price. Not as spicy as others which ia a good thing. Ample seating area and nice environment.

author: J-Ho S. C.
review_text:
A very luxurious environment to enjoy dimsum!

Reasonable price.

Must try those special items.
Normal dimsum still can improve.
The good part, they wave the tax!

The service really must improve.
Came weekday, waited 30 minutes before being serve the food ordered.

Limited car park.

author: Sook Hwa
review_text: Went there on a weekday morning for breakfast. Not many customers yet service is slow. The decor was nice. Limited dim sum options with a few other fried rice and noodle soup options. Initially when we placed order, the staff didn't inform us there's no fried noodles available. When we add more orders, it took half an hour for the additional orders to arrive. If u have no time to loose, better not come here. Only 30% discount is a plus point, food is only average. Dimsum in ipoh and kl is much better.

author: Cher Ong
review_text: I've always loved their food, but this is the 1st time trying their dim sum. Quite a lot of choices & they only steam it when u order. So u have to be patient while waiting. It takes quite some time for your food to be served. Their price range is very reasonable & the best part is they have 30% discount on your total bill before 11 am. That makes it really cheap. Quality & tastes are quite good. The atmosphere is beautiful & comfortable. A relaxing breakfast spot.

author: Wong Yeanling
review_text: The private room service is fine, it is equipped with karaoke system and a private toilet. However, they do not provide change plate service after the dish, and there is no place to put the bones after eating. The food is nice and creative presentation.

author: Ts. Chin (jcstudio.com)
review_text:
**Tangshan Cuisine (唐山美食) in Prai offers authentic Northern Chinese flavors, distinct from Penang’s usual Cantonese or Hokkien fare. Specialties include:
- **Tangshan Dumplings (唐山饺子)** – Thick, handmade skins with juicy fillings.
- **Lanzhou Hand-Pulled Noodles (兰州拉面)** – Chewy noodles in rich beef broth.
- **Savory Pancakes (煎饼)** – Crispy yet fluffy, stuffed with eggs and scallions.

**Unique Traits:**
- Less sweet, more wheat-based (noodles, buns) compared to Southern Chinese cuisine.
- Bold flavors with garlic, vinegar, and cumin, unlike local Malay or Nyonya dishes.
Although its  viral extremely in sosial media, but if you bring your family, please pay extremely 300% patience, the food you order very slowmo to deliver, some need wait untill  more than 20 minutes, only can enjoy food.
This my first visit, hoping that not my last visit.

author: Jiun Yuen Teh (Brandon)
review_text: Great atmosphere but super slow service. Took 30 minutes for dim sum to serve (only 3 tables in the restaurant at that time). If you don't have patience, this place doesn't suit you.

author: Chloe - Recommend
review_text:
The ambience is absolutely stunning. Good to bring family and friends here for celebration. They even have birthday placard and play birthday songs for birthday.

Taste wise some are better, some are not as good. Porridge is not bad, crispy shrimp roll and leek shrimp paste are also good.

However, we are not happy as we placed order since 11.17am but they only deliver one dish. Upon checking with them, the waitress immediately said that for dim sum needs to wait for at least 15 minutes but it was already way more than 15 minutes. Another lady then came to us and said their kitchen only receive one order and not the remaining orders. We waited until over 12pm (about 50min) for the remaining dishes to arrive. Quite disappointed as they don’t sound apologetic at all. Nor the cashier apologise for that. Overall the service level is bad. Completely lack of customer service skill.

author: Sess L
review_text: The restaurant looks very grand in oriental design. Feels like being transformed into olden China the moment we stepped into the restaurant. The food we ordered were mainly spicy but very traditional Chinese flavour.

author: Kee Kelven
review_text: This restaurant has probably the most stunning decoration I've ever seen. The huge wall painting of mountains and the Great Wall of China is just amazing. We were also satisfied with their authentic Chinese food. We had breakfast here, so we ordered dim sum, which was freshly made to order. We also tried their noodles and porridge, which were fresh and flavorful. However, I wish they could speed up the service, as we waited quite a long time for our food, even though it wasn’t busy and there were only a few tables occupied on a Thursday morning.

author: kk teoh
review_text:
I believe the place offers dinners and lunch for the noon and evening/night crowd, but for breakfast, they have dim sum.  Plenty of parking along the street and very convenient, and the shop is located near a popular food court (Fresh Food Food Court).  The interior of the place is beautifully decorated with chandeliers, large painting, a stage, and even a swing, presumably used for wedding dinners and other events too.

We were there for dim sum though and it currently has an offer of 30% off before 11am on weekdays.

For tea, we had tieguanyin, which was pretty good, though the typical Chinese tea pots and cups would be a nicer touch compared to the metal teapot and cups used.

We ordered a number of dumpling baskets and fried food, which were all steamed on order.  So, expect the food to take a while to reach the table.  Having said that, taste wise, they were generally quite delicious.  Portions are fine and the shrimps used were succulent and firm.  We thought the steamed cheong fun, xiao long pau and loh mai kai were average though.  The frog porridge was presented in a small claypot but good enough for 3 to share.

A note that you can also buy frozen dim sums/dumplings to bring home to steam from a freezer near the counter.

Overall, with the discount, it is a worth another visit in the future.

author: Wenliang Ooi
review_text: Overall very nice place to dine for variety of Chinese cuisine, all decent taste and some special one too. Take note of special discount timing.

author: Kim Ling Lim
review_text: Nice place, nice environment but service is super sucks. Served tea no cup, make food order the waiter keep asking to hold, make drinks order but was not delivered. More training and better service if want to make big business to get good and excellent service rating by clients. All staff to be well trained to give your excellent service to clients so that you will be in the heart of others for good good comments. Can see locals don't care much bout the service and requirements by clients but one words your foreigners do even better jobs to served clients.

author: Kevin Yeoh
review_text:
Whoaaa... This place is so so nice. The moment you stepped in, I bet you will be impressed on the overall deco of the restaurant. It feels so nice and comfortable. The food is also great and I personally enjoyed almost all of the dishes that we ordered. There is one simple yet delicious dish which is the fried cabbage with meat. Then you can also order the spicy soup fish meat which I like as well. Service is very prompt as well.

They have a few other outlets too so for example if you stay at island side you can go to the Island outlet near Bayan Lepas area.

Price is not too expensive but a bit above average. Recommended to try !

author: Christeen
review_text: This is our 1st time visit to try their breakfast dim sum. They also serve noodles. Not much choices but overall it taste good. We ordered few items with a pot of tea. Foods tasted good except the popiah.. It's just a plain one.

author: Sin Yee Lee
review_text: The decoration is indeed good, but the quality of the service and food needs to be strengthened. For dimsum, the time to wait for the food to be served is also very long. I have to wait about 30 minutes to come. During eating, there are flies flying around, quite annoying. After eat, make me lost appetizer. Not recommend for dim sum.

author: Nanananana Dada
review_text:
Cozy and glamorous environment. Clean and tidy.
Currently there is a promotion whereby customer can get free wantan and dessert by review in Google.
We ordered salted egg pumpkin, pork, peanut butter noodle and lemon fish.
The ingredient is fresh and portion is generous. Honest review but not doing this for free food lol
Price is high side but justifiable.

author: Joann Ting
review_text: The first dish of peanut butter noodles dampened my anticipation for the food. The noodles were a mess and tasteless. The other food tasted also not good. Hope it can be improved.

author: Food Panda
review_text: I often tell my friends titipapan roti canai is good, but last night  I received two roti canai that were burnt on both sides. I was very disappointed and won't be going there again

author: Zi Xuan Ong
review_text:
RM11 for this small portion of maggi goreng ayam, which is actually at the high side consider the shop is located in BM area. The taste is so so compare to other shops, and it is pretty oily.

The service is bad when I wanna pay thay time. I am already at the cashier, then the staff at the cashier can start an argument with another staffs regarding some Grabfood order. I was there waited for few minutes just to wait them to finish the argument. In between the argument, another staff comes to the cashier and hand over the money which is paid by another customer. The cashier settle that particular payment first instead of mine who are waiting there for them to finish argument.

The most awesome part is, I start to have stomachache while I was driving back home. And had 2 round of diarrhea when I reached home. This is definitely the first and the last visit to this shop. Totally not recommended.

author: WY N
review_text:
Restaurant Titi Papan in Bukit Mertajam is hands down one of the best spots to enjoy a rich, flavorful curry meal. What makes this place stand out is their commitment to serving everything hot—whether it's the curry, rice, crispy fried chicken, or beef. The dishes are always served warm and fresh, and if by chance it’s not hot enough, you can just request them to reheat it on the spot.

In the mornings, their roti canai and chapati are top picks for breakfast—soft, fluffy, and perfect with their thick dhal or curry. Come afternoon, the star is their curry rice loaded with beef, chicken, fried oily egg, and a good mix of vegetables. It’s a hearty, satisfying plate that keeps you coming back. Their curry—whether beef, chicken, or mutton—is always full of flavor, slightly spicy, and incredibly addictive.

By evening and especially on weekends, it can be hard to find a seat because it’s often packed. That’s no surprise—the combination of affordable prices and consistently delicious food makes Titi Papan a local favorite. If you're a fan of good Malaysian-style curry meals, this place is a must-try. Just come early if you want to beat the crowd!

author: Andrew Yeoh
review_text: They have the usual selection of curries - chicken, beef and mutton. They have fried chicken and vegetables as well. The nasi kandar is actually quite delicious. Apart from the rice and curries, they also sell roti canai and mi goreng as well. The restaurant is reasonably clean. Parking may be a problem during peak hours.

author: Jeremy C
review_text:
A bit of a hidden gem in the area. Good food at reasonable price. Friendly service.

The mee goreng is really good. My personal go-to for Mee Goreng Mamak when I'm in the area. If that guy is frying as you walk by, you will smell the lovely mouthwatering aroma.

The nasi kandar has a few highlights but I wouldn't say it's groundbreaking.

author: Ong Chun Keat
review_text:
I have no idea during the time when we want to do the payment, the cashier asked me what I ordered, I was telling what I ordered and he didn't want to listen, kept sembang sembang and shouting, in the end he confirmed with colleagues what I ordered, apparently he wasn't believe in me, after he told me the price and I paid for it, few seconds later they stopped me asked I got order roti or not, mdfk I at the beginning I already told I got ordered roti, he dint want to listen, kept sembang and shouting with colleagues, eventually asked me to pay for additional price for the roti.

In conclusion, if you don't believe in customer don't ask what they ordered lah diu, write it down by your own, during payment just tell the price. Sucks management

author: Yi Wen Chan
review_text: Delicious nasi kandar with very fragrant curry 😍 dhal with roti canai also very nice, Maggie goreng seasoning perfectly nice with “wok hei” 😍😍😍

author: Mr. Boss
review_text: The food is ok only, but preferred to eat the Maggie Qatar, the other food soso only. Price is reasonable. Service abit poor, the food wait very long and if u ask them, their reaction was like "oh okok, sudah sudah."

author: kk teoh
review_text:
A very typical nasi kandar place with a decent selection of options.  There are not too many tables, so seating is limited.  There is no air-conditioner, so it can be a bit warm there. Having said that, most patrons generally opt to take away their food.  Parking is available along the street but is fairly limited.

I did not have a chance to take photos this time as we had to rush.  Having said that, since we enjoyed the food so much, I feel that it deserved a positive review.

The food in general is fresh and delicious.  Freshness and cleanliness are two factors which are important to us as we have had poor experiences at some nasi kandar outlets.  While we were not privileged to see how clean the kitchen was, the food counter/station was quite clean and the food was fresh.  I ordered a white rice with ayam masak merah, some shredded cabbage and deep fried bitter gourd.  As with many other patrons, I asked for a mix of kuah/gravy and in the typical banjir style.  The fried bitter gourd was crispy, even when taken half an hour later at home.  The ayam masak merah delicious and tender, though a bit too sweet.  The shredded cabbage was fresh, unlike those at some outlets that I have tried previously.

Happy to recommend and return to try other dishes.  Thumbs up.

author: Ah 2
review_text: Not a bad spot for gathering, but their serving speed for both food and drinks are just a bit too slow even for a patient person.

author: Kartiyayini Sinathurai
review_text: Good quality Food , especially roti and fried chicken . Only problem with the take away service , once you ordered you have to stand beside them and stare non stop then only they will start to make your food . If you went to sit waiting for the order to get prepared it will take forever and they will ignore , happens few times , probably because it’s just take away and they are prioritising dine in customers or my order was too small

author: Yw Teh
review_text:
Cleanliness need to improve.
Plate and cutlery is so oily till hard to hold. I see the worker grab the plate, cutlery with oily hand.

author: Chow Stephen
review_text:
Nasi Kandar Chicken cooked in red sweet sauce, taste normal, Teh Tarik is ok, nice.

Indian Mamak
Plenty of parking
Environment Indoor and outdoor seating.
Price for Nasi Kandar+Tarik RM 10.40

author: Cole Tor
review_text: The best! All the food is delicious, especially the curry sauce. Ordered fried maggie, nasi kandar with their fried chicken, roti kosong, all delicious!

author: rose jojie
review_text: The chef used to be good. Now it's changed a lot but the price is the cheapest. You can eat it. Big chicken. Ice Milos water if you ask...you can. Don't ask for it. Overall it's okay.

author: Azizan Omar
review_text: This restaurant has delicious food, good service, delicious rice... the fried noodles and pasembor are top notch, and the service is fast. When it's crowded, the counter chief himself goes down to serve customers.

author: Gobert
review_text: Mee goreng is nice, the staff used to be very friendly, but now just normal. Still one of our fav place to chill during supper time.

author: Snowing June
review_text: Can't comment for the rice and dishes because I did ordered before their roti popular, roti Hong Kong, roti john and mee goreng only. The taste of foods are not consistent and depend on which chef make it when you order. Staffs are very nice and friendly. Place a little bit small but lots of table serve at night without the roof. Normally easy to get the parking too.

author: Em Pzhi
review_text:
I order maggie goreng！
only vege and egg - 6 packs！
But didn't put vegetables for me！

author: Marcus CHUA
review_text: Good taste roti canai, staff friendly and service good. Overall cleanliness can be improve.

author: Carbon Lim
review_text: I have been to Chai Leng Park foodcourt so many times but mostly for the Lok Lok. This is the first time i ordered their noodle stalls. As a first image you would know this is a 老字号 already. So we ordered a Char Hor Fun, Tai Lok Mee or people mostly said KL Hokkein Mee, Fried Noodle and lastly a Loh Mee with black vinegar. The Wok Hei is enough and the taste was good also. Is just that this is just a roadside stalls so be prepared if you can't stand the heat in the afternoon. Definitely will return to try their other menu. Price is at affordable. You may need to park far away and walk to stall is more easier.

author: GH Chau (Desmund)
review_text: The taste is good, just sometimes you might need to wait due to a long queue. The best dai lok mee in Butterworth, worth a visit and a try. A normal hawker stall environment, nothing much to expect for the atmosphere.

author: Lay Ying Yeoh
review_text: Their Dai Lok Mee and Sang Mian very very delicious, cooked with wok hei. The sang mian very crispy and soaked with the soup. The sambal sauce a bit spicy but taste good. Please come early if you don't want to wait but they served really faster. The price is reasonable and the portion is okay. The atmosphere not so good but can try. I will come again.

author: Yeoh Ts
review_text: The sauce in the “Dai Luk Mee” hides the boss’s secret recipe, featuring crispy pork lard that adds amazing depth. Served steaming hot, it’s truly unforgettable. The fried crispy noodles are delicious, and the “Da Ban” comes in both dry and wet versions. Even though it’s crowded, the service is surprisingly fast, and the boss is very friendly.

author: CY “Pixandroid”
review_text:
Ok. I love the texture of the noodle and will miss it. Recommended to order big size

The dessert drink beside the stall also good in servicing

author: Kee Kelven
review_text:
One of the hottest spot on the street that always full of customers. Many customers waiting in line to take away, and their tables are always full of customers waiting for the food. The food usually served really fast but to be honest the hygiene of this place was not really satisfying lah.
We loved both Dai Lok Mee 大碌面 and Sang Mian 生面. The Dai Lok Mee was cooked with hot wok hei, thick soy sauce and pork lard, also came with pork meat and shrimp. The Sang Mian was noodles fried until crispy and then covered with thick soup with pork meat and shrimp, so we could taste both crispy noodles and soft noodles that soaked with the soup. You must have it with their pickled chilli and sambal chilli sauce.

author: Ee CW (Ecw)
review_text:
Nice and popular street food place at Perai.
Limited parking space, come as early possible to avoid long waiting time. My favorite is dai lok mee... 😘😘

author: Soon Lay Teong
review_text: If you want to have a terrible service which they will act like you owned them money, want to have bad mood but you just want to order, this is the correct place to visit. Dear staffs here,  if you guys having personal issue, then settle among yourselves, don't throw your negative feeling towards customers.

author: J-Ho S. C.
review_text:
The best Sang Mee in Prai.
Highly RECONMENDED!!

Just.. You need come early..
