Else, you need Q for quite some times to get your food. Up to half an hour.

Parking also an issue here.
So, kindly park at another block of shop and walk here. Else, you will stuck here, due to those brainless customers that simply park beside the road.

author: Low Siew Keong
review_text: Bad experience, bad services, and the environment is terrible. They don't even listen to you when you make order, terrible behavior. Food is not that good but the price is damn high. Strongly not recommend

author: Angela Wong
review_text:
The dalu noodles were average, lacking in flavor, and not as delicious as people say online.

The braised noodles were better than the dalu noodles...

The tangshui was good, with plenty of ingredients and was delicious.

Conclusion: The tangshui was better than the noodles.

author: βigcat 6öhömё
review_text:
This stall is quite famous, featuring several delicious stir-fries. It's a truly delicious place, and there's also a tea stall nearby, which is also quite popular, with crowds on weekdays and holidays.

6:00 PM to 9:00 PM is peak dinner time, so parking is a bit of a gamble, as you'll end up parking farther away. The same goes for tables; you might have to wait a bit.

The prices are pretty standard, a bit higher than they used to be, but still reasonable.

This is just one of the stalls in the entire food stall complex. The overall environment is quite simple and unpretentious, but the food is a perfect blend of local lifestyle, making it a highly recommended place to eat.
23/07/2023🐱

author: Andy
review_text:
This place is famous for its Dalu noodles, Moonlight River noodles, fried noodles, and fried rice noodles during the KL Food Festival.

Every time I go, I always order the fried noodles (RM8) or Dalu noodles (KL Hokkien noodles) (RM8). The owner uses a generous amount of ingredients and the wok is very powerful. The chef stir-fries everything in one large wok, so the food comes out quickly.

author: Ching
review_text:
It was packed, even at 6:00.
We ordered fried rice noodles, and it took almost 25 minutes for our turn. The rice noodles were traditionally cooked.
The taste was average.

author: T4ko
review_text: The food wasn't served in order. Two other tables that arrived 15 minutes later than us had their food served faster than us. They hadn't made reservations; it was obvious they had just arrived and then went to order.

author: Marcus CHUA
review_text: I tried the daluok mee and fried rice noodles, both were good. I had to wait for 15-20 minutes and I had to get it myself. There were a lot of people at the stall and some of them cut in line. I don't know how the boss remembered the order of so many people. To be fair, I suggest distributing numbers, which is easiest

author: Key Star
review_text: The service is so bad. I waited in line for so long and ignored them when I asked for orders. They kept saying that they had finished buying.

author: Eason Neoh
review_text:
Taste: 4.5 stars , quite tasty and delicious.
Ambience: it’s a 1-2stars environment, air is not well ventilated and warm, table top is acceptable but I won’t touch it, the floor is of course expected to be yer… 😅

author: Andrew Chan (www.roadtrippers.asia)
review_text:
One of the best place to have this sang mee and tailok mee (KL Hokkien Mee) in Penang.

The flavoring is good, organized and service is rather fast even though there is usually a lot of people.

The tailok mee is nicely cooked with good smokey frangrance and price wise is also quite affordable at RM6 per plate if not mistaken.

Parking can be an hassle though.

author: hste- lee
review_text: The Tai Lok Mee aka Hokkien Mee (KL style) is nowhere near the KL standard. Far from it to be precise! Lacked wok-hei and the tai lok mee used here is flat instead of the fat round ones, hence the moniker! Wat tan hor is and sang mee is just passable. Maybe the northerners preferred it this way. Surely not for me!

author: Kevin T
review_text:
Really enjoyed the kuey teow soup, the broth was flavorful and comforting. The chicken was juicy and tasty, and the soup sui gao added a nice touch. Also loved the drinks: the pumpkin milk was smooth and unique, while the cold ginger drink was refreshing. Overall, a satisfying and delicious meal
It's a place worth visit whenever I go to Chai Leng Park.

author: Lim CY
review_text: A good place for chicken rice, it offers a wide selection of side dishes to choose from, which adds variety to the meal. The food is decent and consistently prepared. The shop is clean, service is fast and efficient, and prices are reasonable, making it a convenient option for a satisfying meal.

author: Yeoh Ts
review_text:
The food is really good, and the place is clean and tidy. Dishes are served quickly, and you can choose portion sizes based on the number of people which helps avoid waste and ensures everything gets finished.

They don’t just have soup noodles, they also have dry hor fun. The soup noodles’s soup is prawn dumpling soup. The crispy fried prawn wontons that are packed with real ingredients. Paring them with the noodles and bean sprouts is prefect.

Parking is a bit limited.

author: Gerrard Teh
review_text: The place is quite spacious and cooling. Food serving is very fast. The soup hor fun is quite good with fresh clear shrimp broth, however the portion is a bit small to me even though i ordered a large size. The steam chicken is not impressive as the texture is not as smooth as you would like it to be. Ginger tea was ok not too spicy. 😅

author: Richard Lau
review_text: This Hor Fun is really unique in Penang! Totally different style of Kway Teow. The ingredient might looks simple, should be combination of soy sauce, scallion oil and chicken. However it really taste amazing! The texture of the Hor Fun is so smooth, slurp inside the mouth and immediately you can feel it will flow inside to your stomach. Must try the signature white chicken also. The meat is really soft and tender, and the sauce is not overpowering the taste of the chicken. Simple sauce also, and you can add their ginger paste as the topping of the chicken. Delicious!

author: Denne Goh
review_text:
Food was good. Love the dry Ipoh hor fun. Chicken rice and Nasi lemak not my favourite. Luncheon meat which was made in house was good too. But the wonton soup was the most awesome. Especially the soup itself. Very umami.
You can see from the last photo we finished all our food.

author: Helpful Tany
review_text: Came across this restaurant unexpectedly while searching for a breakfast spot, as many were crowded with full parking lots. Opted to try this one due to its decent and clean appearance. The food offered great value for money, with flavors surpassing expectations. The only downside was the absence of coffee. I'll definitely revisit if I find myself in the area again.

author: Aru Karuna
review_text:
Hor Fun @ koay teow thing is really good. Love the balance and the prawn based soup with won ton. Amazing flavours. I will surely be back wt friends.

One setback, the owner got to improve the roti bakar. Plz dont use standard gardenia like bread loaf. Was expecting a nice crispy hainan bread for roti bakar.
The 3 in 1 teh tarik is not my liking as well.

author: Andrew Yeoh
review_text:
Located in a rather busy part of Chai Leng Park, this restaurant is very popular with locals. Parking can be a problem.
This is a very clean restaurant.
The chicken rice is simply delicious. The chicken is smooth. Their noodles are also excellent. They also have the dry version. Customers can order bean sprouts, vegetables and wan ton, too.
I like their pumpkin milk drink. The price is quite reasonable.

author: Swee Koon Ng
review_text: The place is spacious and many fans to keep you cool. Ordered noodle soap, chicken shrimp dumpling and luncheon meat. The luncheon meat is made by the stall themselves with no preservatives,  very good.

author: Justine Hwang
review_text: Scrumptious meal for 3 😋 quality and taste that exceeds the price tag 👌🏻ordered the fried wanton, noodles soy sauce, chicken, tauge, pickled apple cucumber and pumpkin milk. 🍏🥒 The pickled dish is not like what I've tasted before. Sweet sour from the asam with a hint of spicy. def will come here again with my family 😉😉

author: Hammerhead
review_text:
One of the best ho fan you can find in mainland Penang. Delicious, tender chicken and clean environment.

Personally, this is as good as those famous ho fan you could find in Ipoh. Maybe the bean sprouts is not as fat and juicy but good enough for my level 😏.

author: YH
review_text:
A nice place to have soup noodle.
The shop also famous with their pumpkin milk drink too.

Overall, the place is comfortable and suitable to bring your baby here

author: Sora Yew
review_text: The steam chicken is really tender and soft but abit on the saltier side even without the dipping sauce also fine.The garlic also adds a different flavour to the chicken.The prawn wanton soup doesn’t taste as amazing as I expect but the soup is rich.The sa ho fen and the wanton soup is the same so feels like similar stuff but different ingredients.But the pumpkin milk is recommended.

author: Chuah Keat Lee
review_text: This chicken rice shop is unlike others. The steamed chicken is cooked all the way through, no bloody bits. What makes it special is the dipping condiments - the chilli and the green sauce. Oh man, the chicken that's dipped with both sauces are to die for. I have also tried the prawn wan ton soup... It's so good that I forgotten to take a photo. Also, the pumpkin milk beverage is also a must try. I really have nothing bad to say - 5 thumbs up, recommend! 👍🏻👍🏻👍🏻👍🏻👍🏻

author: Antony KW
review_text: All menu selections are reasonably priced. There are 2 sizes (small and large) for most food items, which would perfectly suit food tasters having a go at a few items during the visit. I had their signature items, Sau Ho Fun and Prawn Dumpling Soup with a pumpkin barley drink, all for MYR 14.10. Tables are placed with enough space from each other for social distancing and the restaurant is properly ventilated with ceiling fans, creating a cool setting for customers to enjoy their food selections. Definitely an eating haunt not to be missed if you are in Butterworth (Penang).

author: Nick Chung
review_text:
Fluffy rice , chicken not too oily , soy sauce taste spot on . Ipoh has the best hor fun, but here also quite good. Toasted bread Ipoh style , pretty decent

Clean environment, fast service , well organized business .

author: hai au
review_text: Dear owner, are you sure this is called “sauce”? It was just enough to make your plastic bag wet. Disappointed I like the sauce, went there many time but buy back very dammmmm

author: Sachiko Y
review_text:
The best shrimp noodle ever for me.  i always love tender chicken, bean sprouts, pickled vegetable😍 and pumpkin barley drink😍

On top of that, I had a flat tire with my car and the shop person kindly called to arrange for the repair shop🥹. It was REALLY REALLY helping me a lot and she is so kind.

I sincerely appreciate🙏

Thank you very much🙏

author: WD SonjaInc
review_text:
Used to be 5 stars, taste of the food and the chicken texture was great. Their homemade luncheon meat also good flavor.... But recently the portion has been getting smaller and smaller. The last time I ordered the 4ppl portion chicken for 3 ppl we still had to eat them sparingly cause there was so little meat nia
It's been nice knowing you guys, bye 👋🏻👋🏻

author: Jagen Manogran
review_text: Delicious food with generous portions! Service was good and the place has a nice cozy vibe. Highly recommend Rich Asian Western Food for both Asian and Western food lovers.

author: PHANG WAI HUN
review_text: Delicious chicken chop with cheese! The meat was well-cooked and the cheesy topping made it extra satisfying. Great portion and value for money.

author: evon lim
review_text: Good environment, staff are friendly and helpful.Food portions are big. Great choice for Western classics without spending much.

author: Nien Hwei
review_text: Had a lovely dining experience on a Sunday night. I ordered the Thai-style kerabu chicken chop and it did not disappoint — generous portion, packed with flavor, and definitely value for money. The staff were friendly and welcoming. Will definitely be back to try other dishes

author: Dorene
review_text: Great value for money! The portion sizes are generous and really satisfying. There’s a nice variety of dishes to choose from. The Hainanese chicken chop was decent—huge serving, perfect for one very hungry person! The mushroom soup is a highlight—rich, flavorful, and clearly homemade, not the canned kind. I also enjoyed the tiramisu—not too sweet, just right. Definitely worth a visit! Just a note, it can be very crowded during the weekends so the service will be slower. So, come earlier or call ahead to book a table.

author: Tze Shan Tan
review_text: Good taste of food and atmosphere is good 👍🏻 One of the favourite western food cafe in Butterworth. Highly recommend ! ☺️✨

author: Ams Kalya
review_text: Food was big in portions and delicious. 👍The taste was just right, not too salty or heavy. I was very impressed with the otak-otak seafood spaghetti, which tasted unique and delicious. Drinks taste average. Betta fish coffee is a bit sweet.The service attitude is good and the food comes quickly. They also ask the customer feedback when payment. The restaurant is not big in space, I went for lunch on weekends, not many people. Last weekend I wish to went dinner there, but it was full, and I been informed to wait for more than 30min. Suggest if weekend dinner to call for inquire/reserve.

author: Heng Khai Shen
review_text: I had such a great experience at this stall! The food was fresh, delicious, and full of flavor. The portion sizes were generous, and the prices were very reasonable. The owner was friendly and welcoming, which made the visit even better. Highly recommended if you’re looking for quality and good service!

author: Yew Chong Poh
review_text: Food big portion and good taste, love it. The staff provide  good service and environment also good and nice for family, friends gathering functions. strong recommend it, price reasonable and worth to eat. Nice

author: Jesse Chin
review_text: Ordered chicken chop, the food portion looks great and big, but honestly it is just because of the fried skin and it looks big. The environment needs to be improved as we are sitting just in front of the toilet as in the picture and it smells like Dettol. Why 3 stars, if you ask for extra sauce, the lady at the counter will tell you sauce needs to pay extra! What?! I need more sauce just because your food is served with not enough sauce. Will I come again?🤔Maybe yes, when I have no other choices

author: David Ooi
review_text:
The food portion is generous. Taste wise is also good. Additional request for tar tar sauce is served in a mini sos bowl and chargeable, dont do the mistake like us and ordered two 🤣. Order one cukuo, can share share yah
Tried the vodka and malibu dessert. Nice

author: Lay Ying Yeoh
review_text: Ordered their kerabu chicken chop and otak otak spaghetti,  both taste good and delicious. Like otak otak spaghetti very much, it tastes unique and yummy. The food was in big portion and price is reasonable. We order root beer float as our beverage, it taste okay. Service was fast and friendly. Easy to find parking around this area. Highly Recommended to try a new style western food.

author: lim zhian
review_text: Ordered kerabu chicken chop and otak otak spaghetti, both taste delicious. It tastes unique and yummy. The food was in big portion and price is reasonable. We order root beer float as our beverage, it tastes good as well. Service was great. Easy to find parking around this area. Highly Recommended to try a new style western food.

author: Cheng Mun Mun
review_text:
Food is pretty great. Finally, some good western food in Butterworth!

I tried the otak otak seafood spaghetti. The otak otak is in the sauce. The flavour is really powerful, with a dash of spiciness to it. Makes the whole spaghetti really nice to eat.

The chicken is also nicely fried. Portion is huge.

Ordered an alcoholic beverage with rum in it. Really nice cocktail combo.

Overall I love the food. Will be back for more.

author: Tn T
review_text: Had a great meal at this Rich Asian Western food shop! The chicken chop was juicy and well-seasoned, and the fries were crispy. Cozy atmosphere and friendly service. Will definitely come back again!

author: YVONNE SKYE
review_text: The food taste so so. Portion of spaghetti abit small. Very limited parking as many parking infront of the shop is reserved for their own customer.

author: YC Teh
review_text:
A relatively new restaurant in 2023 serving western food with creative twist.

Food is okay, sevice is decent, price is reasonable (around Rm20 for a main).

A summary -
Hawthorn Cheesy Chicken - 4/5
Kerabu Fish and Chips - 2.5/5
Mushroom Soup - 3/5

On to the deets:
Their Hawthorn Cheesy Chicken is savoury and juicy. The chicken cutlet is thick as well. Overall not bad.

The plating, fries, sides and taste reminds me of Empat Sekawan’s chicken chops for those of you who have tried it.

The Kerabu Fish and Chips pales in comparison.
The fish fillet feels like one of those dory from the supermarket frozen foods section.
It lacks the flakiness and creaminess of a good fillet.

Nothing special about the mushroom soup. There are mushroom chunks but could be better with fewer fillers and more mushroom-y.

Would I return again?
Maybe, but only for their chicken.

author: Ying Ying Eeow
review_text: Great place for Western food! The portions are generous, the flavors are spot on, and the staff are super friendly. Definitely coming back again!

author: Yoon Yit Sam
review_text:
Service and environment are okay, clean, friendly staffs.

Food is kopitiam level western food. Pasta noodles were fresh, however, the sauce is too sweet for my taste. We ordered 2 pastas and both tasted too sweet. They use the same mushroom for the two pastas, lacking variations (eg french beans, nuts, fresh basils etc.). The frozen seafood used is a RED FLAG to me. The frozen clams tasted very bad. Its a shame to see them using frozen materials everywhere eventhough the wet market was just within walking distance. Another RED FLAG is the cheap sausage that they used to sell for 50cents in school canteen. Maybe they display that on the menu as a deterent from people who has high expectation.

Overall not worth the time and stomach if you are looking for some legit western food.

author: Wei Leng
review_text: Place is clean, pleasant and tidy. Food is tasty and price is reasonable. Will come again next time. Thank you for the good food.

author: Richard Ho
review_text: Khao Khun Mookata is a super value for money mookata outlet. Setup is simple, food ingredients are fresh with a free flow of beverages and even ice cream for dessert. This outlet at Raja Uda Butterworth is worth visiting as the dining space is airy and open. Perfect environment to eat mookata, with an option of spicy tomyum or clear broth soups. As usual, there was a section of pre-cooked finger foods, with very tasty chilli crab and yummy fried wonton and nicely grilled satay. Staff were kind and attentive, and even helped us shift to a shady and cooler spot as our table was in a warm location. Excellent mookata place for everyone to try in the Butterworth area.

author: Jacques Rerolle
review_text:
Rm36.50 Free Flow best Mookata 🤩

So tasty. Pork available, ice cream and soft drinks too. All free flow.

Video review is on my youtube channel. Please subscribe : Jac reviews stuff

author: C J
review_text:
Food choices are a lot from ready to eat fried foods, satay to steambot stuffs like frozen foods, seafood and vegetables.

Lot of seats available but may need reservation if you come eat around peak hours at 8pm onwards.

Parking is difficult to find and you may need to park far a bit.

Tomyam soup is rather too sweet and no spicy for me personally.

author: Jhung Lim
review_text: When I think about mookata, I always think of Khao Khun Mookata! They have so many dishes to choose from, including ready-to-eat items which is a big plus. The variety is amazing, fresh meats, seafood and side dishes, all at a good price. Staff are ready to refill the soup either u choose for Tomyam or the normal one. Drinks and ice cream are all free!

author: Sarah Lee
review_text:
Most affordable and valuable mookata buffet in Northern area- Khao Kun offers unlimited buffet with a wide range of choices for food at the price of RM29.90.

They have cooked food stations, ice stations, popcorn, drinks, ice-cream and plenty of ingredients for you to cook with. With the time limit of 120 minutes, it’s more than enough to enjoy the buffet.

For cooked food, their signature fried chicken is a must try. During our visit, they were running a promo of free lala pot which was packed with flavours and fresh.

For the mookata, you can opt for tomyam soup or clear soup. The ingredients here were fresh and of all the meat, the lemongrass and tomyam chicken & pork tasted the best.

author: Pin Yeoh (Foodie life)
review_text: RM $29.9 per person charcoal hot pot and bbq grilled with pork butter  all you can eat! There are lots of choices and the food quality is great! We really enjoyed crab and clam. The hot pot soup tasted delicious! I love their ice lemongrass drink. There is 2 hours time limit. It’s recommended to reserve a table beforehand because the place is popular. Be prepared to SWEAT! It is hot and humid when you first sit down, but it gets better once you get used to the temperature.

author: Jonathan Foo
review_text:
Upside :
Reasonable pricing for Rm29.90 (not including tax) Buffett style has reasonable choices of food spoiled for choices. Fresh prawn, clams and even crab was observe. Unlimited flow of coke, Thai Milk tea and even lemongrass for you to pick.

Downside :
Limited parking space , the environment is too humid especially if you come on midday! All so so hot like oven despite the fan used!
Not your romantic place ya guys.

author: Dwayne Yong
review_text:
Mookata, a Thai-style steamboat and grill, offers a wide variety of ingredients, both cooked and raw. The selection is great, from fresh vegetables to marinated meats.

The pork belly is tasty but has too much fat. A better balance would be 2/3 meat and 1/3 fat, which would make it perfect.

Overall, Mookata is a good choice for those who enjoy grilling and boiling their own food, but the pork belly could use a slight improvement. Definitely a good place for family and friends' gathering

author: Axel Koh
review_text:
All the staffs are friendly. There are many variety of foods but all of them are just mediocre or normal.

Beverages are too sweet, once you drink you will get even more thirsty and drink more.

Surrounding is fine but if there's better ventilation it'll add points. During rainy time I still sweat a lot during my visit. Overall the restaurant is fine, with reasonable pricing.

author: Yiling Lai
review_text:
Sun 22 Dec 2024

The mootaka lala hotpot is well worth the price of MYR 29.90. They offer a wide variety of food, the cutlery is spotless, and the air-conditioned environment is quite pleasant. I’ll definitely visit again.

The total bill for four people came to MYR 132.70.

author: Benny Poh
review_text: The environment isn't great; it can get very hot. I believe this is due to the low buffet price of RM29.90, which attracts a large number of customers. The service is acceptable, and the food tastes average, although I often feel very thirsty after dinner. It's worth a try.

author: Janice Chang
review_text: better make reservation during weekends, they open at 530pm. many varieties of raw and ready eat food, i especially like the moopin and the mushroom soup.  Free flow of ice cream and drinks, my all time favourite is the lemongrass drink..

author: lio mas
review_text: Worth it with its price,they offered a vast variety of foods,the cutlery is very clean and the place is considerably pleasant,will definately come again

author: Stanic Teoh
review_text:
A little bit hot, however it is BBQ mookata, so already set expectations for hot environment.
With the price RM29. 90 it is worth, prawn, sotong, crabs, and many choices
Free flow drinks, should give a try.

author: john chan
review_text:
Worth the price, food also not bad expecially the prawn and crab, very fresh
Drink also quite tasty. For me, I will go second times.

If the owner can improve a bit on the ventilation will be better. The environment quite hot there.

author: kelvin sim
review_text: First time going there, price quite cheap but problem the meat and seafood quite terrible. Meat not fresh and look like few week meat where not fresh produce then seafood like not fresh at all where prawn look dark and head come out and lembik. Meat mostly  some terrible smell.

author: Someone who adore Nature
review_text:
Tomyam soup is just nice
Many options of frozen food
Chicken and other fresh stuff like seafoods not really fresh
They had the roti bakar , nugget , Maggie Goreng was quite nice too.
You can spend 2 hours which cost you rm29.90 each.
Worth to try .
Quite crowded

author: May C
review_text: For the price of rm29.90 perpax ,there is nothing to feel dissatisfied. U got crab n prawn, other sode dishes, all the frozen foods and drinks.u canot find thos price elsewhere..tomyam soup base a bit salty whole clear soup almost tasteless...try to put a scoop or 2 of chocolate ice cream into thai milk tea..terrific

author: Tan Soo Xian
review_text: Reasonable price for a all-you-can-eat buffet style hotpot and grill; provided meat and some seafood. A bit hard to get parking and the location is hidden behind the shop lot and housing area.

author: Kaixuan Soh
review_text: the food is not fresh especially the meat and the seafood which have a stinky smell. the pork is generally fatty with very little of meat, and doesnt taste good. it doesnt worth a try at all.

author: Lee Rong Chen
review_text:
Best Thai Food in Malaysia.

Available in not too spicy version

As for the drink such as the Yen (Original Milk Tea) and Kiew (Green Milk Tea), literally is the most delicious and healthy version! Super refreshing and authentic💞🌅🌌🤓👍👍

author: BOON LEONG TAN
review_text: Our family members came to this famous restaurant at Jitra after we went for prepared our Thailand car insurance at Changlun. This restaurant famous among locals and outsider. The restaurant prepared the Thai style dishes. Most of the dishes are hot and spicy. The pricing are at upside as this only a small town at Kedah.

author: CM Teo
review_text:
First visit after so many years, Nicely Renovated, Clean bright and Neat set up.

Food portion was good and tasty. Friendly staff and good service.

Happy with the "New Feel"

Will definitely come back for the Food again!

Recommended....

author: Hakimi Hamizi
review_text:
The food and environment is great and cozy. Suitable for family and friends gatherings. I would recommend, Ikan Goreng Khengsom (fried sea bass dipped into sour-spicy soup) when you eat here.

Worth the price. As for me, the food taste is bold and delicious. Would consider this restaurant for the next visit.

author: KH Seh
review_text: The glass noodle with prawn is tasty. Recommended to try. Tomyam broth taste authentic. Lime steamed fish if slight more sour will be the best. Overall is great.

author: Jureena Sisuwan
review_text: The interior is beautiful. Food quality has declined. Had a tough time eating the squids, both from fried squid and tomyam was very tough. Tomyam is too sweet & strong artificial flavour. Lemonade was too sweet too.

author: Qiao Yi Ng
review_text: Food portion very small with price given. Food not as good and affordable as before renovation. Green curry is too sweet.

author: chee chin hoe
review_text: Food was tasty. Had the fish head HorFun, ikan keli goreng, kerabu chicken feet & fried bitter gourd. All good. Service could be better though

author: NORSHAM SUHAINA BINTI YAAKOB (FRIM)
review_text: Great meal at Restoran 5 Utara!Loved the Siakap Goreng Khengsom (crispy, flavorful) and Udang Padphet (spicy, aromatic)—will reorder! Kangkung Garlic and Ayam  Goreng Garlic were solid. Decent price for 3 pax. Only downside: tea too sweet. Highly recommended!

author: Sashwin Govintesamy
review_text: Very disappointing experience. The tomyam was a letdown — only 2 prawns served for 6 people, which is unacceptable. The Kam Heong chicken was extremely dry and lacked flavor. On top of that, portion sizes were very small and definitely not worth the price. Would not recommend if you're looking for value or quality.

author: Alt Ernate
review_text:
Great food terrible service! Waited 30 min seated at a dirty table, staff cleaned tables of guests that arrived later than us. Waited another 30 min before the first dish came: eggs, with no rice, plates, or cutlery. Went to get it ourselves after a few mins.

Wrong orders served, duplicate dishes given, went up to ask about missing dishes and they asked us to cancel. Waiter was also incapable of calculating bill, so we did it for them. Overall impressive how terrible everything was, really couldn't be worse!

author: SK
review_text: Came here for late lunch after out from Hatyai. Food was served kinda slow probably not much chefs are on duty during off peak hour.

author: Jaykay Teoh
review_text: Used to be the landmark of Jitra, my favorite restaurant for the past 30 years until recent when the kid(2nd gen) took over, revamped the place to high class restaurant look but the food level has dropped! Kensom, aka sour tomyam - has no more the basic essence, the chicken feet kerabu - somehow the taste and feel are totally gone, pra kra pao - for my son's favourite, left 50% untouched. Very sad to say, this is the last time I ever step to this stall!

author: Wailing Mok
review_text: We went to order tonight's dinner at 11.30 in the morning and when we arrived, they actually forgot our order, how come this will be happened?  And they told us that a table can seat 15 people but they couldn't. The food was not delicious at all, serviced was very poor. Will not come again.

author: CS Weng
review_text: One of the best authentic Thai food at jitra with authentic thai herbs and spices. Located on the main street of jitra main road. Environment and vibes are good.

author: Mark ปาริน
review_text: Pleasant fine dining with air conditioning restaurant, thai foods, drinks and of course mango and glutinous rice with coconut milk...

author: Dominic Ho
review_text: Authentic Thai food - kengsom fish (excellent), deep fried catfish (a bit dry) & kerabu chicken feed (excellent). The sambal belacan is fantastic (available for sale). Service is quite fast. The ambience can be improved upon.

author: Phaik Sia Lee
review_text: They are not service food by sequence even you are coming earlier and order first. The food still serve for the table came after you.

author: Pohkim Cheng
review_text: The food is great 👍 really tasty especially the fish in Tom yam soup I don't remember what it called but it was really good that I Plan to go back someday 😋

author: RED EVE
review_text:
Tried this restaurant due to their good ratings. Would have given higher ratings if the fried chicken and lele were not overcooked.
Expected the rice to be fragrant Thai rice but turned out not.
Overall the food portion was adequate and price was  reasonable.

author: Yelloboi Jaysen TJ
review_text:
I was recommended by my Indian friend. So I purposely came over to try.
But it's not up to our expectation. The curry is not flavorful enough.
The price is quite reasonable, staff is friendly.
There are more nasi kandar with better taste. Sorry, no second visit.

author: Syah Zakaria
review_text: came for dinner, the food was acceptable, for penang lang, myb the curry was not so kick enough, but for us outsiders is acceptable, hv aircond area, price wise really reasonable compared to other nasi kandar place. recommend dish “ayam bawang”

author: BUSAIKUNA ISHIMOTO
review_text: Food here slaps and is not overpriced. It has a WIDE variety of selections compared to other small mamaks I’ve been to and the chefs here know how to cook well. Warning though, it is better to dine in than ordering on grab, as the portions are very small. This place is quite good and is very busy even during midnight.

author: Elton Hiew
review_text:
One of the best or if not the best Nasi Kandar you can find in Penang. A lot of variety selection and most importantly is that the price is reasonable. They are not stingy with the sauce (kuah) for their Nasi Kandar.

Maggie is also best here. Not sure what spices they used but you can’t find anywhere better for Maggie goreng.

author: Cher Ong
review_text: It's definitely not the best, but it's quite food. My regular supper spot as i love maggi goreng & theirs is 1 of the most consistent tasting one. It's hard to get a delicious maggi goreng at nasi kandar place because they seem to have multiple chef frying. I love their fried chicken as well, well seasoned & crispy skin. Of course, there are other better ones, but their's is good enough if u don't compare. They have an air cond zone, so if you're afraid of stuffy air flow, then u can opt to sit in. Their nasi kandar is good as well. The kuah campur 😋. Ingredients are not too fancy, basics only.

author: ng Sp
review_text:
having supper here
taking roti canai and murtabak with some drink
overall the roti and murtabak taste good with acceptable pricing
seating come with and without aircon area

author: alex cheong
review_text: 4 big stars for nasi kandar rafei ali because i would say one of the best nasi kandar in tanjung tokong. Roti canai and maggie goreng also damn good. Only downside is the air ventilation and fumes in the restaurant.

author: CEOEatTravelRepeat
review_text: One of the best Nasi Kandar in Penang. Ayam Bawang is delicious. The joki will candi all the kuah and mixed well. The nasi kandar taste became super delicious when you take away and eat after a few hours. Very recommended

author: John D'Cruz (Kajangfood)
review_text: This is my go-to place for Nasi Kandar in Tanjung Bungah/Tokong area. It’s not famous but has good curries, buzzing vibe with mainly locals and reasonable prices. All the nasi kandar favourites are here - ayam goreng, daging masak hitam , ayam Ros, telur sotong etc. Eat to your hearts content and look for a place for a siesta afterwards. 😅

author: akarosco
review_text:
Very popular nasi kandar (mamak) restaurant especially with locals suggests good quality & value. This has been exactly our experience.
Speedy & friendly service was a bonus.
Our recent breakfast included roti telur bawang (egg & onion roti) and Malaysia's national dish nasi lemak.
Both were delicious and on our table in no time, closely following our teh tarik.
My now favourite place for breakfast. Looking forward to visiting again for lunch & dinner sometime.

author: phang c fong
review_text: Quite a lot's of people's here.. Friendly staff's..They have indoor air con and outdoor seating. Sometimes enjoying the football Channel .

author: deRykcihC
review_text: The mixed curry and fried chicken is probably the star of this nasi kandar restaurant. Especially the chicken, spices are just enough to make it crispy and juicy.

author: Kin Han Loo
review_text: Ayam bawang was good, and slightly sweetish which went well towards balancing the umami from the other curry gravies. However, I felt that the overall kuah campur wasn’t pekat enough for my liking, so 4 stars for now.

author: YMRHRI (Tok Engku Mie)
review_text: The food was good especially the nasi kandar, kuah kari jockey and tandoori but the service.... simply horrible! The workers tend to talk to each other in Tamil and do not seem to bother customers who called to order. Most of the time they took the wrong order and actually cursed customers in their native tongue when they were  pointed out the mistakes. Also noticed that most of them actually do not understand bahasa melayu or english. It is dumbfolding how they can get into this country so easily and fast! Overall, places like Line Clear, Hamediah, Ketapang, Medina are much much better in terms of price and food taste. Please consider other options when in Penang.

author: Siti Nurzahidah Ishak
review_text: Worst nasi kandar ever I have been. Bad service, rude waiter, we ask for order 3 times. We even go to them and ask properly, but they just ignore and said wait at the table. Been observe them how long they will take time to get our order and come to serve us, Unfortunately they just go serve the existing customer who ady have food in their table. Worst worst worst, bad service

author: Gau
review_text: Rafei Ali is one of my favourite nasi kandar spots. Their speciality is their ayam goreng! I’ve been eating here for years and always loved it. Today (9/4/24) I came with a foreigner and I was charged RM3.60 for 2 air kosong. I’m aware of the latest 8% SST but am I missing out something? 1 ais kosong is RM1.80? I did not confront them and not planning to make go to KPDN but just be aware that there are workers there who just put the price randomly based on THE LOOKS. The best part is the workers there are foreigners themselves. I’m sure he did not wrongly written it down because I asked him “dua ini 3.60? and he nodded yes”

author: DARSH (DJSUMO)
review_text:
Nasi Kandar Rafei Ali holds a cherished place in my memories, transporting me back to my childhood where the rich aromas and vibrant flavors of their dishes created an unforgettable experience. The journey through the years has been remarkable, as I have observed the establishment not only preserve its authenticity but also enhance its offerings to meet the evolving preferences of its patrons.

The introduction of two distinct seating options reflects this commitment to customer comfort and satisfaction. One can now choose to dine in an air-conditioned environment, which provides a respite from the tropical heat, or enjoy a more traditional experience in an open area with normal fans. This thoughtful expansion caters to diverse preferences, as some patrons may appreciate the cool respite of the AC, while others might prefer the outdoor ambience that allows for a more casual and social dining atmosphere.

Moreover, it is noteworthy how Nasi Kandar Rafei Ali has managed to maintain the essence of its culinary offerings amidst expansion. The flavors that once captivated my youthful palate remain vibrant and true to their origins, while the improved facilities enhance the overall dining experience. Such dedication to quality and customer experience is commendable and speaks volumes about the establishment's commitment to excellence.

As I reflect upon my visits over the years, I cannot help but appreciate the journey that Nasi Kandar Rafei Ali has undertaken. Its ability to adapt and grow while still evoking the warm nostalgia of youth is a testament to its enduring legacy. I look forward to many more visits, where I can enjoy not only the delicious food but also the increased comfort and ambiance that this beloved establishment now offers.

author: Melvin Phil
review_text: Whenever i buy food over here, they always don’t follow my order. I always ask for chicken curry but the workers are lazy to walk and giving me fish curry EVERY SINGLE TIME.  Always disappointing me 👎🏻

restaurant: LAO XIANG CLAYPOT BAK KUT TEH
author: Lim CY
review_text: The soup version is decent, though we were expecting a slightly richer broth. The dry version is enjoyable, with a pleasant squid aroma and flavour. Everything is well balanced, the you char koay is nicely done, crispy on the outside yet still soft and doughy inside, and the vegetables are cooked just right. Overall, it was a satisfying meal, though the price is slightly higher compared to some other bak kut teh shops that offer slightly larger portions.

restaurant: LAO XIANG CLAYPOT BAK KUT TEH
author: Ohaiyo Simidaa
review_text:
Stumbled upon this bak kut teh place unexpectedly.
Delicious food –
• Soup is rich with herbal flavor.
• Meat is tender and not dry.
• Dry version is fragrant, with squid adding extra aroma.

Popular spot –
• Arrived around 5pm and it was already nearly full.

Good service –
• Staff were friendly.
• Requested soup refill and it was served quickly.

Minor downsides –
• Vegetables were slightly overcooked.
• 油炸鬼were too oily.

Reasonable pricing – fair for the quality and portion.

Overall – Highly recommended and would return!

restaurant: LAO XIANG CLAYPOT BAK KUT TEH
author: buck low
review_text: Usually we only eat BKT in Port Klang and seldom in other places. But bcos it was raining, we wanted to find something with soup. And so glad we had this. Can easily rival with any top BKT shops in Port Klang and anywhere else. Their dried one is a must try.

restaurant: LAO XIANG CLAYPOT BAK KUT TEH
author: Joshua Yap
review_text: Came around 5:40pm. Tried the dry bkt with some 油条. The soup is very herbalicious. The dry BKT was flavourful. Worth a try. One person dry BKT was around RM16.50, Garlic rice RM1.50, 油条(RM1.5) and a cup of Chinese tea (RM0.70)

restaurant: LAO XIANG CLAYPOT BAK KUT TEH
author: WY N
review_text:
This bak kut teh establishment consistently operates at full capacity, requiring patrons to endure long queues. The allure lies in the delectably hot and tasty food, accompanied by an enticing aroma that lingers. The experience is incomplete without pairing it with rice, creating a taste that leaves a lasting impression in your memory.

Situated in a location boasting ample parking space, which is free at night, adds to its appeal. This convenience makes it an ideal spot to bring together friends and family. The welcoming atmosphere, coupled with the savory dishes, transforms this bak kut teh place into more than just a dining spot; it becomes a preferred destination for shared moments and enjoyable meals.

restaurant: LAO XIANG CLAYPOT BAK KUT TEH
author: Ty lee
review_text: The restaurant serves two types of Bak Kut Teh. I preferred  the fragrant herbal tea soup type .The other is the dry spicy version. Ordered the iceberg lettuce as another side dish. The restaurant is quite popular and usually packed with customers for dinner. Service is fast. Price has gone up slightly and the portion has reduced too.

restaurant: LAO XIANG CLAYPOT BAK KUT TEH
author: YAT Lifestyle
review_text: My parent first choice. Food is delicious enough, with bak kut teh soup and dry type. The service is outstanding, crew will auto top up soup for you without calling. The crew is equipped with Chinese multi dialects and communicate well.

restaurant: LAO XIANG CLAYPOT BAK KUT TEH
author: Joel H
review_text: Quite easy to navigate, very easy to spot its location via Google Map’s navigation upon reaching the traffic light. They offer both soup and dry variation. We ordered the soup Bak Kut Teh, along with some side dishes. Appreciate that we are able to top the soup without extra charges. Condiments are offered generously as well. One of the service crew actively offered to top our soup when it’s running low. Overall a great dining experience!

restaurant: LAO XIANG CLAYPOT BAK KUT TEH
author: wai yin Sit
review_text: Bak Kut Teh here promises a comforting and aromatic experience. So gather your ingredients, let the flavors meld, and enjoy this hearty dish! 🍲🌿

restaurant: LAO XIANG CLAYPOT BAK KUT TEH
author: Clarissa Mulan
review_text: I have been eating bak kut teh from this shop since young until now. We are from kulim btw. Still the best in town. From 1 shop expanded to 2 shops. U should try the soup and dry one it's so good plus with the uichakoi.

restaurant: LAO XIANG CLAYPOT BAK KUT TEH
author: Onion Yeoh
review_text: Always my favorite! I always bring my friends to this famous and delicious bak kut teh, every of my friends are amaze by the taste of bak kut teh here hope they sell their food forever!

restaurant: LAO XIANG CLAYPOT BAK KUT TEH
author: Suzanne Lim
review_text: By far the best BKT in Penang. Very similar taste to Klang BKT. Very organize even with big crowd. Service is fast, good, responsive and friendly.

restaurant: LAO XIANG CLAYPOT BAK KUT TEH
author: See Chun Keat
review_text: First time eating BKT here. The taste is good, but the disappointed thing is all the pork given are fat. Who willing to pay money just for eating fat?

restaurant: LAO XIANG CLAYPOT BAK KUT TEH
author: Erwin Wagner
review_text: Excellent claypot BKT. We had the dry one with soup served separately.  Was very fragrant and not too salty. The fact that they use ikan bilis and shrimp paste enhances the flavor of the BKT. Meet was very tender and veggies excellent too. I actually enjoyed it way more than the usual BKT place I go to in Klang.

restaurant: LAO XIANG CLAYPOT BAK KUT TEH
author: Chee Kheong Lau
review_text:
The BKT is very tasty. Have tried the soup and dried type.
The meat is soft and tender.
Service is good. Soup is auto add on as the waiters are very alert and attentive.

restaurant: LAO XIANG CLAYPOT BAK KUT TEH

review_text: Very good bak kut teh and friendly boss that offers a free refill of the herbal soup. Everything tastes fresh. Seating was not ideal right next to the shoplot on the roadside but par for course for BM establishments, I think.
